The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks. 105 D D Dragon, Coruscine A slender, serpentine dragon with branching antlers and dragonfly wings holds court from the branches of a tall tree. Its scintillating scales shimmer in the dappled light like hundreds of tiny diamonds.

legendary.name: Fey Realm Dragons
entries: Coruscine dragons reside primarily in the wooded regions of the faerie realms and are often found in the company of fey. Their non-traditional features, such as their wings and antlers, stem from their ties to the faerie world.

legendary.name: Color-Changing Chameleons
entries: A coruscine dragon’s scales have a natural shimmering, iridescent quality, depending on the angle and intensity of the light, but they can also actively shift the coloration and patterning, allowing them to blend in more easily in their chosen environments. As they age, the natural pastels of their scales gradually darken, though they never lose their iridescence.

legendary.name: Capricious and Calculating
entries: Like their fey comrades, coruscine dragons can be highly mercurial, mischievous, and impulsive. With age, they are better able to temper their impulses with patience and cunning, embracing a knack for long-term scheming and courtly politics on par with the greatest of fey sovereigns. At any age, they cherish secrets of all sorts and the sordid, intertwining affairs of other creatures—reveling especially in scandals and rumors. Many coruscine dragons collect trinkets as mementos of such affairs. They can recall in exquisite detail the story behind each such treasure, whether the ring of a heartbroken, spurned lover or the crown of a king betrayed by their closest advisors.

legendary.name: Maturing
entries: Coruscine wyrmlings are often exceedingly temperamental, swinging from childlike glee to violent outbursts and back again over the slightest provocation. They spend much of their time exploring with sprites and other fey, and when they find the right location, they claim it as their own, crafting a connection with the surrounding D D 106 land over the span of years. As coruscine dragons mature and establish their lair, the regional fey will often offer tribute or propose an alliance—knowing the dragon’s uncanny ear for gossip. A mature coruscine dragon often enjoys the favor of various fey lords and ladies and can sometimes be seen at court, observing the affairs of others with great interest. A CORUSCINE DRAGON’S LAIR A coruscine dragon most commonly settles in the faerie realms, where they roost in the canopies of dense forests. Once established in a region, they gain some element of control over the nearby greenery and can shape it, crafting chambers and tunnels out of the thick foliage. These lairs can be as elaborate as any grand mansion, consisting of various areas designated for specific purposes and even hiding secret rooms and passageways. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Disorienting Blooms. Up to five blossoms sprout on five different points the dragon can see within 120 feet of it, releasing pollen. Each creature within 5 feet of a blossom must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be poisoned until initiative count 20 on the next round. While poisoned, a creature is blinded, its speed is halved, and when it moves, it moves in a random direction. • Faerie Fire. Shimmering motes fill a 30-foot cube centered on a point the dragon can see within 90 feet of it. Each object in the area is coated with a shining dust, and each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 15

legendary.name: DEX save or also become coated in the dust
entries: Any attack roll against a creature or object coated in the dust has advantage if the attacker can see it, and such creatures and objects can’t benefit from being invisible. The dust lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round. • Scintillating Light. Rays of sunlight or moonlight in the lair bend and warp toward the dragon, reflecting off its scales in a rainbow of colors. Each creature within 30 feet of the dragon and that can see it must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or be blinded until initiative count 20 on the next round. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region containing the coruscine dragon’s lair is warped by its presence, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Eye for Drama. The coruscine dragon is aware of the presence of all creatures within 1 mile of its lair, feels whenever a creature in the area experiences heightened emotions, and knows what the emotion is. While in its lair, the dragon can use an action to cast the scrying spell (spell save DC 15) on any creature within 1 mile of the lair. • Sweet Water. All sources of water within 5 miles of the lair are clear and sweet. Once per day, when a creature other than the dragon drinks the water, it must roll a d100. On a result of 1–50, the creature has advantage on CHA checks for the next 24 hours; on a result of 51–100, it has disadvantage on CHA checks for the next 24 hours. • Vivid Dreams. A creature that sleeps or meditates within 10 miles of the lair experiences dreams of personal conflicts or other social interactions rife with tension that have already occurred or could possibly occur in the future. If the dragon dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

legendary.name: Instead of scales, the dragon’s hide seems to consist of leaves
entries: Bees flit about the various flowers that sprout from its neck and tail.

legendary.name: Plant Shepherds
entries: Verdure dragons live harmoniously with nature, ensuring the plants under their care thrive and thrilling at the seasonal perfume and color of the flowers. They continually tend to the plants, ensuring no blight or other foul agent can gain a foothold. This “flora-first” focus isn’t to suggest they display antagonism toward fauna, and in fact, herbivores are essential to keep more competitive or invasive plants from taking over. And, while the dragons specifically forbid crop cultivation in their lands, they take no umbrage at crops outside their territory.

legendary.name: Plant Friends
entries: Since verdure dragons are more in tune with nature, they tend to enjoy the company of many plant creatures and fey. They particularly enjoy relationships with dryads and sprites—both of whom have a vested interest in preserving the sanctity of local plant life—and their lairs are often populated by awakened plants, treants, and similar plant creatures. Conversely, the dragons often feel uneasy (at best) with other varieties of dragons, wary of even the most well-intentioned, who so readily, even if inadvertently, destroy beloved plants in their path when just stopping by for a visit.

legendary.name: Maturing
entries: Young verdure dragons, or sometimes even wyrmlings, start their independence by picking out a patch of land at the edge of their parents’ gardens, where the flora is somehow less vibrant. They then set out to improve conditions and expand their little patches into large verdant pastures. These patches become their sanctums, where they cultivate rare or unique flowers. As they age, a verdure dragon’s appearance reflects the season—from the D D 110 wyrmling’s “early spring” appearance, sprouting fresh buds from its body, to the ancient’s “late autumn” appearance, running the gamut of fall colors over its leafy scales. A VERDURE DRAGON’S LAIR Verdure dragons live in wide-open spaces featuring flora of all types. Their lairs attract druids, plant creatures, and other creatures in tune with nature, where they can spend their time in a garden of delights and learn and absorb magic that they can use to beautify their own homes. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Grasping Plants. Vines and grasses growing in the dragon’s lair animate centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point or that enters the area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be restrained by the plants. A creature, including the restrained creature, can take its action to free the restrained creature by succeeding on a DC 15 STR check. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until the dragon uses this lair action again, or until the dragon dies. • Overwhelming Perfume. Flowers in the lair release an overwhelming, potent perfume on a point the dragon can see within 90 feet of it. Each creature within 30 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be poisoned until initiative count 20 on the next round. • Whisper of Leaves. Wind picks up among the leaves and grasses, creating a disquieting sound centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 30 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or be frightened until initiative count 20 on the next round. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region containing a verdure dragon’s lair is warped by its magic, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Bounteous Flora. Plant growth is more abundant within 10 miles of the dragon’s lair, making the area difficult terrain for all except the dragon and Plants. • Clean Air. Within 1 mile of the dragon’s lair, creatures that spend hit dice to regain hit points during a short rest double their CON modifier when determining how much they regain. If a creature spends a long rest within 1 mile of the lair, it has advantage on saves to end ongoing diseases or poisons. • Controlled Fires. Fires started by mundane or natural means within 1 mile of the dragon’s lair last long enough to clear undergrowth before sputtering out. If the dragon dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

Its eyes sparkle in the light of a nearby candle.

legendary.name: False Pseudodragons
entries: These dragons are roughly the size of small dogs, and they spend much of their time in libraries and laboratories. Along with their very stinger-like spiked tail and their poisonous bite, this has earned them the moniker of greater pseudodragons. However, they bear no true relation to pseudodragons. Plus, they have no desire to become some spellcasting dilettante’s familiar, for they tend to consider the practice demeaning.

legendary.name: Knowledge Hoarders
entries: Greater pseudodragons treasure knowledge above all else. Their hoards typically consist of rare books and ancient scrolls gathered over the course of decades. On rare occasions, they might take up residence in a library, school, abandoned mage’s tower, or similar place of knowledge, claiming the space as their own—though perhaps begrudgingly allowing others continued access, such as with a library, but always under observation. They guard their personal collections jealously but will permit access to petitioners bearing suitable offerings of rare or obscure knowledge.

trait.name: Demonic Resilience
entries: The arachnoth is resistant to cold, fire, and lightning damage. In addition, it is immune to poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The arachnoth has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The arachnoth makes one Claw attack and four Piercing Leg attacks. The arachnoth can replace its Claw attack with one Stinger attack.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the arachnoth can’t use its Claw on another target. D D 86 Piercing Leg. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6+ 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Stinger
entries: Melee Weapon Attack. +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, a creature is considered a thrall of the arachnoth. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Vomit Swarm (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The arachnoth spews forth a 15-foot cone of biting and stinging spiders and scorpions. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 25 (10d4) piercing damage and 27 (6d8) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Command Thrall
entries: The arachnoth can telepathically command a thrall or arachnid within 120 feet of it. The target can use its reaction to immediately move up to its speed or make one melee attack against one creature within 5 feet of it. An unwilling target must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or do as commanded.

bonus.name: Thrall Sight
entries: The arachnoth perceives through the senses of a spider, scorpion, or other arachnid within 120 feet of it or through the senses of one of its thralls for 1 minute. While perceiving in this way, it is deaf and blind in regard to its own senses. The arachnoth can use this bonus action again to end this effect. Demon, Demon Lord, Darhask The demon lounges on a bed of webbing—a long, stinger-tipped tail wrapping around its bright carapace like a shawl. It idly shifts its many limbs while watching on with a look of seeming boredom-tinged disdain.

bonus.name: Lord of All That Skitters
entries: Deep in the Hells drowses

bonus.name: Demon Lord Darhask, Lord of Spiders
entries: From the center of his ever-changing palace of webs, constantly collapsing and rebuilding, he claims dominion over various vermin and things with venom—mostly prizes stolen from other demon lords or stripped from their remains. Only his command of spiders and his legions of arachnoths (also in this book) are naturally his own.

bonus.name: Spiteful and Insecure
entries: Darhask is spiteful, even by the standards of demon lords. He remembers being “lesser” than his peers, remembers skittering among the footfalls of giants, trying to survive, and he resents anything that reminds him of those times. His ever-shifting plans often build from the need to avenge some slight or another, whether real or imagined, and his actions are always vastly disproportionate to the perceived offense.

bonus.name: Ever-Churning Webs
entries: Darhask embodies the churn of a web-spinning arachnid, constantly destroying and rebuilding his web of schemes to fit his needs and whims. These plans are always elaborate, multi-part affairs yet fragile and gossamer thin, so as they unspool, the participants can’t help but be caught up and damned by the consequences. Meanwhile, Darhask lounges in his web untouched, spinning up new plots from the old even before the dust settles.

bonus.name: Patron of Manipulators
entries: Darhask makes deals with those who imagine themselves master manipulators— with con artists, spymasters, scheming nobles—offering the service of his venom and his arachnoths to those who enmesh their schemes within his own. Unlike many demon lords, Darhask always offers those bound to him an out: if you succeed, realize all your desires while keeping your schemes intact, the Lord of Spiders will acknowledge your skill and refrain from claiming your soul when you die. Of course, such an alluring offer is more perilous than it seems, for Darhask is all too willing to cut an ambitious underling free to preserve his own schemes. DARHASK'S LAIR Darhask’s lair, the Silk Demesne, is an ever-shifting palace of webs that he builds, deconstructs, and rebuilds constantly. When he takes personal interest in the schemes of a subordinate, he extrudes strands of the Silk Demesne into that conspirator’s own lair. This enables direct support from the demon lord—at least until he loses interest or, after some slight, withdraws his support. While so linked to the strands of the Silk Demesne, lairs are warped by Darhask’s power, which creates one or more of the following regional effects: • Arachnid Surveillance. Spiders, scorpions, and other arachnids are a constant presence within 1 mile of the lair, and Darhask can perceive through the senses of any such creatures. • Sow Laxity. Humanoids near the lair are lax in personal defenses, becoming more susceptible to lies and less likely to raise questions. A creature has advantage on CHA (Deception) and CHA (Persuasion) checks against a Humanoid that has spent at least 24 hours within 10 miles of the lair. • Watcher’s Protection. Darhask knows when the subordinate or its underlings have been harmed within 5 miles of the lair and can summon a swarm of spiders to attack creatures in that area no more than once every 8 hours. If Darhask withdraws this connection or if the subordinate connected to the lair dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The arbalest crab is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The arbalest crab can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Stonewalker
entries: The arbalest crab can move through stone as if it was difficult terrain. The crab takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The arbalest crab makes two Pincer or Boulder attacks.

action.name: Pincer
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16). The crab has two pincers, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Boulder
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be knocked prone.

bonus.name: Squeeze
entries: One creature grappled by the arbalest crab must make a DC 16 STR save, taking 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

trait.name: Evasion
entries: If the arcane grenadier is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a DEX save to take only half damage, the arcane grenadier instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: The arcane grenadier is proficient with alchemist tools and doubles its proficiency bonus for any ability check it makes with alchemist tools. NPC FEATURES HUMANOID TRAITS Dwarf, Duergar Resistant to poison damage and the poisoned condition, darkvision 120 ft., Duergar Resilience trait, Reduce trait, Sunlight Sensitivity trait Elf, Drow Darkvision 120 ft., Fey Ancestry trait, Sunlight Sensitivity trait Elf, Shadow Fey Darkvision 60 ft., Fey Ancestry trait, Sunlight Sensitivity trait Formicbane Resistant to acid damage, burrowing speed of 30 ft., darkvision 60 ft., Dedicated Tunneler trait, Pack Tactics trait, Spiked Mane trait

action.name: Lob Explosive
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target suffers one of the following additional effects based on the type of bomb the grenadier used: • Bewildering Bomb. The target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. • Sticky Bomb. The target is restrained by a sticky, alchemical substance until the end of its next turn. • Thunderous Bomb. The target is deafened and can’t cast spells with verbal components until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Liquid Fire (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The arcane grenadier hurls an alchemical vial at a point it can see within 30 feet. The vial shatters and erupts into flames on impact. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a DC 13 DEX save, taking 10 (3d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, the area continues to burn until the end of the grenadier’s next turn. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 3 (1d6) fire damage. FEATURES Invisibility action, Enlarge bonus action — Shadow Traveler bonus action (usable a number of times per day equal to the creature’s PB) Spit Acid attack, Tail Swipe bonus action, Distracting Spit reaction

reaction.name: Concussive Blast
entries: When a creature the arcane grenadier can see hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it, the grenadier can clap two alchemical substances between its hands, blending them together and creating a blast of concussive energy. Each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from the grenadier must make a DC 13 STR save. On a failure, a creature is pushed up to 10 feet away from the grenadier and knocked prone. On a success, a creature is pushed up to 10 feet away from the grenadier but isn’t knocked prone.

trait.name: Devil’s Sight
entries: Magical darkness doesn’t impede the devil’s darkvision.

trait.name: Devilish Resilience
entries: The devil is resistant to cold damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to fire damage and poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Fear Aura
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the automata devil must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or be frightened until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The automata devil has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The automata devil makes one Bite attack, two Claw attacks, and two Whip attacks. It can replace both Claw attacks with a use of Shredding Maw.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) slashing damage.

action.name: Whip
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d4 + 6) slashing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 17). The automata devil has two whips, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Shredding Maw
entries: One creature grappled by the automata devil is pulled up to 10 feet toward the devil’s central maw, which shreds the creature with churning gears, razor teeth, and whirling blades. The target must make a DC 17 STR save, taking 36 (8d8) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Teleport
entries: The automata devil magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. 97 D D Devil, Blight A hunched, bald fiend—emaciated and jaundiced, with sunken features and a scorpion’s tail—grins malevolently as flakes of peeling skin fall from it like a shroud.

bonus.name: Agrarian Bargains
entries: Blight devils approach farmers, herders, and others who work the land, offering to improve crops or change the weather if the individual signs an infernal contract. As with all such bargains, those who sign find their souls damned.

bonus.name: Nature Meddlers
entries: These fiends use their powers over plants and weather without caring for how such changes effect the wider balance of nature, often causing entire ecosystems to spiral into ruin. Most druidic orders will eradicate blight devils wherever they are found.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The axolotl can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Limited Regeneration
entries: The axolotl regains 2 HP at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 HP. In addition, it regrows severed limbs after 24 hours.

trait.name: Underwater Camouflage
entries: The giant axolotl’s Stealth is 20 while underwater.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant axolotl makes one Bite attack and two Tail Slap attacks. It can replace its Bite attack with a Swallow.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the axolotl can’t Bite another target.

action.name: Tail Slap
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Swallow
entries: The axolotl makes one Bite attack against a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is swallowed, and the grapple ends. The swallowed target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the axolotl, and it takes 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of the axolotl’s turns. The axolotl can have only one target swallowed at a time. If the axolotl takes any damage from the swallowed creature, the axolotl must succeed on a DC 12 CON save at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone in a space with 5 feet of axolotl. If the axolotl dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting prone.

bonus.name: Suction
entries: The axolotl rapidly draws air or liquid into its mouth in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be pulled up to 15 feet closer to the axolotl. The axolotl can’t use Suction if it is grappling a creature.

bonus.name: Lunge (Recharge 4–6)
entries: When on land, the axolotl moves up to 30 feet. Opportunity attacks made against it during this movement have disadvantage.

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The ballista sentinel doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The ballista sentinel is immune to poison and psychic damage, and immune to exhaustion, and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ballista sentinel makes four Slam or Ballista Fire attacks. If two Slam attacks hit one Large or smaller creature, the ballista sentinel can choose for the target to be pushed up to 10 feet away from the sentinel.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Ballista Fire

action.name: Quarrel Blossom (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The ballista sentinel arcs a hail of ballista bolts toward a point on the ground it can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must make a DC 16 DEX save, taking 33 (6d10) piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Fortified Position
entries: The ballista sentinel extends its shield-like arms out from either side of its body. These shields provide three-quarters cover to creatures within 10 feet of the sentinel’s sides and to creatures no more than 5 feet behind it. The sentinel and its shields have arrow slits and similar holes to allow creatures to launch ranged attacks from these protected positions. While protected in this way, creatures making ranged attacks don’t suffer disadvantage from attacking while within 5 feet of a hostile creature, provided the hostile creature is on the other side of the sentinel’s shield arm. While its shield arms are extended, the ballista sentinel’s speed is halved, and it has disadvantage on ranged weapon attack rolls.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: As the myrmeke.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny myrmeke. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

trait.name: Thieving Swarm
entries: A creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or the swarm steals one object it is wearing or carrying. The object must weigh no more than 10 pounds, can’t be a weapon, and can’t be wrapped around or firmly attached to the target. The swarm can hold up to 15 such items at a time.

action.name: Pummels
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. Hit: 27 (6d8) bludgeoning damage, or 13 (3d8) bludgeoning damage if the swarm has half of its HP or fewer. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is restrained and moves with the swarm when the swarm moves. A creature, including the restrained creature, can free the restrained creature by succeeding on a DC 14 STR check. 213 M M

entries: The bar brawl can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the bar brawl can move through any opening large enough for a Medium Humanoid. Except for Liquid Courage, the bar brawl can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The bar brawl is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

action.name: Barstool
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 0 ft., one target in the bar brawl’s space. Hit: 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage, or 9 (2d8) if the bar brawl has half its HP or fewer.

action.name: Broken Bottles
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 0 ft., one target in the bar brawl’s space. Hit: 14 (4d6) slashing damage, or 7 (2d6) if the bar brawl has half its HP or fewer.

action.name: Darts
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft. Hit: 15 (6d4) piercing damage, or 7 (3d4) if the bar brawl has half its HP or fewer.

bonus.name: Liquid Courage (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The bar brawl imbibes nearby alcohol to gain access to a hidden reservoir of audacity and grit. The bar brawl gains 7 (2d6) temporary HP that last for 1 minute. 55 B B

trait.name: Artistic Expression
entries: The bard maestro has one primary form of artistic expression, such as song, poetry, dance, fashion, paint, or similar. It is immune to one type of damage associated with that artistic expression. For example, singing or oration might grant immunity to thunder damage, while painting might grant immunity to acid or poison damage. This trait can’t give the maestro resistance to force, necrotic, or radiant damage.

trait.name: Expressive Weapons
entries: The bard maestro’s weapon attacks are magical. When the maestro hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 damage of the type determined by Artistic Expression.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bard maestro makes three Rapier or Hand Crossbow attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Rapier
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) damage of the type determined by Artistic Expression.

action.name: Hand Crossbow
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: + 8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) damage of the type determined by Artistic Expression.

action.name: Full Performance (Recharge 6)
entries: The maestro sings a melody, dances a short routine, or gives some other performance related to its Artistic Expression, choosing up to three friendly creatures and up to three hostile creatures it can see within 60 feet of it. Each friendly target regains 9 (2d8) HP and has advantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the start of the maestro’s next turn.

action.name: Each hostile target must make a DC 17 CHA save
entries: On a failure, a creature takes 42 (12d6) psychic damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls and saves until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and doesn’t have disadvantage on attack rolls and saves.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The bard maestro casts one of the following spells, using CHA as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At will: dancing lights , mage hand , message , prestidigitation 3/day each: charm , disguise self , hideous laughter , suggestion 2/day each: dispel magic , hypnotic pattern , tongues 1/day each: confusion , greater invisibility

bonus.name: Quick Performance
entries: The maestro says a clever quip, paints a symbol that magically hangs in the air for a moment, performs the perfect pirouette, or gives some other short performance related to its Artistic Expression, choosing one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. If the target is friendly, the target gains 9 (2d8) temporary HP. If the target is hostile, the target must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the bard maestro’s next turn.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: The bard maestro adds 4 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the maestro must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

trait.name: Death Seeker
entries: If a barquil’s ward is killed, it descends into a rage for 1 hour. For the duration, its Shillelagh attacks deal an extra 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage on a hit.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The barquil is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Loyal Guardian
entries: The barquil can designate one ally within 30 feet of it to be its ward, creating a magical bond between them. Once a ward has been chosen, a new one can’t be chosen for 24 hours. The barquil has advantage on attack rolls against creatures that have dealt damage to its ward within the last hour.

trait.name: Quills
entries: A creature that touches the barquil or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The barquil makes three Shillelagh or Quill attacks.

action.name: Shillelagh
entries: Melee Weapon Attack. +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Quill
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack. +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage. If the target is a creature other than a Construct or Undead, it must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or lose 2 (1d4) HP at the start of each of its turns, as the quill sticks in the wound and causes excessive bleeding. Any creature can take an action to remove the quill and stanch the wound with a successful DC 10 WIS (Medicine) check. The wound also closes if the target receives magical healing.

bonus.name: Bolster Ward
entries: The barquil sacrifices its health for the benefit of its ward. It loses 4 (1d8) HP, and its ward gains an equal number of temporary HP.

reaction.name: Defensive Transport
entries: When the barquil’s ward takes damage from an attack or effect the barquil can see, the barquil can teleport up to 30 feet toward the ward into an unoccupied space. If it ends up in a space within 5 feet of its ward, it can reduce the damage the ward takes by 7 (2d6).

trait.name: Disease Sense
entries: The batonabi can pinpoint the location of poisoned creatures or creatures suffering from a disease within 60 feet of it and can sense the general direction of such creatures within 1 mile of it.

trait.name: Graveplague
entries: Not a specific disease, graveplague is a catch - all term for the collection of lesser diseases and leftover plagues carried and spread by batonabis. When a creature becomes infected with graveplague, it suffers one of the following diseases, determined randomly by rolling a d6. The disease lasts until cured or until the creature succeeds on a DC 13 CON save after finishing a long rest: 1. Aching Joints. The infected creature has disadvantage on weapon attack rolls. 2. Hacking Cough. The infected creature can’t take the Dash action, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet. 3. Itching Rash. The infected creature has disadvantage on INT and CHA saves and on CON saves to maintain concentration on a spell. 4. Painful Pustules. Each time the infected creature takes damage, there is a 25 percent chance a pustule bursts, sending pain throughout its body and incapacitating it until the end of its next turn. 5. Muscle Weakness. The infected creature’s weapon damage rolls are halved. 6. Swollen Nodes. The infected creature has disadvantage on saves against exhaustion and on saves against being paralyzed, poisoned, or stunned.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The batonabi doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The batonabi is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The batonabi makes two Plague Claw or Plague Bolt attacks. If both attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or contract the graveplague disease (see the Graveplague trait).

action.name: Plague Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage Plague Bolt. Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage plus 5 (2d4) poison damage.

action.name: Infectious Wind (Recharge 6)
entries: The batonabi exhales a sooty wind in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 13 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage and contracts the graveplague disease (see the Graveplague trait). On a success, a creature takes half the damage and doesn’t contract a disease. 57 B B

trait.name: Crop Whisperer (3/Day)
entries: The blight devil can spend 10 minutes sitting in an outdoor place in nature and cause the plants within a 1-mile radius of it to grow healthy and enriched (producing twice the normal yield) or cause the plants in that area to wither and die. If the devil enhanced the plants’ production, the effects last for 7 days.

trait.name: Devil’s Sight
entries: Magical darkness doesn’t impede the devil’s darkvision.

trait.name: Devilish Resilience
entries: The blight devil is resistant to cold damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to fire damage and poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The blight devil has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Weather Worker (3/Day)
entries: The blight devil can spend 10 minutes sitting in an outdoor place in nature and change the precipitation and temperature within 3 miles by up to two stages, up or down. This effect works like the weather conditions aspect of the control weather spell, except the conditions change at the end of the 10 minutes, the effects last for only 1 hour, and the devil doesn’t need to maintain concentration for that hour. D D 98

entries: The blight devil makes two Claw attacks and one Sting attack.

action.name: Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) slashing damage

reaction.name: The devil surveys all from behind its empty black eyes
entries: It clutches a scroll—seemingly covered in burning script—in one hand while the laws of the universe echo from its beak in a hollow rasp. Its bloody wings are folded around it like a shroud.

reaction.name: Magistrates of the Hells
entries: Jurist devils are responsible for maintaining law and order in the Hells. They adjudicate disputes between other devils, and they act as representatives when grievances are brought forth from outside the rigid infernal hierarchy. Though they are hardly the most powerful of devil-kind, their words are treated as binding by arch-devils. They also typically oversee and serve as witness to important infernal treaties and agreements.

reaction.name: Infernal Counsellors
entries: Jurist devils are among the least overtly violent of devils, serving primarily as historians and record-keepers. They are frequently sought by mortals for their extensive knowledge—their knowledge of the planes is second to few—and they have a greater than passing familiarity with matters of magic and nature. Jurist devils rarely trade in souls like other devils and are instead more interested in bartering to gain permission to remain on the Material Plane for extended periods of time. They are especially fond of libraries.

monster.name: Blueshroom
senses: keensense 120 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The blueshroom is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Warmth Recovery
entries: The reduction in HP maximum from a blueshroom’s features lasts for a creature until the creature finishes a long rest or until it finishes a short rest near a fire or in temperatures above 70 degrees Fahrenheit.

trait.name: Warmth Sense
entries: The blueshroom’s Perception is 17 when perceiving warm-blooded creatures or detecting temperatures above 70 degrees Fahrenheit.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The blueshroom makes two Slam or Icicle attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) cold damage. If the target is a creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead, it must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or its HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the cold damage taken, and the blueshroom regains HP equal to half that amount. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

action.name: Icicle
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) cold damage.

action.name: Deep Chill (Recharge 6)
entries: The blueshroom induces a drastic reduction in temperature in a 20-foot radius around it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 CON save, taking 14 (4d6) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save also has its HP maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken, and the blueshroom regains HP equal to the single highest amount of cold damage dealt. A creature dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

bonus.name: Ice Shield
entries: When the blueshroom is the target of an attack, it can release a lattice of ice crystals to protect itself. Until the start of its next turn or until the blueshroom takes fire damage, it has a +2 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack.

trait.name: Infernal Mark
entries: A creature that takes damage from the bog bounder suffers an infernal mark around the wound until it finishes a long rest or until the mark is removed with a greater restoration spell or similar magic. While marked, a creature has disadvantage on saves against effects from Fiends other than the bog bounder, and Fiends within 1 mile of the marked creature can sense its direction and general location.

trait.name: Soulstep
entries: Once on its turn, the bog bounder can use 10 feet of its movement to step magically into a Medium or larger creature marked with its demonic mark within 1 mile of it and emerge from the creature into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the creature. When the bog bounder emerges, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or take 5 (2d4) necrotic damage and be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Swamp Walk
entries: The bog bounder can move across the surface of water as if it were harmless, solid ground. This trait otherwise works like the water walk spell. In addition, difficult terrain composed of mud, water, or swamp plants doesn’t cost it extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bog bounder makes two Talon or Teleportation Barb attacks.

action.name: Talon
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (4d4 + 4) slashing damage, and the target suffers an infernal mark (see the Infernal Mark trait).

action.name: Teleportation Barb
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) psychic damage, the target suffers an infernal mark (see the Infernal Mark trait), and the target must succeed on a DC 14 WIS save or be teleported to an unoccupied space on the ground within 15 feet of it that the bog bounder can see.

bonus.name: Flit
entries: The bog bounder takes the Disengage or Hide action.

bonus.name: Noxious Geyser
entries: A spray of stench erupts from a point on a surface the bog bounder can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 5 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. 59 B B

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The ogre can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The ogre is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Staggering Opportunist
entries: When the ogre hits a creature with an opportunity attack, the target must succeed on a DC 14 STR save or be knocked prone. O O 224

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ogre makes two Greatclub attacks.

action.name: Greatclub
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Rotting Belch (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The ogre exhales a cloud of vile vapor in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 14 CON save, taking 18 (4d8) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Bubbling Burp
entries: When the bog ogre hasn’t released its

bonus.name: Rotting Belch, gases roil and bubble in its gut
entries: While Rotting Belch is available, the ogre can release a short burp toward up to two creatures it can see within 10 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. Ogre, Riptide The massive humanoid leaps to the deck with a thunderous crash and whoop, wearing a kilt made from sailcloth and belted with a thick hemp rope and cargo netting across their chest. They wield a club made from a broken mast in one hand and twirl an anchor tied to a rope in the other.

bonus.name: Salty Seafarers
entries: Riptide ogres love being in and around the sea, delighting at the wind in their hair and the salty air in their lungs. Consummate salvagers and tinkerers, they plunder ships and communities to obtain what materials they need.

bonus.name: Loose Guidelines
entries: Found near coasts, riptide ogres collect ragtag crews of other ogres, sea-dwelling humanoids, and occasionally, coastal or seafaring landlubbers. Each crew is its own culture of rowdy pirates with all the carousing, rivalries, and competition one might expect.

bonus.name: Deep-Sea Connection
entries: Riptide ogres can control small waterspouts, waves, and whirlpools, and they use these to capture creatures and claim cargo. Unlike most other pirates, they can store their captured cargo beneath the waves, and they often broker deals with underwater creatures to protect hidden treasure.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the bone whale remains motionless and prone, it is indistinguishable from an inanimate whale skeleton.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The bone whale deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The bone whale doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bone whale uses its Withering Curse. It then makes two Fin attacks and one Tail Slap attack.

action.name: Fin
entries: Melee Weapon Attack. +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (6d6 + 5) piercing damage.

action.name: Tail Slap
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (4d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 18 STR save or be pushed up to 20 feet away from the bone whale.

action.name: Withering Curse
entries: Each creature of the bone whale’s choice within 120 feet of it must succeed on a DC 18 CON save or be cursed. If a creature’s save is successful, the creature is immune to the bone whale’s Withering Curse for the next 24 hours. Every 24 hours that elapse, the cursed creature must repeat the save, reducing its HP maximum by 3 (1d6) on a failure. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest after the curse is cured. The creature dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

bonus.name: Encage
entries: The bone whale rears up and wraps the bones of its ribs around one Huge or smaller creature it can see within 10 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 18 STR save or be caged. While caged, the target is restrained, can’t teleport or be teleported outside the cage, and can’t be hit by the bone whale’s attacks, and it takes 9 (2d8) necrotic damage at the start of each of the whale’s turns. When the bone whale moves, the caged creature moves with it. The whale can have up to one Huge, two Large, four Medium, or eight

bonus.name: Small creatures caged at a time
entries: A creature within 5 feet of the bone whale can take its action to free a caged target by succeeding on a DC 18 STR check.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The gnoll’s Perception is 21 when perceiving by smell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bone-brewer makes two Eldritch Bite or Eldritch Bolt attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, the target is hexed until the start of the bone-brewer’s next turn. While hexed, the target subtracts 1d4 from each ability check, attack roll, and save it makes.

action.name: Eldritch Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage. G G 160 Eldritch Bolt. Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) force damage.

bonus.name: Unleash Marrow
entries: The gnoll bone-brewer tears open a ritually prepared bone, unleashing the magic. The bone-brewer sends the magic to up to two creatures it can see within 60 feet of it, causing one of the following effects on each: • Attack! The target has advantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the start of the bone-brewer’s next turn. • Bolster. The target gains 5 (2d4) temporary HP. • Hinder. The target must succeed on a DC 14 STR save or have its speed reduced by 10 feet. • Terrify. The target must succeed on a DC 14 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Bracing Rampage
entries: When a gnoll the bone-brewer can see uses its Rampage reaction, the bone-brewer can bite into a bone and attack rolls against that gnoll don’t have advantage from the gnoll’s Rampage reaction. Golem, Hoard A pile of gold, jewelry, and weapons rises on its own like a tidal wave of riches—and displays a cold and determined face.

reaction.name: Dragon Fears Made Real
entries: The hoard golem was born from a dragon’s paranoia at losing their treasures to thieves. Despite their great power, dragons are often very suspicious of others, and the first hoard golem was created with one’s realization that there could be no guardian more trustworthy than the hoard itself. Since then, the secret of hoard golem construction has spread.

reaction.name: Patient Homebodies
entries: Hoard golems are patient guardians, lying in wait for anyone other than their creators to come within striking distance. Hoard golems fight to the death, but they rarely leave the rooms they inhabit for fear that clever treasure hunters might trick the hoard into walking itself right out of their owner’s lair.

reaction.name: Silent and Wealthy
entries: Hoard golems can’t speak and are typically 25 feet tall, weighing 20,000 pounds. A hoard golem’s body is composed of various items—copper, silver, gold, works of art, armor, weapons, and magical items— and worth at least 5,000 gp.

monster.name: Bonebrash
languages: understands the languages of its creator but

trait.name: Bone Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to piercing and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

trait.name: Clambering Crawl
entries: Difficult terrain doesn’t cost the bonebrash extra movement.

trait.name: Nebulous Bond
entries: The necromantic bonds keeping the bonebrash’s individual pieces together are tenuous at best. If a bonebrash takes radiant damage, it must succeed on a DC 12 CON save or lose cohesion until the end of its next turn. During this time, the bonebrash’s speed is halved, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls.

trait.name: Skeletal Clutch
entries: The bonebrash’s disparate bone parts grab and cling to creatures in its space. A creature that attempts to leave the bonebrash’s space must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or fall prone in the bonebrash’s space.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for the Tiny skull of a Humanoid. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The bonebrash doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The bonebrash is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Skeletal Assault
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (4d6) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the bonebrash’s choice) plus 11 (2d10) necrotic damage, or 7 (2d6) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the bonebrash’s choice) plus 5 (1d10) necrotic damage if the bonebrash has half its HP or fewer.

bonus.name: Scramble
entries: The bonebrash takes the Dash action but has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of its next turn. CREATING A BONEBRASH A spellcaster can cast the animate dead spell to create a bonebrash. Instead of a pile of bones or a corpse, the caster must instead have the remains of at least four skeletons that were once animated then reduced to 0 HP. When you cast the animate dead spell in this way, the casting time is 10 minutes. 61 B B

trait.name: Boundary Bond
entries: The border sentinel is bound to a gate or wall made of stone or of greenery, such as a hedge, and it is aware of damage dealt to any part of the boundary. If the sentinel moves farther than 60 feet from its wall, it loses its Animate Boundary and Boundary Teleport bonus actions. If it remains farther than 1 mile from its bound wall for 24 hours, it is automatically teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of its bound wall, regardless of distance. It can bind itself to a different wall with an 8-hour ritual.

trait.name: False Appearance (Animated Form Only)
entries: While the border sentinel remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary wall, hedge, or similar boundary.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The fey is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The border sentinel can move through other creatures and objects as if they

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The border sentinel makes three Fey Touch attacks, or it makes two Slam or Fling Debris attacks.

action.name: Fey Touch
entries: Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) psychic damage.

action.name: Slam (Animated Form Only)
entries: Melee Weapon Attack : +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Fling Debris (Animated Form Only)
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (4d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Animate Boundary
entries: The spirit inhabits and animates a section of the wall that serves as its bound boundary or ends the effect, returning the material to the wall. While animating its bound wall, the border sentinel is Large, has an AC of 15, loses its immunity to the grappled, prone, and restrained conditions, and can’t fly. If the sentinel moves through a creature or object with Incorporeal Movement while animating its boundary, the material falls off its spectral body, ending this effect.

bonus.name: Boundary Teleport (True Form Only)
entries: The border sentinel teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of any section of its bound wall. If it is animating its bound boundary when it uses this bonus action, the animation immediately ends.

trait.name: Standing Leap
entries: The brachysnatch’s long jump is up to 30 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The brachysnatch makes one Bite attack, two Vise Claw attacks, and one Gore attack, or it makes three Acid Spit attacks. It can replace its Bite attack with an Acid Spit attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) acid damage.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage.

action.name: Vise Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and takes 4 (1d8) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the brachysnatch’s turns. The brachysnatch has two claws, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Acid Spit
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) acid damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Disgorge (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The brachysnatch empties out some of the contents of its stomach in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 14 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 28 (6d8) acid damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Detach Claw
entries: The brachysnatch detaches one of its vise claws. A creature grappled by the claw remains grappled after this detaching. The brachysnatch can use its bonus action to reattach its claw while within 5 feet of the claw. Otherwise, it regrows a detached vise claw after it finishes a long rest. 63 B B

monster.name: Broken Fixer
languages: understands the languages of its creator and

trait.name: Auto-Repair
entries: The broken fixer regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 HP. If the fixer takes lightning damage, this trait doesn’t function at the start of the fixer’s next turn.

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The broken fixer doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The broken fixer is immune to poison and psychic damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The broken fixer makes two Deadly Tool attacks. It can replace one attack with Repair.

action.name: Deadly Tool
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the fixer’s choice).

action.name: Repair
entries: The broken fixer restores 11 (2d8 + 2) HP to a

action.name: Construct or object within 5 feet of it
entries: It can’t use this action to repair itself.

action.name: Flame Jet (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The broken fixer unleashes a jet of flame in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 13 DEX save, taking 31 (7d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Overclock
entries: The broken fixer makes adjustments to a friendly construct it can see within 5 feet of it, enhancing the target’s performance. Until the end of the target’s next turn, the target’s speed is doubled, it gains a +2 bonus to AC, it has advantage on DEX saves, and it gains an additional action. This extra action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action. When this effect ends, the target can only take an action or bonus action on its next turn, not both, and can’t make more than one melee or ranged attack during its turn.

monster.name: Broodlings
languages: understands Deep Speech but can’t speak

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and the swarm has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form. C C 72 Scuttling Shield. Friendly creatures in the swarm’s space have half-cover against attacks originating outside of the swarm’s space.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny broodling. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

action.name: Gnaw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. Hit: 18 (4d8) piercing damage, or 9 (2d8) piercing damage if the swarm has half its HP or fewer, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 DEX or its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Water Jet
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (6d4) bludgeoning damage, or 7 (3d4) bludgeoning damage if the swarm has half its HP or fewer, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the swarm.

reaction.name: Brood Protection
entries: When a friendly creature in the swarm’s space takes damage, that creature takes only half the damage, and the swarm of broodlings takes the remaining damage. Chuul, Potentate

reaction.name: The towering chuul raises a claw skyward
entries: The air crackles with magical potential as arcane energy arcs from the sky, lighting up the claw with a baleful light.

reaction.name: Imperial Remnants
entries: Once, potentates led the armies of ancient chuul empires. They would wade into the thick of battle at the head of grand armies, tearing opposing champions to pieces and leading grand war rituals. When the empires fell, however, the surviving chuul lost the means to elevate their own to such levels.

reaction.name: Accidental Empowerment
entries: Occasionally, when a chuul devours a potent source of magic or survives exposure to a powerful magical effect, it might trigger the metamorphosis. These potentates immediately grow in intellect and power, able to channel arcane energies through their bodies.

reaction.name: Revanchist Warlords
entries: After its metamorphosis, a potentate gathers any nearby wandering chuul into a warband and sets about conquering any coastal settlements in their path, attempting to reclaim past glory.

monster.name: Candlecorpse
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the candlecorpse remains motionless and prone, it is indistinguishable from an inanimate, wax-covered Humanoid skeleton.

trait.name: Hot Wax
entries: A creature that touches the candlecorpse or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) fire damage.

trait.name: Illumination
entries: The candlecorpse sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The candlecorpse doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The candlecorpse is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The candlecorpse makes two Battleaxe attacks.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands, plus 4 (1d8) fire damage.

action.name: Flame Wave (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The candlecorpse directs the fire of its wicks in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 14 DEX save, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success.

bonus.name: Burning Wax
entries: The candlecorpse lobs a wad of hot wax at one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or be restrained by wax. While restrained in this way, the creature takes 2 (1d4) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. This damage ends after 1 minute or if the creature takes cold damage. A creature, including the restrained target, can take its action to free the creature by succeeding on a DC 14 STR check. If the restrained target has taken cold damage, this check is made with advantage. 65 C C

monster.name: Carrion Nightmare
languages: any languages it knew in life

trait.name: Heightened Sight and Smell
entries: The carrion nightmare’s Perception is 17 when perceiving by sight or smell.

trait.name: Speak with Scavenger Birds
entries: The carrion nightmare can communicate with vultures, giant vultures, and other carrion birds as if they shared a language.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The carrion nightmare doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The carrion nightmare is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The carrion nightmare makes two

action.name: Beak attacks and two Claw attacks
entries: It can replace both Claw attacks with Harvest Organ. C C 66 Beak. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target.

action.name: Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage
entries: The target is grappled (escape DC 17) if it is a Medium or smaller creature and the carrion nightmare isn’t already grappling a creature.

action.name: Harvest Organ
entries: The carrion nightmare digs into the flesh of a creature it is grappling. The creature must make a DC 17 CON save, taking 28 (8d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that failed the save also has its HP maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

reaction.name: Consume Organ
entries: If the target of Harvest Organ failed its save, the carrion nightmare can eat the harvested organ and regains HP equal to the necrotic damage taken by the target.

trait.name: Desert Walk
entries: Difficult terrain composed of nonmagical sand doesn’t cost the camel extra movement.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Spit (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The cavalry camel spits a nauseating wad of phlegm at a creature it can see within 15 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be blinded until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Defensive Kick
entries: When a creature the camel can see within 5 feet of it deals damage to the camel or its rider, the camel can kick the creature. The attacker must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the camel and knocked prone.

monster.name: Celebrant Shade
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The celebrant shade can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The celebrant shade doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The celebrant shade is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The celebrant shade makes two Induce Celebration or Fling Debris attacks.

action.name: Induce Celebration
entries: Melee Spell Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) psychic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 CHA save or spend either an action or bonus action (the target’s choice) on its next turn dancing, shouting, or performing some other celebratory activity.

action.name: Fling Debris
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Overindulge
entries: A creature the shade can see within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be poisoned for 1 minute, feeling as if it overindulged in food, drink, or some other vice. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

reaction.name: Party Harder
entries: When a creature the shade can see within 30 feet of it succeeds on an ability check or save, the shade fills the creature’s mind with unearned gregariousness. The creature must succeed on a DC 13 CHA save or be charmed by every creature it can see until the end of its next turn. 67 C C

monster.name: Cerulean Slime
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Adhesive
entries: The cerulean slime adheres to anything that touches it. A Large or smaller creature adhered to the slime is also grappled by it (escape DC 16). Ability checks made to escape this grapple have disadvantage. The slime can grapple only one creature at a time. C C 68 Amorphous. The cerulean slime can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Amphibious

trait.name: Grappler

trait.name: Ooze Nature

trait.name: Ooze Resilience

trait.name: Spider Climb

trait.name: Underwater Camouflage

bonus.name: Chilling Jet

trait.name: Inscrutable

trait.name: Limited Magic Immunity

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt

action.name: Chaotic Pulse (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The chaos-touched rakshasa unleashes a wave of energy from its chaos-wracked mind in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 CHA save. On a failure, a creature takes 28 (8d6) psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more is stunned until the end of its next turn instead.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The chaos-touched rakshasa casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using CHA as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16). At will: hideous laughter , minor illusion 3/day each: bestow curse , suggestion 1/day: confusion

bonus.name: Terrifying Gaze

bonus.name: DC 16 CHA save or be frightened for 1 minute

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience

trait.name: Barbed Grapple

trait.name: Fear Aura

action.name: Claw

action.name: Barbed Tentacle
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 15). The chasmal horror can grapple up to two creatures at a time.

action.name: Phantasmal Dread (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The chasmal horror exhales an ear-piercing and mind-rending screech in a 30- foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 CON save, taking 18 (4d8) psychic damage and 17 (5d6) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Mind Drain
entries: The chasmal horror feeds on the fear of one frightened creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 INT save or be frozen with fear until the end of its next turn. While frozen with fear, a creature’s speed is reduced to 0, and the chasmal horror has advantage on attack rolls against it. If the target fails the save by 5 or more, its INT is reduced by 1d4. The target becomes a mindless thrall of the chasmal horror if this reduces its INT to 0. Otherwise, the reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. 69 C C

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the chilldeath grass remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a patch of tundra grass.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The chilldeath grass is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Seed Blast
entries: When the chilldeath grass dies, its stored heat bursts out in an explosion of super-heated, immature seeds. Each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or suffer a level of exhaustion from the heat.

action.name: Barbed Blades
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage, and barbs break off the plant into the wound. A creature with chilldeath barbs in its wound loses 2 (1d4) HP at the start of each of its turns, as the barbs irritate the wound and prevent it from closing. Any creature can take an action to remove the barbs and stanch the wound with a successful DC 12 WIS (Medicine) check. The barbs also pop out if the target receives magical healing.

bonus.name: Leech Heat
entries: The chilldeath grass lashes a heat-sapping tendril at a creature it can see within 10 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or its HP maximum is reduced by 3 (1d6). The chilldeath grass regains HP equal to that amount. The target has disadvantage on the save if the chilldeath’s barbs are stuck in its wound. Chol, Ystol A lanky, translucent figure slinks out from a crack in the rock face and whips out extremely long arms in attack.

bonus.name: Mercenary Nature
entries: Ystol are some of the lowest ranked fiends of the chol: weaker than their brethren but therefore also cheaper to hire. In larger forces, ystol are typically used as infantry, but they are sometimes hired as advance scouts to infiltrate and assess enemy territory or potential battlegrounds. They prefer payment in cut gems and other precious stones.

bonus.name: Flexible Bodies
entries: Ystol have long, boneless arms that they wield like whips, and their lanky, flexible forms allow them to squeeze into spaces in which larger creatures can’t fit. They take advantage of this for stealth and infiltration, hiding in unlikely and out-of-the-way spaces to observe or ambush foes.

bonus.name: Rejected Ascension
entries: Like their chol brethren, a ystol can ascend into a higher form of chol, typically a czol, once it has absorbed enough of its preferred payment. However, many ystol forego or delay their ascension, preferring the fluidity and flexibility of their current forms and the unique jobs these forms allow them to take.

trait.name: Construct Nature

trait.name: Construct Resilience

trait.name: Surveillance Unit

action.name: Poisoned Dart

bonus.name: Disassembly
entries: The assassin reconfigures its body into a snakelike, segmented cylinder, which allows it to move through a space as narrow as 6 inches wide. It can reassemble itself into its true form by using this bonus action again. While in its snake form, the assassin’s walking and climbing speeds each increase by 15 feet, and it can’t attack.

action.name: Wind Up (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The constructor anchors its feet into the ground and winds up its gears. Until the start of its next turn, its movement speed is 0, and it can’t take reactions. At the start of its next turn, it releases the tension, swinging its sledgehammer in a wide circle. Each creature within 20 feet of the constructor when it swings must make a DC 16 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage, is pushed up to 10 feet away from the constructor, and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed or knocked prone.

bonus.name: Mortar Spray

A creature, including the restrained target, can take its action to free the target by succeeding on a DC 16 STR check.

entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) poison damage. The scorpion then chooses one of the following alchemical solutions, and the target must make a DC 16 CON save. The effect is determined by the chosen solution. • Hallucinatory Elixir. On a failed save, the target sees enemies everywhere for 1 minute. On its turn, the target uses its action to make a melee attack against the nearest creature that is not the clockwork scorpion, moving up to its speed toward the creature, if necessary. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful save, the target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn instead. • Vocal Paralytic. On a failed save, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the target is unable to speak or cast spells that require verbal components. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target succeeds on the initial save, it is poisoned until the end of its next turn instead.

action.name: Acid Spray (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The clockwork scorpion spews acid in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 DEX save, taking 42 (12d6) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

reaction.name: Gas Nozzles
entries: When the clockwork scorpion takes damage, it can release a toxic gas. Each creature within 5 feet of it takes 3 (1d6) poison damage. If the damage it took was fire, the gas ignites and deals an extra 3 (1d6) fire damage.

trait.name: Fey Resilience

trait.name: Familiar
entries: The flitkith can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the flitkith senses as long as they are within 1 Flitkith Resilience. The flitkith is immune to poison damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

action.name: Cloth Whip
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be pulled up to 10 feet toward the flitkith.

bonus.name: Manipulate Cloth
entries: The cloth flitkith magically manipulates a piece of cloth worn by a creature within 60 feet of it, causing one of the following effects: • Strangle. The target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be unable to breathe, speak, or cast spells with verbal components until the end of its next turn. • Tangle Limb. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or have disadvantage on weapon attacks until the end of its next turn. • Trip. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or fall prone.
