trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The coastal marauder is immune to poison and psychic damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Internal Cargo Space
entries: There is a hollow, watertight interior within the bulk of the marauder’s body, accessed through its mouth. The marauder can hold up to 540 pounds, up to one Medium creature, or up to two Small creatures within this space.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The coastal marauder deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The coastal marauder makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) slashing damage.

action.name: Breach
entries: The coastal marauder swims up to 20 feet, emerging from the water and landing on the surface. Each Large or smaller creature within 10 feet of where it lands must make a DC 15 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 31 (7d8) bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from the marauder. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed.

bonus.name: Create Drag
entries: The marauder grabs onto a seagoing vehicle within 5 feet of it while beneath the waterline, creating drag and slowing the vehicle. While the marauder is attached, the vehicle’s speed is reduced by 10 feet, to a minimum speed of 5 feet. For each marauder beyond the first using Create Drag, the vehicle’s speed is reduced by an additional 10 feet. Until the marauder ends this effect (no action required), it moves with the vehicle and can’t make Claw attacks.

bonus.name: Swallow
entries: The coastal marauder opens its jaws and swallows one Medium or smaller object that isn’t being worn or carried or one willing Medium or smaller creature, depositing the target into its internal cargo space. A creature can exit the marauder by spending 10 feet of movement, falling prone in a space within 5 feet of the marauder. 77 C C Corpselight Gardener A thin, pale figure—notable for its pointed ears and unruly hair—crouches before a stand of gnarly trees, incongruous with their surroundings. A ghostly glow seems to emanate from the trees themselves, outlining the sickle clutched in the figure’s hand.

bonus.name: Preservers of Life
entries: Corpselight gardeners are enigmatic fey devoted to bringing life to the barren spaces of the world in the form of ghostly groves, resulting in especially eerie oases. Because such areas are largely inhospitable and unable to normally sustain such growth, these fey must feed the lifeforce of mortal creatures to the groves. And though the ghostly, bilious glow of the trees is ever-present, it flares more brightly when actively feeding.

bonus.name: Dedicated Protectors
entries: A corpselight gardener’s dedication to their grove is an almost sacred duty that supersedes all other concerns. They will fight with equal ferocity to either feed or defend a grove, for failure would surely mean death for the trees. However, most gardeners stop short of sacrificing their own lives for their groves since, while a difficult, time-consuming process, starting a new grove is far from impossible.

bonus.name: Ghostly Light
entries: Some suspect a connection between corpselight groves and will-o’-wisps, but other than tales of will-o’-wisps being drawn to such areas, nothing is certain. A CORPSELIGHT GARDENER’S LAIR Corpselight gardeners keep careful watch over groves of corpselight trees, planting them in barren areas, such as badlands, deserts, ruins, and even arctic realms. The gardeners call their groves home, protecting the trees and in turn being protected by them. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the corpselight gardener can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the gardener can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Branch Swipe. Tree branches in the corpselight grove swipe at up to two creatures the corpselight gardener can see within 60 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet in a direction of the gardener’s choice and knocked prone. • Corpselight Flare. The light emitted by the corpselight grove flares brightly. Up to two creatures the corpselight gardener can see within 60 feet of it must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or be blinded until initiative count 20 on the next round. • Quicksand. The ground centered on a point the corpselight gardener can see within 60 feet of it turns to quicksand. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 16 DEX save or be restrained C C 78 by the quicksand. The quicksand lasts for 1 minute, until the gardener uses this lair action again, or until the gardener dies. A creature, including the restrained target, can take its action to free the restrained creature by succeeding on a DC 16 STR check. If a creature restrained by quicksand isn’t freed by the start of its second turn after being restrained, it begins to drown. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region containing a corpselight gardener’s lair is warped by the grove, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Befouled Water. Within 1 mile of the lair, the air is filled with a stinking, rotten-smelling fog at dawn and dusk that lightly obscures the area, and standing water in the area is tainted and not safe to drink. • Dead Echoes. Ghostly representations of the creatures that fed the corpselight grove fade in and out of view within 1 mile of the lair. • Will-o’-Wisp Attraction. Will-o’-wisps are drawn to the region and are encountered more often within 10 miles of the corpselight grove. If the corpselight gardener dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Corpselight Tree Stride
entries: Once on its turn, the gardener can use 10 feet of its movement to step magically into one corpselight tree within its reach and emerge from a second corpselight tree within 60 feet the first tree, appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the second tree. Both trees must be Medium or larger.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The gardener is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the gardener fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Necrotic Weapons
entries: The gardener’s weapon attacks are magical. When the gardener hits with any weapon, it deals an extra 3d8 necrotic damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Speak with Plants
entries: The gardener can communicate with Plants and nonmagical plants as if they share a language.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The corpselight gardener makes three Sickle or Necrotic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Sickle
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Necrotic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) necrotic damage.

action.name: Deathly Growth (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The corpselight gardener causes glowing, life-sapping vines and roots to erupt from a point on the ground it can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must make a DC 16 DEX save, taking 31 (7d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The area then becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes 4 (1d8) necrotic damage for every 5 feet it travels. The gardener is immune to the effects of its Deathly Growth.

bonus.name: Intimidate
entries: The corpselight gardener projects fear at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. That creature must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or the gardener has advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the gardener’s turn.

legendary.name: Detect Life
entries: The corpselight gardener automatically detects every creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead within 30 feet of it, pinpointing the current location of each.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The gardener moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. HAZARD: CORPSELIGHT GROVE A corpselight grove consists of gnarly trees that glow with ghostly light and sap the life from creatures that spend too long among them. Creatures entering these groves find them cold and unnerving, filled with disorienting shadows and strange sounds and smells. Trigger: When a creature enters a grove of at least two corpselight trees, it suffers the effects of the hazard. Effects: While in the area, a creature that isn’t a Construct, Fey, or Undead has disadvantage on death saves. When such a creature finishes a short or long rest

legendary.name: Drain Life (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 10 feet of the gardener that isn’t a Construct or Undead must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or take 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. The gardener then regains HP equal to the total necrotic damage dealt. in the area, it must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or its

legendary.name: HP maximum is reduced by 5 (2d4)
entries: A creature dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest outside of the grove. Resolution: An affected creature must leave the area or finish a long rest outside the area, if being in the grove reduced its HP maximum. If the corpselight gardener that tends the grove is slain, the grove perishes 2d100 days later and is no longer a hazard. 79 C C Crab, Arbalest The oversized crustacean balances nimbly on shovel-like legs as it hurls a boulder with its pincers. A tangled mass of tentacles protruding from its armored maw seem poised to burst forth and latch onto whatever prey comes near.

legendary.name: Built for War
entries: The creatures that would come to be known as arbalest crabs were once common crabs. Historically, when charged by their ruler to devise a living weapon to support their mountain kingdom’s armies, the court’s magic wielders worked together to meet the challenge. Though largely successful in their experiments in making giant crabs, the earliest results ultimately proved too easily manipulated and were turned against their creators.

legendary.name: Uncontrollable Weapons
entries: Iterating on their designs to perfect their living siege engines, the creators of the arbalest crab increased their subjects’ intelligence. This had the desired effect of making them less susceptible to enemy manipulation, but their own control over the creature’s was drastically compromised. The final nail in the coffin was their unexpected ability to move through stone. The creatures easily escaped their captivity, laying waste to much of the kingdom on their way out.

legendary.name: Wild and Dangerous
entries: Now, arbalest crabs breed true in the wild. While few of their eggs or young survive to adulthood, existing populations of the crabs are still large enough that they pose a real danger to settlements in mountainous regions—or even those underground. They are highly territorial and attack intruders on sight. Survivors of such attacks swear the creatures specifically targeted spellcasters over other available targets, which has given the creatures an undeserved reputation as magic detectors.

trait.name: Adaptive Camouflage
entries: If the dragon spends at least 1 minute in a particular type of terrain, such as a forest, its Stealth is 18 while in that terrain.

trait.name: Pounce
entries: If the dragon moves at least 15 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Claw attack on the same turn, the target must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the dragon can make one Claw attack against it as a bonus action.

entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Psychic Fog Breath
entries: (Recharge 5–6). The dragon exhales a 15-foot cone of sparkling blue fog. Each creature in the area must make a DC 10 CON save, taking 21 (6d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

trait.name: Misty Form
entries: The crimson mist can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Sapping Mist
entries: The crimson mist regains 5 HP at the start of its turn if the mist has at least 1 HP and if at least one creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead and that has blood is in its space. A creature that starts its turn in the mist’s space has disadvantage on attack rolls that use STR or DEX until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The crimson mist doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The crimson mist is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The crimson mist makes two Life Sap attacks, or it uses Call Blood.

action.name: Life Sap
entries: Melee Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the mist’s space. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) necrotic damage, and the target’s HP maximum is reduced by half the necrotic damage taken. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest.

action.name: Call Blood
entries: The crimson mist calls forth the blood from within up to two creatures it can see within 30 feet of it that aren’t Constructs or Undead and that have blood. The target’s blood drips from its skin, eyes, mouth, nose, and similar then floats through the air into the mist. Each target must make a DC 15 CON save, taking 31 (7d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The crimson mist regains HP equal to half the total necrotic damage dealt.

reaction.name: No Escape
entries: When a creature in the crimson mist’s space moves out of that space, the crimson mist can fly up to half its speed, moving with the creature and remaining in the creature’s space, provided it has the movement. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks from the moving target, but it can provoke opportunity attacks from other creatures. 81 C C

trait.name: Uncontrollable
entries: The crypt lurcher can’t be magically commanded or placed under the control of another creature.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The crypt lurcher doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The crypt lurcher is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The crypt lurcher makes two Claw attacks .

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage. C C 82

bonus.name: Hurl Limb
entries: The crypt lurcher pulls a limb off its body and throws that limb at a creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target suffers a different effect depending on the limb thrown: • Arm. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the crypt lurcher’s next turn, as the arm briefly hangs on it. • Head. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or the head gains a hold on the target with its teeth. The target takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature, including the target, can detach the head by succeeding on a DC 13 STR check. • Leg. The target must make a DC 13 DEX save, as the leg bucks and kicks at the target’s legs. On a failure, the target is knocked prone, and its speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a success, the target’s speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Counterattack (Recharge 6)
entries: When a creature the crypt lurcher can see hits it with an attack, the crypt lurcher can make one Claw attack against the attacker.

monster.name: Crystalline Servitor
languages: understands all languages but can’t speak,

trait.name: Bane of the Undead
entries: The crystalline servitor has advantage on attack rolls against Undead, and Undead have disadvantage on saves against the servitor’s abilities. When the servitor deals damage to an Undead, the damage isn’t reduced by any resistances or immunities the Undead has to that damage.

trait.name: Blizzard Aura
entries: The crystalline servitor emits a vortex of snow, ice, and wind that extends out from it, lightly obscuring the area within 15 feet of the servitor. A creature that starts its turn in the area or enters the area for the first time on a turn takes 3 (1d6) cold damage and must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or become chilled until the start of its next turn. While chilled, a creature has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its speed is halved. At the start of its turn, the servitor chooses if this aura is active.

trait.name: Celestial Resilience
entries: The crystalline servitor is resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The crystalline servitor has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The crystalline servitor’s weapon attacks are magical.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The crystalline servitor makes three Icicle attacks.

action.name: Icicle
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) cold damage.

action.name: Hailstorm (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The crystalline servitor calls down hail in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point on the ground it can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 DEX save, taking 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and 14 (4d6) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute or until the servitor uses this action again.

reaction.name: Snow Flurry
entries: When a creature the crystalline servitor can see within 120 feet of it deals damage to it, the servitor can send a flurry of snow at the creature. That creature must succeed on a DC 17 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) cold damage. 83 C C

trait.name: Grafted Arm
entries: The necrograft cultist has one of the following arms grafted in place of its original arm, affecting its Multiattack action: • Ghoul Arm. The target is paralyzed until the end of its next turn. In addition, the cultist is resistant to the paralyzed condition. • Wight Arm. The target’s HP maximum is reduced by 5 (2d4). This reduction lasts until the target finishes a short or long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0. In addition, the cultist gains the Parry reaction (included in Reactions). • Zombie Arm. The target is poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. In addition, the cultist’s HP total is 95 instead of 85. 331 Grafted Organs. The necrograft cultist has grafted Undead organs into its body. It has either darkvision out to 60 feet or keensense out to 30 feet, and it has one of the following: • Deathly Mettle. The cultist is immune to exhaustion and to the charmed and frightened conditions. • Magic Resistance. The cultist has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects. • Undead Fortitude. If damage reduces the cultist to 0 HP, it must make a CON save with a DC equal to 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the cultist drops to 1 HP instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The necrograft cultist makes three Slam attacks or two Necrotic Bolt attacks. If two Slam attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or suffer an additional effect, as described in Grafted Arm.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Necrotic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack : +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.

reaction.name: Parry (Wight Arm Only)
entries: The necrograft cultist adds 2 to its

reaction.name: AC against one melee attack that would hit it
entries: To do so, the cultist must see the attacker and have a grafted wight arm.

trait.name: Demonic Poison
entries: A creature resistant to poison damage or the poisoned condition isn’t resistant to Darhask’s poison. A creature immune to poison damage or the poisoned condition is instead resistant to Darhask’s poison.

trait.name: Demonic Resilience
entries: Darhask is resistant to cold, fire, and lightning damage. In addition, he is immune to poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Darhask fails a save, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Lord of Spiders
entries: Darhask’s movement can never be reduced below its normal value while he is standing on or in contact with webbing. Darhask can communicate with spiders, scorpions, and other arachnids as if they shared a language.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Darhask has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: Darhask can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. 87 D D Web Walker. Darhask ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Darhask makes one Sting attack and four Claw attacks. He can replace two Claw attacks with Web Lash.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (4d6 + 7) slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 22 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Sting
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 22 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

action.name: Web Lash
entries: Darhask sends strands of webbing to wrap around up to three creatures he can see within 60 feet of him.

action.name: Each target must make a DC 22 DEX
entries: On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and is restrained. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t restrained. A creature, including the target, can take its action to free the restrained target by succeeding on a DC 22 STR check. A creature has advantage on this check if the restrained target has taken fire damage.

bonus.name: Eight Million Eyes
entries: Darhask perceives through the senses of a spider, scorpion, or other arachnid within 1,000 feet of it or through the senses of an arachnoth within 120 feet of it. While perceiving in this way, he is deaf and blind in regard to his own senses. Darhask can use this bonus action again to end this effect.

bonus.name: Venomous Manipulation
entries: Darhask manipulates the poison within a creature he can see within 120 feet of him that is poisoned and causes one of the following effects: • Envy. Envy boils up in the creature, blinding it. The target must succeed on a DC 22 CON save or be blinded while it’s poisoned. • Isolation. The creature is overcome with loneliness. The target must succeed on a DC 22 WIS save or be unable to receive help from others, including receiving healing or the effects of beneficial spells, while it’s poisoned. • Sloth. The poison in the creature’s body weighs it down. The target must succeed on a DC 22 STR save or its speed is halved while it’s poisoned.

legendary.name: Web Teleport
entries: Darhask dissolves into web and reforms in an unoccupied space he can see within 60 feet. This distance increases to 120 feet if the origin and destination locations are both on webbing.

legendary.name: What’s Yours is Mine
entries: Darhask pulls on the threads of webbing restraining up to two creatures he can see within 30 feet of him. Each target must succeed on a DC 22 DEX save or Darhask steals one item the target is wearing or carrying, provided the item weighs no more than 30 pounds and isn’t wrapped around or firmly attached to the target, such as armor. The item flies through the air on a thread of webbing into one of Darhask’s hands or lands in his space (Darhask’s choice).

legendary.name: Poisonous Webs (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Darhask causes the webs restraining up to two creatures he can see within 120 feet of him to drip with poison. Each target must make a DC 22 CON save, taking 22 (4d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Demon, Drenqatu The demon—a thickset, reptilian body covered in short, nasty - looking spikes—snarls and raises its barbed tail, dripping with venom.

legendary.name: Demonic Vanguard
entries: When cultists open a portal to the Void and call forth a horde of demons to destroy a world, the fearsome drenqatus are typically part of that vanguard. Like their allies, the golmana and wrack demons (see Monster Vault for both), these burly reptilian horrors dwell in the deepest reaches of the Abyss, where the Lower Planes and the Void blur into one. Dull-Witted Bruisers. Not renowned for being clever, drenqatus revel in mindless mayhem and destruction. Their bodies are covered in poisonous spikes, which they can launch in all directions, injuring friend and foe alike. The spikes then grow back rapidly, enabling the drenqatu to unleash the barrage again in mere moments. Those that fall to such attacks are quickly and eagerly consumed by the demon.

trait.name: Evasion
entries: If the deadeye giant is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a DEX save to take only half damage, the giant instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The giant is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition. G G 150 Phrenic Weapons. The deadeye giant’s weapon attacks are magical. When the giant hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 psychic damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Preserve the Pattern (100 HP or Fewer)
entries: When the deadeye giant fails a save or takes damage, it can reroll the save or force the damage dice to be rerolled, taking the new roll result or the original, whichever it prefers.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The deadeye giant makes two Spear attacks or three Psychic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Spear
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) piercing damage, or 18 (3d8 + 5) piercing damage if used with two hands, plus 18 (4d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Glimpse the Future
entries: The deadeye giant senses its future regarding one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must make a DC 17 WIS save. On a failure, the giant can choose for the target to have disadvantage on attack rolls against the giant, or the giant can choose to have advantage on attack rolls against the target. The effect lasts until the start of the giant’s next turn. Giant, Dolmen With a gesture, a wall of stone erupts from the ground, blocking a volley of arrows aimed at a giant in a furred mantle.

bonus.name: Mountainous People
entries: A hearty and clannish folk, dolmen giants build their communities in rough mountains and hilly badlands, near passes and high valleys. They charge tolls to cross these thoroughfares, preferring trade goods to coins or similar wealth. They especially enjoy fermented beverages, allowing entire caravans passage for relatively paltry amounts of ale or wine.

bonus.name: Hum of Stones
entries: Akin to druids, dolmen giants tend to live in harmony with the land, entwining their traditions with the thrum of power inherent in the stone and dirt. They call on the magic embedded within the land, singing it to the surface. Their deep, sonorous melodies move and shape the stone, creating teleportation circles, star-aligned dolmens for divination, various monuments that draw the power of ley lines or attract mythical creatures, and other structures related to divination and conjuration.

trait.name: Dizzying Display
entries: The colorful and chaotic display of thousands of flapping wings disorients creatures. A creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space is incapacitated until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Potent Poison
entries: Undead with resistance or immunity to poison damage or the poisoned condition can be affected by the swarm’s poison.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny butterfly. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions. D D 84

action.name: Bites
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. Hit: 28 (8d6) piercing damage, or 14 (4d6) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its HP or fewer. The target must make a DC 12 CON save. On a failure, it takes 10 (3d6) poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The decatrine is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Exceptional Hearing and Sight
entries: The decatrine’s Perception is 24 when perceiving by hearing or sight. Its many ears and eyes also prevent it from being surprised if it can see or hear.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The decatrine makes four Leg attacks. It can replace one Leg attack with one Bite attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 32 (4d12 + 6) piercing damage.

action.name: Leg
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Pinning Bone
entries: The decatrine launches a large bone spike from one of its legs at a creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 18 DEX save or be knocked prone and restrained by the bone spike. A creature, including the target, can take its action to remove the bone spike by succeeding on a DC 18 STR check. Alternatively, the bone spike can be attacked and destroyed (AC 15; HP 30; vulnerability to bludgeoning damage; immunity to poison and psychic damage). The decatrine can launch up to nine bone spurs. Its speed is reduced by 5 feet for each bone spur it has launched since its last long rest, and it regrows all launched bone spurs when it finishes a long rest.

reaction.name: Getaway Leap
entries: When a creature the decatrine can see targets it with an attack, the decatrine can leap up to a number of feet equal to 10 below its current walking speed to an unoccupied space it can see without provoking opportunity attacks. The attack fails if this puts the decatrine out of range of the attack. 85 D D Demon, Arachnoth The arachnid-like humanoid—with its many legs and stinger - tipped tail—vomits forth a spray of spiders and scorpions .

reaction.name: Servants of Darhask
entries: Arachnoths are arachnoid fiends that typically serve the Demon Lord of Spiders. They are often called on to serve mortals who make deals with their lord, though they are always “plucking at the strings” of such contracts—seeking weak points through which to slip their bindings.

reaction.name: Spider Demons
entries: An arachnoth resembles a humanoid but with a thick carapace. It has multiple eyes and claws, a tail like a scorpion, and several legs sprouting grotesquely from its torso. Like their lord, arachnoths can exert a level of control over arachnids, including seeing through their eyes and speaking through them.

reaction.name: Control and Conquer
entries: Though physically imposing, an arachnoth’s true threat is its ability to manipulate and even outright control others through use of its poison. Those under its thrall might not even realize they are acting in the creature’s interests, therefore sowing distrust and discord among even the most tightly knit groups.

trait.name: Gift of Foresight
entries: While the diviner is conscious and wearing no armor and wielding no shield, it adds its WIS modifier to its AC (included above).

trait.name: Intuition
entries: The diviner rolls two dice for initiative, taking the higher number. In addition, the diviner has advantage on WIS (Insight) checks.

trait.name: Phrenic Weapons
entries: The diviner uses its WIS modifier when calculating weapon attack rolls. When the diviner hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 2d6 psychic damage (included in the attack).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The diviner makes three Dagger attacks or two Psychic Bolt attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, different possible fates for the creature are briefly revealed, and attack rolls against it are made with advantage until the start of the diviner’s next turn.

action.name: Dagger
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) psychic damage.

action.name: Cast the Runes (3/Day)
entries: The diviner casts a divination ritual of 3rd circle or lower. Alternatively, it can expend all uses of this action to cast the divination spell. It uses WIS as its spellcasting ability.

bonus.name: Word of Warning
entries: The diviner sees a glimpse of the upcoming fate for a friendly creature it can see within 60 feet of it. If that creature can see or hear the diviner, it has advantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the diviner’s next turn.

reaction.name: Saw That Coming
entries: When the diviner makes a save or when a creature it can see within 60 feet of it attacks it, the diviner can have advantage on the save or impose disadvantage on the attacker’s attack roll.

trait.name: Earth Glide
entries: The giant can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the giant doesn’t disturb the material through which it moves.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The giant is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dolmen giant makes three Stone Club or Boulder attacks.

action.name: Stone Club
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 33 (5d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Boulder
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 32 (4d12 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Song of Stone
entries: The dolmen giant sings a short melody that calls to the land, creating one of the following effects: • Deep Thrum. A 20-foot-radius patch of ground centered on a point the giant can see within 60 feet of it becomes difficult terrain until the start of the giant’s next turn. Its speed isn’t reduced when moving through this area. • Rumbling Vibrato. Rocks and soil climb up the giant’s legs, covering it. Until the start of the giant’s next turn, the giant is vulnerable to thunder damage, and all damage it takes is halved, except for thunder. • Sudden Crescendo. A pillar of stone bursts from the ground beneath one creature the giant can see within 60 feet of it, throwing the creature up to 60 feet in a random direction and knocking it prone. If a thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 18 DEX save or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

reaction.name: Stone’s Protection
entries: When a creature the dolmen giant can see within 60 feet of it, which can include itself, is attacked while on the ground, the giant can shout for the earth to protect the creature. A thin barrier of stone bursts out of the ground along one side of the target’s space, giving it three-quarters cover along that side, including against the triggering attack, until the start of the giant’s next turn. 151 G G Giant, Fire Giant Commander The giant’s long, flowing hair matches the flames that crackle along the blade of their sword. Standing imperiously, they issue commands to other giants nearby, who obey swiftly and without question.

reaction.name: Tested Leader
entries: A fire giant commander is often leading a force of fire giant raiders or overseeing the garrison of a mighty fortress. Chosen for their skill in battle, tactical prowess, and unmatched might, a fire giant commander is feared and respected by their troops, who in turn benefit from the commander’s presence and experience.

reaction.name: Mighty Warriors
entries: Fire giant commanders are chosen from the ranks based on their victories, might, and talent. Their innate, fiery power allows them to easily dominate average foes, setting them alight with burning blades and launching exploding boulders behind enemy lines.

monster.name: Doomwing
languages: understands Common but can’t speak except

trait.name: Armor-Piercing Beak
entries: When the doomwing makes a Beak attack against a creature wearing armor that is primarily made of metal, it has advantage on the attack roll.

trait.name: Heightened Hearing and Sight
entries: The doomwing’s Perception is 20 when perceiving by hearing or sight.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The doomwing can mimic Humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 15 WIS (Insight) check.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The doomwing’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The doomwing is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The doomwing makes three Beak attacks or four Bladed Feather attacks.

action.name: Beak
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or suffer a bleeding wound. A creature with a bleeding wound loses 5 (2d4) HP at the start of each of its turns. Any creature can take an action to stanch the wound with a successful DC 15 WIS (Medicine) check. The wound also closes if the target receives magical healing.

action.name: Bladed Feather
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Feather Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The doomwing sprays bladed feathers in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 27 (6d8) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Steel Mockery
entries: The doomwing chatters at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it in a mimicked, mocking voice. The target must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the doomwing’s next turn.

reaction.name: Wing Bash
entries: When a creature the doomwing sees misses it with an attack while within 10 feet of it, the doomwing can bash the attacker with its wings. The attacker must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be stunned until the start of the doomwing’s next turn. 101 D D Dragon, Adamantine The dark-gray metal scales of this dragon seem to absorb the light. It shifts ponderously under the weight of its great bulk, and the surrounding area shows the significant wear of the creature’s activity—cracked stone and impacted earth, shredded tree trunks, and dug out hollows.

reaction.name: Ponderous Philosophers
entries: Slow, deep thinkers, adamantine dragons spend much of their time contemplating the mysteries of the world and beyond. They enjoy philosophical discussions with visitors, whether those they invite or unexpected intruders. Confident in their near imperviousness, they often dismiss or ignore opening attacks, instead inviting trespassers to sit and discuss ephemeral matters. They tend to be slow and deliberate in their speech, presenting their thoughts with care. And they can be remarkably patient with the boorish.

reaction.name: Untidy Lairs
entries: Since adamantine dragons spend much of their time deep in their thoughts, they’re not very tidy with their lairs, typically found deep in mountains rich with metal ore. They leave the books and letters they have accumulated over the years, decades, centuries, scattered haphazardly, and they assure themselves they know exactly where everything sits, but visitors can attest to waiting extraordinary lengths of time for the dragon to retrieve some particular thing. The dragons also often pace while ruminating, even creating ruts around their lairs and inadvertently undercutting and destabilizing the walls. Luckily, they are large and tough enough to avoid serious danger from any resulting tunnel collapses. Adamantine scales also occasionally slough during their day-to-day activities, making their lairs even more of a treasure trove for those who can work the metal into armor and weapons. The dragons seem to take no mind if guests take these—or otherwise clean up after them.

reaction.name: Metal Collectors
entries: Adamantine dragons are fascinated by objects crafted purely from metal. This includes coins, but they especially value well-crafted weapons, armor, and art, especially statues. Metal treasures enjoy protection from corrosion while in an adamantine dragon’s lair, and subtle details of the items become more noticeable. The dragons often commission pieces from renowned artists and crafters, generously compensating them with a preponderance of non - metallic treasures.

reaction.name: Maturing
entries: Young adamantine dragons are impatient and take little interest in the pontificating of their elders. However, they are eager to learn from experience and travel extensively. This is also when they can jumpstart their lifelong accumulation of metallic treasures. As they age, they settle down into their increasingly contemplative tendencies, occasionally returning to their families to share in their gathered tales but definitely starting the search for some ore-laden lair they can claim. Ancient D D 102 adamantine dragons spend most of their time in their lairs, lost in thought. When they hear especially enticing news on something they have a special interest in, however, they will travel to learn all they can—and perhaps argue the finer points with those involved. AN ADAMANTINE DRAGON’S LAIR An adamantine dragon typically lairs in ore-laden mountains, carving their home deep within the rock. Part of their diet consists of these ores, which they often idly gnaw on for days while deep in thought. Expansive caverns and twisting tunnels, occasionally collapsed, make up the dragon’s lair. Much of their hoard is just scattered throughout, but the most valued metalworks are typically found near where they rest, serving as a focus for contemplating the mysteries of the universe. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Bolster. Skin or armor toughens for up to three creatures the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. Each target gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until the dragon uses this lair action again, or until the dragon dies. • Cloud of Shavings. A 20-foot-radius swirl of adamantine slivers rises up centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 9 (2d8) piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. • Tunnel Collapse. The ground splits open centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it, creating a pit. The pit is either a circular hole with a 10-foot radius or a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide.

reaction.name: Regardless of its shape, the pit is 20 feet deep
entries: Each creature in the pit’s area when it appears must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or fall into the pit, taking falling damage. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region containing an adamantine dragon’s lair is warped by its magic, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Hardened Hearts. Creatures residing at least 7 days within 10 miles of the dragon’s lair slowly adopt a more pragmatic view of the world. Any CHA (Deception or Persuasion) check made against such a creature has disadvantage. • Sturdy Structures. Each structure within 3 miles of the dragon’s lair increases its damage threshold by 5. • Untarnished Metal. Within 1 mile of the dragon’s lair, metal takes on an uncanny resilience and can’t be affected by normal or magical rusting. Metal that has rusted returns to its original state after being in this area for 1 day. If the dragon dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Demonic Resilience
entries: The drenqatu is resistant to cold, fire, and lightning damage. In addition, it is immune to poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The drenqatu has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Spiky Skin
entries: A creature that hits the drenqatu with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage. A creature that starts its turn grappling or grappled by the drenqatu takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The drenqatu makes two Claw attacks and one Tail attack. If both Claw attacks hit a Medium or smaller creature, the target is grappled (escape DC 17). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the drenqatu can’t make Claw attacks against other targets.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 17 CON save, taking 10 (4d4) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Hail of Spikes (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The drenqatu launches a hail of spikes from its body. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 17 DEX save, taking 15 (6d4) piercing damage and 20 (8d4) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Toxic Hug
entries: The drenqatu hugs one creature it is grappling, impaling the target on its poisonous spikes. The target must make a DC 17 CON save, taking 5 (2d4) piercing damage and 5 (2d4) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

reaction.name: Opportune Feast
entries: When a creature is reduced to 0 HP by the drenqatu’s Hail of Spikes, Spiky Skin, or Toxic Hug, the drenqatu can move up to its speed toward the creature without provoking opportunity attacks. If this movement brings it to within 5 feet of the creature, it feasts on the body. The drenqatu regains HP equal to the creature’s CR or level, and the creature has disadvantage on the next death save it makes, if it is making death saves. 89 D D Demon, Drouk The goat-legged humanoid raises their mug, offering up the sloshing ale. Their boisterous laughter seems tinged with malice.

reaction.name: Demon Drink
entries: These demons are entities of revelry given fiendish form. Drouks are the embodiment of the evils of excess, especially alcohol. Their presence—whether at a large celebration or just a quiet night at a tavern—ensures chaos and violence will erupt. While tempting those espousing temperance is always pleasing to a drouk, they take special glee in bringing the sober back to the bottle.

reaction.name: Ghost Friends
entries: The revelries spurred by drouks mark the celebrants’ souls, which are then later collected upon death. Occasionally, a creature overindulges and dies during the revelry, becoming then a celebrant shade (also in this book) instead of being marked. Drouks have an uncharacteristic softness for celebrant shades and are occasionally found partying alongside them.

reaction.name: Satyr Rivals
entries: While drouks bear some resemblance to satyrs—in both appearance and drive—they aren’t related. However, this has led to a sort of rivalry where each might take an opportunity to disrupt the festivities of the other.

trait.name: Cursed Drink
entries: With a 1-minute ritual, the drouk can curse all alcoholic beverages within a 20-foot radius of it, up to a maximum of 20 gallons. A creature that imbibes a glass or mug of the cursed alcohol must succeed on a

trait.name: DC 13 CON save or be poisoned for 1 hour
entries: If a creature continues to imbibe glasses or mugs of the cursed alcohol, it must repeat the save with each glass, increasing the DC by 2 for each additional drink consumed. While poisoned by the cursed alcohol, a creature falls prone if it tries to move more than half its speed during its turn.

trait.name: Demonic Resilience
entries: The drouk is resistant to cold, fire, and lightning damage. In addition, it is immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The drouk has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects. D D 90

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The drouk makes two Fist attacks.

action.name: Fist
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The drouk breathes fire in a 15 - foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 DEX save, taking 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Change Shape
entries: The drouk magically transforms into a Medium or Small Humanoid, or back into its true form, which is a Fiend. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying transforms with it. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

bonus.name: Unwitting Urge
entries: The drouk telepathically implants a subtle urge into the mind of a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. This urge must be in the form of a simple action that can be performed in 1 action or less. For example, the drouk could instill the urge to insult a fellow taverngoer, dump a drink on someone’s head, or steal an item. The target must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be compelled to act upon this urge. A creature poisoned from drinking cursed alcohol has disadvantage on the save. Demon, Icerift The icy blue figure pulls a large shard of ice from its body and throws it, impaling a rabbit in the snow. It pulls and readies another shard.

bonus.name: Cold-Bodied
entries: Icerift demons manifest as jagged, icy humanoids with angry features lined with icicles. Their bodies are the deep blue of compacted glacier ice, dusted with a crust of snow and studded with blue-white spikes. These creatures of the Abyss are often found in the coldest reaches of the Material Plane.

bonus.name: A Dish Best Served
entries: Icerift demons can create small chasms filled with ice and withdraw spears of ice from their flesh. Those wounded by such demons often suffer a terrible, lingering hunger that taints the souls of those that die from it.

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: The drow is resistant to the charmed condition, and magic can’t put the drow to sleep.

trait.name: Poisoned Weapons
entries: The drow’s weapons are magical. When the drow hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 2d8 poison damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its Perception is 11 when perceiving by sight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The drow mystic makes two Poisoned Dagger or Poison Bolt attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Poisoned Dagger
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage. E E 124 Poison Bolt. Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) poison damage.

action.name: Venomous Barbs (Recharge 5–6)
entries: Insectoid stingers erupt from the drow mystic. Each creature within 10 feet of the mystic must make a DC 14 CON save. On a failed save, a creature takes 27 (6d8) poison damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. While poisoned, a creature is frightened of the drow. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The drow casts one of the following spells, using WIS as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14). At will: guidance , light , thaumaturgy 3/day each: bless , command , cure wounds , spider climb 2/day each: alter self , calm emotions , web 1/day each: bestow curse , fear

reaction.name: Reactive Exoskeleton
entries: When a creature the drow mystic can see hits it with an attack, the mystic can call on the power of its insectoid deity to briefly cover it in an exoskeleton, reducing the damage taken by 7 (2d6). Elf, Shadow Fey Confidante

reaction.name: The courtier sighs as the assassin draws a dagger
entries: A flick of the wrist sends the bladed edge of their fan across the assassin’s throat.

reaction.name: Ambitious Advisors
entries: The courts of the shadow fey are no place for the weak of heart. Confidantes haunt the parlors, throne rooms, and bedchambers of the court, making deals, offering advice, and occasionally cutting down those who would stand in their way.

reaction.name: Unpredictable Chatelaines
entries: Each confidante keeps a chatelaine—a piece of jewelry comprised of a series of fine chains, each linked to a charm. Each of the charms can be imbued with unique properties, ensuring the confidante is prepared for a wide variety of situations.

trait.name: Duergar Resilience
entries: The duergar is resistant to the charmed and paralyzed conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells and illusions.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The duergar warformer’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its Perception is 6 when perceiving by sight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The warformer makes two Staff or Acid Bolt attacks.

action.name: Staff
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands, plus 7 (2d6) acid damage.

action.name: Acid Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) acid damage. D D 122 Invisibility. The duergar warformer magically turns invisible until it attacks or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment the warformer wears or carries is invisible with it.

bonus.name: Enhancing Transformation
entries: The duergar warformer enhances one or more nearby friendly duergar, which can include the warformer, in one of the following ways: • Augment Growth. One enlarged duergar the warformer can see within 30 feet of it becomes Huge instead of Large and triples its damage dice on weapon attacks. This effect lasts until the target uses Reduce, the target dies, the warformer dies, or the target starts its turn more than 60 feet away from the warformer. • Enduring Invisibility. Up to four duergar within 30 feet of the warformer have enhanced invisibility. Until the start of the warformer’s next turn, attacking doesn’t end Invisibility. • Forced March. Up to four duergar within 30 feet of the warformer have enhanced speed, increasing each target’s speed by 10 feet until the start of the warformer’s next turn. • Swift Assault. Up to two duergar the warformer can see within 30 feet of it have enhanced attacks. Each target can make one extra attack on its next turn.

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: As the fractidron.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: As the fractidron .

trait.name: Separate
entries: If the duodekadron takes lightning damage, it must succeed on a DC 20 CON save or separate into 12 dupladrons , each appearing in an unoccupied space within the duodekadron’s space or a space within 5 feet of it. The duodekadron’s remaining HP is split between the dupladrons and any conditions affecting it affect one random dupladron. To reform, each of the 12 dupladrons must be within 5 feet of one of the other dupladrons and use an action on its turn to reconnect back into a duodekadron.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: As the fractidron .

trait.name: Unerring Mind
entries: The duodekadron can perfectly recall information any of its component dupladrons have seen or heard in the past 90 days.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The duodekadron makes four Melee Armament or Eye Beam attacks.

action.name: Melee Armament
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (6d6 + 5) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the duodekadron’s choice).

action.name: Eye Beam
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (5d8 + 4) force damage. M M 202 Cutting Beam (Recharge 5–6). The duodekadron shoots brilliant energy in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 18 DEX save, taking 58 (13d8) force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Nonmagical objects that aren’t being worn or carried are destroyed by the beam.

bonus.name: Tractor Beam
entries: One creature the duodekadron can see within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 18 STR save or be pulled up to 25 feet into an unoccupied space of the duodekadron’s choice within 5 feet of it.

reaction.name: Repulsor Beam
entries: When a creature the duodekadron can see deals damage to it while within 10 feet of it, the duodekadron can release a repulsor beam. The target must succeed on a DC 18 STR save or be pushed up to 20 feet away from the duodekadron and be knocked prone.

trait.name: Dust Camouflage
entries: The dustcloak’s Stealth is 19 while in dusty, foggy, or cloudy conditions.

trait.name: Dust Form
entries: The dustcloak can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing, and the dustcloak can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn, that creature must make a DC 16 CON save. On a failure, it takes 5 (1d10) bludgeoning damage and is blinded for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half the damage and isn’t blinded. A blinded creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Elemental Nature
entries: The elemental doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: The elemental is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dustcloak makes one Bite attack and two Tail Whip attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (4d8 + 5) piercing damage.

action.name: Tail Whip
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Dust Burst (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The dustcloak expels a choking dust cloud around it. Each creature within 10 feet of it must make a DC 16 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and 21 (6d6) slashing damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The dust cloud remains for 1 minute or until the dustcloak’s concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). The dust cloud’s area is heavily obscured.

bonus.name: Scouring Dash (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The dustcloak moves up to 20 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Large or smaller creature without provoking opportunity attacks. Each creature the dustcloak passed through must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or take 7 (2d6) slashing damage and be knocked prone. 121 D D Dwarf, Duergar Warformer The grizzled, gray-skinned dwarf raises a stout staff, gesturing at their companions and speaking harsh words of power.

bonus.name: Squad Leader
entries: The warformer is an unusual duergar: they have forgone all but the most basic martial training to hone their natural magical abilities, focusing on transmutation magic at the expense of being able to enlarge themselves. They use such magic to help repair tools, enhance construction, and otherwise improve the quality of goods and fortifications in duergar communities. On patrol or in combat, they use their magic to enhance the fighting potential of their allies.

bonus.name: Transformative Adept
entries: Warformers can be dangerous foes individually, but they are most effective when leading and supporting a group. With a warformer at their backs, a duergar force’s martial prowess and natural magical abilities are enhanced, giving them a greater chance of overcoming foes.

monster.name: Eldritch Ooze
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Magic Affinity
entries: The ooze can absorb power from magic damage it takes, gaining an affinity for the magic. Whenever the ooze takes cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, or thunder damage, it gains an affinity for that damage type for 1 hour or until it takes another one of these damage types. While it has this affinity, it is immune to that type of damage.

trait.name: Ooze Nature
entries: The ooze doesn’t require sleep.

trait.name: Ooze Resilience
entries: The ooze is resistant to the grappled and restrained conditions, and it is immune to exhaustion and to the blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, and prone conditions.

trait.name: Sense Magic
entries: The ooze senses and can pinpoint the location of magic within 60 feet of it. If it senses magic and can see the creature or object bearing the magic it senses, it sees a faint aura around that creature or object.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The ooze can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The eldritch ooze makes two Pseudopod attacks or three Magic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) acid damage or damage of the type noted in the Magic Affinity trait.

action.name: Magic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) damage of the type noted in the Magic Affinity trait.

reaction.name: Magical Backlash
entries: When a creature the ooze can see within 30 feet of the ooze attacks it while it has an affinity to magic, the ooze can cause a magical backlash, flaring radiance, splashing poison, or similar. The attacker must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or take 4 (1d8) damage of the type noted in the Magic Affinity trait and suffer an effect based on that affinity: cold (speed is halved), fire (deal only half damage with attacks that use STR or DEX), lightning (incapacitated), necrotic (have disadvantage on saves), poison (poisoned), radiant (blinded), or thunder (deafened). The effect lasts until the end of the attacker’s next turn. 227 O O Ooze, Glass Light seems suspended within the thick liquid mass, studded with small crystalline formations. Droplets of the liquid harden to razor shards as they are flung from the surging ooze.

reaction.name: Two-State Oozes
entries: Glass oozes are able to paradoxically act as both liquid and solid. While they can easily shift their form to completely exist as one or the other, they seem to prefer the duality, though the rapid shift is useful when ambushing prey. Drawn to the Light. Though they are as mindless as other oozes, glass oozes display the barest vestiges of personality. They eschew dark places and seek out sources of illumination where they can best display their artful, ever-shifting bodies. The brighter a space is, the more the ooze stretches out, creating gemlike, faceted pseudopods ending in blades, lenses, or fans. They sometimes spend hours seemingly enjoying their own artifice, creating ever finer and more intricate webs of glass and ignoring everything that doesn’t actively threaten them.

trait.name: Heightened Hearing and Smell
entries: The eldritch sable’s Perception is 19 when perceiving by hearing or smell.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The eldritch sable is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition. ELDRITCH SABLE FAMILIARS Some eldritch sables are willing to serve spellcasters as familiars, especially spellcasters that practice more esoteric arts. Such eldritch sables have the following trait.

trait.name: Familiar
entries: The eldritch sable can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the eldritch sable senses

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage. Instead of dealing damage, the eldritch sable can steal one item the target is wearing or carrying, provided the item weighs no more than 10 pounds, isn’t a weapon, and isn’t wrapped around or firmly attached to the target. For example, a sable could steal a hat or belt pouch but not a creature’s shirt or armor.

bonus.name: Steal Luck
entries: The eldritch sable flicks its bushy tail and attempts to steal the luck of one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or have disadvantage on the next ability check, attack roll, or save (eldritch sable’s choice) it makes before the end of its next turn. If the target fails the save, the eldritch sable has advantage on one attack roll or save it makes before the start of its next turn.

reaction.name: Defensive Roll
entries: The eldritch sable adds 2 to its AC against one attack that would hit it. To do so, the eldritch sable must see the attacker and not be grappled, restrained, or otherwise unable to move. as long as they are within 1 mile of each other, and the companion’s maximum Luck is increased by 1. While the eldritch sable is within 10 feet of its companion, the sable can grant advantage to its companion instead of itself when it successfully uses Steal Luck. At any time and for any reason, the eldritch sable can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond. 123 E E Elf, Drow Mystic Powerful winds seem to whip at the elf ’s robes as they gather power in their outstretched hands.

reaction.name: Spiritual Leaders
entries: Ever since the drow separation from the surface-dwelling elves, they have formed their own societies, mirroring the collectivist nature of the insects they revere. They are spiritually guided by their mystics, who reinforce a carefully ordered and hierarchical existence and encourage them to embrace their place in the grand design. Each creature in a hive has its duties, from the queen to the common worker, and without their seamless cooperation, the whole hive would perish.

reaction.name: Holy Power
entries: Drow mystics have a connection with their chosen deity that allows them to channel divine powers to protect, heal, and defend their congregations and to coat their weapons in a magical poison. They wield that power against threats from without, but zealous mystics have no qualms with turning their gaze on threats from within. Such mystics that get any hint of rebellion quickly eliminate such threats to preserve the stability of the community.

monster.name: Empty Soul
languages: the languages it knew in life

trait.name: Detect Arcana
entries: The empty soul can pinpoint the location of any creature within 60 feet of it that has cast a spell within the last hour.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The empty soul can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The empty soul doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The empty soul is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The empty soul makes two Draining Touch or Arcane Shriek attacks. E E 126 Draining Touch. Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) necrotic damage plus 21 (6d6) force damage. If the target is a spellcaster, it must succeed on a DC 18 CON save or lose a spell slot of the highest circle it currently has available.

action.name: Arcane Shriek
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +10 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (6d6 + 5) force damage plus 22 (5d8) thunder damage.

action.name: Arcane Burst (Special)
entries: The empty soul erupts with energy in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 CON save, taking 49 (14d6) force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. When a creature fails the save against the empty soul’s Draining Touch, this action recharges.

bonus.name: Haunting Step
entries: The empty soul teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature within 5 feet of the origin and destination spaces must succeed on a DC 18 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Leech Magic
entries: When a creature the empty soul can see within 60 feet of it casts a spell, the empty soul can choose to benefit from the spell as if it was an additional target, provided it is within the spell’s range. The empty soul doesn’t count against the maximum number of targets of the spell. Ettercap, Spellweaver Four additional spider legs sprout from this arachnid humanoid’s torso, and its mandibles drip a foul ichor. It wears a glyph- studded ceremonial robe and wields a gnarled staff of bone and crystal.

reaction.name: Arcane Arachnids
entries: Some ettercaps experiment with the arcane, seeking to enhance their natural abilities. These spellweavers conduct dark rituals on prisoners and other creatures, deep in the caves dotting their territories of ancient forest—the goals of which are known only to themselves. Any sizable ettercap raiding party often has at least one spellweaver among them.

trait.name: Celestial Resilience
entries: The naga is resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The naga has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Radiant Strikes
entries: The naga’s weapon attacks are magical. When the naga hits with any weapon attack, the weapon deals an extra 3d8 radiant damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Rejuvenation
entries: If it dies, the naga returns to life in 1d6 days, regaining all its HP and becoming active again. Only a wish spell can prevent this trait from functioning.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The enlightened naga makes four Slam or Radiant Bolt attacks, or it makes one Constrict attack and three Slam attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Constrict
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target . Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) radiant damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 17) if it is a Large or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the naga can’t Constrict another target.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) radiant damage.

action.name: Radiant Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) radiant damage.

action.name: Thousand-Fist Strike (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The enlightened naga lashes out with spectral hands. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 17 CON save, taking 22 (5d8) bludgeoning damage and 22 (5d8) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The enlightened naga casts one of the following spells, requiring only verbal components and using WIS as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17). At will: guidance , thaumaturgy 3/day each: bless , command 2/day each: hold , remove curse 1/day: death ward

bonus.name: Protective Teacher
entries: The naga magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a friendly creature it can see. Damage dealt to that creature is reduced by 9 (2d8) until the start of the naga’s next turn.

reaction.name: Deflection
entries: The naga adds 5 to its AC against one attack that would hit it. To do so, the naga must see the attacker and have at least one hand empty. 215 N N Naga, Sea The creature has the serpentine lower half of a sea snake, banded in white and blue, while its top half is that of a scaled humanoid. A crown of coral sits atop its head.

reaction.name: Sea Guardians
entries: Sea nagas guard sunken ruins and the tombs and prisons of forgotten terrors deep beneath the waves. They are more solitary than their terrestrial kin— few can reach their watery abodes—and spend their time deep in prophetic fervor. Of those rare intruders, it often demands they prove themselves in combat, regardless of their motives.

reaction.name: Demanding Saviors
entries: When an unnatural storm or monster sinks a ship, a sea naga might appear to a survivor, offering to save as many souls as they wish. Once complete, it demands that survivor complete a task for each soul saved. These are generally heroic feats related to some prophecy or danger known only to the naga.

monster.name: Eye Coral
senses: keensense 30 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The coral can breathe both air and water.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The coral is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Poison Secretions
entries: A creature that touches the coral or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) poison damage.

action.name: Tendril
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) poison damage. E E 128 Eye Burst. While the eye coral is not submerged, it can cause one of its eye growths to burst in a shower of poison. Each creature within 5 feet of the coral must make a DC 12 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 5 (2d4) poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned.

action.name: Eye Jet
entries: While the eye coral is underwater, it can emit a burst of sonic energy from one of its eyes in a line that is 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 12 DEX save. A creature without a swimming speed has disadvantage on this save. On a failure, a creature takes 5 (2d4) thunder damage and, if it is underwater, is pushed 10 feet away from the eye coral. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed.

reaction.name: Poison Flood (Recharge 6)
entries: When the eye coral takes damage while underwater, it can secrete a 10-foot-radius cloud of poison into the water around it. The area is lightly obscured, and the cloud remains for 1 minute. A creature that enters the cloud’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 12 CON save or be poisoned until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The facefetch is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Reflection Dissonance
entries: If the facefetch sees its reflection while wearing another creature’s face, it must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or take 7 (2d6) psychic damage and lose its current face, immediately ending the effects of Wear Face. On a success, it doesn’t need to make this save again until it sees its reflection while wearing a different face.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The facefetch makes three Slam or Psychic Assault attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target.

action.name: Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage
entries: This attack deals slashing damage instead when the facefetch isn’t transformed.

action.name: Psychic Assault
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Steal Face
entries: The facefetch magically steals the face of a

bonus.name: Medium or smaller Humanoid it can see within 30 feet
entries: That creature must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or lose its face, retaining only smooth, featureless skin where its face once was. The facefetch can then immediately use Wear Skin to wear that creature’s face. A creature without a face is blinded, deafened, and can’t speak. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, regaining its face on a success. The creature also regains its face if the facefetch dies, if the facefetch uses this bonus action on another creature, or if the facefetch dismisses or otherwise loses the face. If the target dies while its face is stolen, the facefetch can keep the face for up to 3 days before the face crumbles.

bonus.name: Wear Face
entries: The facefetch puts on a face it has stolen and magically transforms into that person. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying transforms with it or is borne by the new form (the facefetch’s choice). It reverts to its true form if it dies. While transformed, the facefetch knows any language that creature knew, and each ally of that creature has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes against the facefetch each round.

bonus.name: It can use this bonus action to end this effect
entries: If this effect ends while the creature with the stolen face is still alive, the stolen face is destroyed. 129 F F

monster.name: Fen Lurcher
