languages: understands Deep Speech but can’t speak

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The fen lurcher is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The fen lurcher can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Limited Telepathy
entries: The fen lurcher can magically transmit simple ideas, emotions, and images telepathically to any creature within 120 feet of it that can understand a language. This telepathy extends to 1 mile when transmitting to other fen lurchers. Unlike standard telepathy, the target of the transmission can’t telepathically respond.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fen lurcher makes one Corruptive Bite attack and two Psychic Claw attacks, or it makes three Psychic Bolt attacks. If both Psychic Claw attacks hit one creature, the target’s speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Corruptive Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or contract a disease. Until the disease is cured, the infected creature F F 130 is poisoned, and the fen lurcher can sense the creature’s direction while within 1 mile of it. Every 24 hours that elapse, the infected creature must repeat the save, reducing its HP maximum by 5 (1d10) on a failure or recovering from the disease on a success. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. The creature dies if the disease reduces its HP maximum to 0. A creature that dies while infected rises as a fen lurcher 24 hours later.

action.name: Psychic Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing damage plus 5 (1d10) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Mental Onslaught
entries: The fen lurcher projects horrific images and sensations into the mind of one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 INT save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn as it reels from the projection.

bonus.name: Nightmare Step
entries: The fen lurcher magically teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a creature it can see. The target must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Heightened Hearing and Smell
entries: The fenrosk’s Perception is 17 when perceiving by hearing or smell.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The fenrosk is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The fenrosk has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the fenrosk’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fenrosk makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target.

action.name: Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage
entries: If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be knocked prone.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.

bonus.name: Toppling Roll
entries: The fenrosk curls into a ball and rolls up to 20 feet in a straight line. It can move through the space of any Large or smaller creature without provoking opportunity attacks. The first time the fenrosk enters a creature’s space during this move, the creature must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be knocked prone.

reaction.name: Defensive Curl
entries: When a creature the fenrosk can see attacks it, the fenrosk can curl into a tight ball, increasing its AC by 2 until the start of its next turn, when it uncurls. 131 F F

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The fey chamberlain is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The fey chamberlain has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fey chamberlain makes three Chamberlain’s Staff attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting. F F 132 Chamberlain’s Staff. Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) force damage, and the fey chamberlain can choose for the target to be pushed up to 10 feet away from the chamberlain.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The fey chamberlain casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using INT as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15). At will: dancing lights , mage hand , minor illusion , prestidigitation 3/day each: faerie fire , mirror image , silent image 1/day each: major image , suggestion

bonus.name: Withering Look
entries: The fey chamberlain stares pointedly at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or be unable to speak until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Take Out the Trash (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The fey chamberlain wags a disapproving finger at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or be teleported to a spot on the ground within 500 feet the chamberlain can see, visualize, or describe by stating distance or direction.

reaction.name: Stinging Reprimand
entries: When a creature the fey chamberlain can see hits it with an attack, the chamberlain can admonish the attacker. The attacker must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or have disadvantage on the next ability check, attack roll, or save it makes before the start of the chamberlain’s next turn. Fey Lady, Selkolla The fey has a woman’s torso atop a seal’s tail— like a faerie mermaid. She raises her arms, and harsh, icy magic coalesces around her webbed fingers. Her jet-black eyes and razor teeth seem to reflect only malice. Lady of Selkies and Seals. Though considered a minor noble among the fey courts, Selkolla is an ancient and powerful fey who has claimed dominion over selkies and pinnipeds since time immemorial. She keeps court in a flooded cave in the northernmost of the selkies’ secluded isles, and she can occasionally be seen at high tide, beckoning selkies to the water. While in court, she accepts news and gifts from the myriad selkie tribes and organizes grand dances throughout the depths.

reaction.name: Cold and Vengeful
entries: Selkolla knows of every selkie who has had its sealskin stolen. The frequency of such thefts has left her cold and cruel toward mortals, and she views coastal settlements as an inherent threat to her people and their pinniped kin. To protect them, she leverages fearsome ice-storms or joins battle as a powerful seal. She rarely takes the time to discriminate between guilt and innocence when her vengeful wrath takes over.

reaction.name: Patron of the Dispossessed
entries: Selkolla has sympathy for those she views as isolated or dispossessed and often takes in abandoned children and orphans, whom she gifts sealskins and turns into selkies. These former humanoids are often the only ones who can calm her rage when she is on the warpath.

trait.name: Fey Blessed
entries: The feymount raccoon is resistant to the charmed condition and uses its WIS modifier when making saves against illusions or to discern an illusion for what it is.

trait.name: Heightened Hearing and Smell
entries: The feymount raccoon’s Perception is 17 while perceiving by hearing or smell.

trait.name: Woodland Walk
entries: Difficult terrain composed of nonmagical plants doesn’t cost the feymount raccoon extra movement. In addition, the raccoon can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The feymount raccoon makes one Bite attack and two Gore attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage Gore. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Intimidating Display
entries: The raccoon puffs up its fur, stamps its feet, and growls. Each creature within 15 feet of the raccoon that can see it must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn. The feymount raccoon doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks from creatures frightened of it. 323

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The hag is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The hag can mimic the buzzing and chirring of insects. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 15 WIS (Insight) check.

trait.name: Speak with Insects
entries: The hag can communicate with insects, spiders, and other insectoid Beasts as if they shared a language.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hag makes three Claw or Poison Thorn attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Claw (Hag Form Only)
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) slashing damage.

action.name: Poison Thorn (Hag Form Only)
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage. The target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. H H 172 Consuming Swarm (Recharge 5–6). The hag unleashes a cloud of voracious insects in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point it can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (4d4) piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) poison damage, and the insects devour up to 5 pounds of food worn or carried by the target and that isn’t in a magical container. On a success, a creature takes half the damage, and its food is unaffected.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The hag casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using CHA as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15). At will: druidcraft , entangle , fog cloud 1/day each: giant insect , plant growth

bonus.name: Change Shape
entries: The hag magically transforms into a Medium or smaller Beast, or back into its true form, which is Fey. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying transforms with it. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

reaction.name: Bug Bites
entries: When a creature the hag can see hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it, the hag can command insects to bite the attacker, dealing 5 (2d4) piercing damage to the attacker. Hag, Grave A wizened, gray-skinned woman’s face peers out beneath a load of bones piled high on her back. Her voice is both guttural and piercing, like steel dragged along stones. The carried skulls’ eye sockets seem to leer.

reaction.name: Torturous Sadists
entries: Grave hags subsist on the primal fear felt by creatures that know they are moments from death—also known as thanatophobia. Some hags lure victims into their cozy homes only to submit them to the death traps inside. Others subject their victims to agony in torture chambers. Others still wander fields of battle after the slaughter, looking for those soon to die and gorging on the palpable desperation.

reaction.name: False Chirurgeons
entries: Surprisingly well-versed in the treatment of injuries, grave hags often disguise themselves to take positions in hospitals, sanitoriums, and other places of healing. In these positions, they comport themselves well, treating minor injuries while supping on the fear rolling off the patients that are unlikely to survive. Similarly, some grave hags act as caregivers in communities wracked by plague, treating cuts and bruises while growing fat on the growing fear from the disease-ravaged residents.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The viletrap is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fiendish viletrap makes one Bite attack and one Root Whip attack, or it makes three Root Whip attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage.

action.name: Root Whip
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13) if it is a Medium or smaller creature. The fiendish viletrap can have up to two creatures grappled at a time.

action.name: Burning Nectar
entries: The fiendish viletrap whips its flowers, flinging globs of a viscous, burning liquid at up to two creatures it can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature must make a DC 13 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) fire damage and the glob sticks to it. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and the glob doesn’t stick to it. A creature with a glob stuck to it takes 4 (1d8) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature, including the target, can use its action to scrape off the glob, ending the effect.

bonus.name: Chomp
entries: The fiendish viletrap wraps its leafy mouth around a creature it is grappling, and the grapple ends. While inside the viletrap’s mouth, the target is restrained, it has three - quarters cover against attacks and other effects outside the mouth, and it takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the viletrap’s turns. The viletrap can have only one creature wrapped in its mouth at a time, and while trapping a creature in this way, the viletrap can’t make Bite attacks. A creature, including the target, can take its action to free the target from the mouth by succeeding on a DC 13 STR check.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The fiery phantom troll can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The fiery phantom troll regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. If the troll takes cold or radiant damage, this trait doesn’t function at the start of the troll’s next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 HP and doesn’t regenerate.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The fiery phantom troll doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The fiery phantom troll is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fiery phantom troll makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack, or it makes two Fire Bolt attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) necrotic damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) necrotic damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Fire Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) fire damage.

bonus.name: Horrifying Scream
entries: The fiery phantom troll screams in agony in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area that can hear the scream must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Fiery Retaliation
entries: When a creature the fiery phantom troll can see within 30 feet of it hits it with an attack, the troll can hurl fire at the attacker. The attacker must make a DC 13 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) fire damage. 291 T T Troll, Toadstool The troll is stooped to little more than half its height, as though the large fungi on its back is too heavy to bear. The creature breaks a smaller mushroom off one of its shoulders and munches on it.

reaction.name: Fungus Bearers
entries: Through some natural or magical means, toadstool trolls have developed a symbiotic relationship with mushrooms and other fungi. They grow mushrooms and shelf fungus all over their bodies, including a large toadstool from their back that serves to shade the troll from rain and sun. Where a toadstool troll’s blood falls on the ground, clusters of mushrooms are sure to grow, and when one of the trolls dies, its body decomposes into a hillock of fungus.

reaction.name: Trusting Allies
entries: Toadstool trolls have a reputation for friendliness and can often be found in the company of forest creatures, fey, and even other trolls. Though they are easier to get along with than their more mundane cousins, they retain their ferocity, and once angered, they are difficult to calm once again. A toadstool troll can be a lifesaving ally to those it trusts however, sharing the rejuvenating magic of its mushrooms.

monster.name: Fir Beast
languages: understands Common and Sylvan but can’t speak

trait.name: Charge
entries: If the fir beast moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Horn attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be knocked prone.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the fir beast remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal bush or shrub.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The fir beast is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Relentless (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: If the fir beast takes 15 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 HP, it is reduced to 1 HP instead.

trait.name: Rooted Stance
entries: The fir beast has advantage on checks and saves against being pushed or knocked prone.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fir beast makes one Needle Horns attack and one Root Stomp attack.

action.name: Needle Horns
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Root Stomp
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. one target. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target’s speed is halved until the end of its next turn, as roots cling to its legs.

bonus.name: Root Eruption
entries: The fir beast stomps its foot, causing roots and vegetation to erupt from the ground around it in a 20-foot radius. That area becomes difficult terrain for all creatures except the fir beast until the start of its next turn. 139 F F

trait.name: Familiar
entries: The fire cat can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the fire cat senses as long as they are within 1 mile of each other. While the fire cat is within 10 feet of its companion, the companion shares the fire cat’s Smokesight trait. At any time and for any reason, the fire cat can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond. F F 140 Heightened Smell. The fire cat’s Perception is 18 when perceiving by smell.

trait.name: Smokesight
entries: The fire cat can see through areas obscured by fire, fog, and smoke without penalty.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) fire damage, and the fire cat attaches to the target. While attached, the fire cat can use the Smoky Yowl bonus action and can make only Bite attacks. At the start of each of the fire cat’s turns, the target takes 5 (2d4) fire damage. The attached fire cat moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the fire cat’s movement. It can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement on its turn. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the fire cat by succeeding on a DC 12 STR check.

bonus.name: Smoky Yowl
entries: The fire cat exhales a puff of smoke in a short yowl. Each creature within 5 feet of the fire cat must succeed on a DC 12 CON save or choke on the smoke until the start of the fire cat’s next turn. While choking, a creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and can’t cast spells with verbal components. A creature that doesn’t need to breathe is immune to this effect. Flitkith A doll with painted and exaggerated features seems to turn its head toward some nearby movement or noise.

bonus.name: Childlike Fey
entries: Flitkith are tiny fey that resemble children’s toys. Like children, they express wonder at novel things and can be quite mischievous. This grants them a natural affinity with humanoid children, and flitkith might form attachments to certain children.

bonus.name: Fashionable Familiars
entries: In rare cases, flitkith form attachments to adults, acting as traveling companions . These flitkith providing crafting advice and often help their partners navigate tricky social situations.

bonus.name: Collectors
entries: The most common flitkith appear as cloth, metal, and wooden dolls and toys. They can come in other forms, such as folded-paper sculptures or porcelain dolls, but an individual’s form never seems to change. They are driven to hoard more of that material. A cloth flitkith, for example, might see gingham for the first time and feel compelled to cut a swatch of it for their collection.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The fire giant is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fire giant commander makes two Flaming Greatsword or Lava Boulder attacks.

action.name: Flaming Greatsword
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 29 (6d6 + 8) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage. If the target is a creature or a flammable object, it ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the target takes 4 (1d8) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

action.name: Lava Boulder
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage, and the boulder explodes. Each creature, other than the target, within 10 feet of the target must make a DC 17 DEX save, taking 9 (2d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Volcanic Burst (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The fire giant commander expels built-up heat from within itself, sending a blast of lava outward. Each creature within 15 feet of the fire giant must G G 152 make a DC 17 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 45 (10d8) fire damage and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knocked prone.

bonus.name: Issue Command
entries: The fire giant commander bellows one of the following tactical commands at up to three friendly creatures it can see within 60 feet of it: • Double Envelopment. Each target can immediately move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks and must move toward at least one enemy. It then has advantage on the next melee attack it makes before the start of the commander’s next turn. • Fortify. Until the start of the commander’s next turn, each target has disadvantage on attack rolls, and attack rolls against the targets have disadvantage. • Rally. Each target afflicted by an ongoing effect that allows for a repeated save to end the effect can immediately make a new save. • Saturating Boulders. The commander chooses a point it can see within 60 feet of it. Each target that makes a ranged attack at a creature within 15 feet of that point before the start of the commander’s next turn has advantage on that attack. Giant, Frost Giant Jarl The icy blue giant wields a massive axe, and its armor appears to be of ice. Its eyes glow with indomitable rage.

bonus.name: Frost Giant Commanders
entries: When frost giants join their clans together into an army, typically to face some great threat, one of the giants goes through a transformation, becoming more powerful and better able to lead the conjoined forces. The other frost giants tend to automatically defer to this jarl and unquestioningly follow their commands. If the giants are still in need of the army when their jarl dies, another will rise to take their place.

bonus.name: Retired Jarls
entries: Since frost giants prefer smaller clan groups, their armies are almost always ephemeral, typically lasting only long enough to complete their mission or avert the immediate threat. Once the army disbands, the jarl retains the power but has no place among their clan. They instead withdraw from society, becoming willing outcasts—loners that continue to stand against threats to their kin.

trait.name: Death Burst
entries: When the firedrop fungus dies, it explodes in a burst of steam. Each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 7 (2d6) fire damage.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the firedrop fungus remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal fungus.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The fungus is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Vent Steam
entries: The firedrop fungus sprays a 30-foot cone of steam. Each creature in that area must make a DC 13 CON save, taking 7 (2d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

reaction.name: Scalding Blast
entries: A creature that deals slashing damage to the firedrop fungus while within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn. F F 146

trait.name: Armor of Foresight
entries: While the first servant is wearing no armor and wielding no shield, it adds its WIS modifier to its AC (included above).

trait.name: Divine Blessing
entries: The first servant is resistant to necrotic damage or radiant damage, as appropriate for the servant’s deity.

trait.name: Divine Weapons
entries: The first servant’s weapon attacks are magical. When the first servant hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 necrotic or radiant damage (included in the attack), the first servant’s choice.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The first servant makes three Divine Burst attacks or one Blinding Rod attack and two Divine Burst attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Blinding Rod
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) necrotic or radiant damage (the first servant’s choice), and the target must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or be blinded and deafened until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Divine Burst
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack : +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (5d8 + 5) necrotic or radiant damage (the first servant’s choice).

action.name: Healing Touch (4/Day)
entries: The first servant touches another creature. The target magically regains 20 (4d8 + 2) HP and is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The first servant casts one of the following spells, using WIS as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At will: bane , command , protection from evil and good , thaumaturgy 3/day each: cure wounds (as a 5th-circle spell), dispel evil and good , speak with dead 1/day each: heal , holy aura

bonus.name: Inspire Awe
entries: The first servant channels divine energy through it toward up to three creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or be unable to use bonus actions or reactions until the start of the first servant’s next turn.

trait.name: Heated Weapons
entries: When the salamander hits with a metal melee weapon, the weapon deals an extra 7 (2d6) fire damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Super-Heated Body
entries: A creature that touches the salamander or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 3 (1d6) fire damage, and at the start of each of the salamander’s turns, flammable objects within 5 feet of it that aren’t being worn or carried ignite.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The salamander makes one Pronged Pike attack and two Tail attacks, or it makes four Fire Bolt attacks.

action.name: Pronged Pike
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage. If the target is wielding a weapon or shield, it must succeed on a DC 16 DEX save or drop the weapon or shield (the salamander’s choice if the target is wielding both).

action.name: Tail
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, the salamander can automatically hit the target with its tail, and the salamander can’t make Tail attacks against other targets.

action.name: Fire Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) fire damage.

action.name: Blazing Dash (Recharge 6)
entries: The flamescale salamander moves up to 30 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Large or smaller creature without provoking opportunity attacks, leaving a trail of fire in its wake. The first time it enters a creature’s space during this move, that creature must succeed on a DC 16 DEX save or take 28 (8d6) fire damage and be knocked prone. Each space along that line and within 5 feet of it catches fire until the end of the salamander’s next turn. A creature that enters a burning space for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 16 DEX save or take 10 (3d6) fire damage.

bonus.name: Call to Arms
entries: The flamescale salamander calls out to up to two Elementals it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target can gain advantage on the next melee weapon attack it makes before the start of the salamander’s next turn, or it can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks (the target’s choice). 257 S S

monster.name: Flock Caller
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but

trait.name: Corvid Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the flock caller to 0 HP and the damage isn’t radiant or from a critical hit, the flock caller is reduced to 1 HP instead, as long as at least one swarm of ravens is within 30 feet of it.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The flock caller doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The flock caller is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The flock caller makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

action.name: Summon Ravens (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The flock caller magically calls two swarms of ravens . The swarms appear in spaces the flock caller can see within 30 feet of it, act as allies of the flock caller, and obey its mental commands. The swarms act on the flock caller’s initiative, taking their turns immediately after the flock caller. The ravens remain for 1 hour, until the flock caller dies, or until the flock caller dismisses them as a bonus action. The flock caller can have up to four swarms of ravens under its control at one time.

bonus.name: Wheatfield Snare
entries: The flock caller sends entangling plants toward up to two creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be restrained by the plants until the start of the flock caller’s next turn. A creature, including the restrained target, can take its action to free the creature by succeeding on a DC 13 STR check.

reaction.name: Shield of Crows
entries: When a creature the flock caller can see hits it with an attack, the flock caller can call ravens to protect it, reducing the damage by 5 (2d4). 143 F F

monster.name: Flotsam Guardian
languages: understands the languages of its creator but can’t

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The guardian doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The guardian is immune to poison and psychic damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the guardian remains motionless and prone, it is indistinguishable from regular swamp debris.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The guardian has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects. F F 144

trait.name: Rooted Feet (Terrestrial Form Only)
entries: The guardian can’t be moved against its will and has advantage on saves to avoid being knocked prone.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The flotsam guardian makes two Bite attacks and one Kick or Paddle Wheel Thwomp attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Kick (Terrestrial Form Only)
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the flotsam guardian.

action.name: Paddle Wheel Thwomp (Aquatic Form Only)
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. Paddle Wheel Vortex (Recharge 5–6, Aquatic Form Only). Each creature within 20 feet of the flotsam guardian must make a DC 15 STR save. On a failure, a creature takes 24 (7d6) bludgeoning damage and is pulled up to 15 feet toward the flotsam guardian. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pulled. This action can be used only while the guardian is in or on the water.

bonus.name: Reconfigure
entries: The flotsam guardian shifts from its terrestrial form to its aquatic form or back.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The Forgotten Smith is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Flaming Weapons
entries: The Forgotten Smith’s weapon attacks are magical. When he hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 fire damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the Forgotten Smith fails a save, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The Forgotten Smith has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Forgotten Smith makes three Forge Maul or Molten Metal attacks. He can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Forge Maul
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) fire damage. If the target is wearing manufactured armor, the armor takes a permanent and cumulative −1 penalty to the AC it offers. Armor reduced to an AC of 10 is destroyed.

action.name: Molten Metal
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +12 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) fire damage.

action.name: Call Constructs
entries: The Forgotten Smith magically calls 2d6 flying swords , 1d4 animated armors , or 2 rugs of smothering . The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the Forgotten Smith and obeying its spoken commands. The Constructs remain for 1 hour, until the Forgotten Smith dies, or until the Forgotten Smith dismisses them as a bonus action. The Forgotten Smith can have any number of Constructs under its control at one time, provided the combined total CR of the Constructs is no higher than 7.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The Forgotten Smith casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using CHA as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 20). At will: detect thoughts , invisibility , mage hand , mending 3/day each: dispel magic , freedom of movement , slow

bonus.name: Exploit Flaw
entries: The Forgotten Smith magically senses and exploits a flaw in the armor worn by one creature he can see within 30 feet of him. The target’s AC is reduced by 1d4 until the start of the Forgotten Smith’s next turn. This effect can’t destroy the armor.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: The Forgotten Smith adds 6 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, he must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The Forgotten Smith automatically detects the presence of magic within 60 feet of him, pinpointing the current location of each item or effect.

legendary.name: Teleport
entries: The Forgotten Smith magically teleports, along with any equipment he is wearing or carrying, up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see.

legendary.name: Construct Support (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The Forgotten Smith uses Call Constructs.

legendary.name: Melt Equipment (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The Forgotten Smith causes manufactured metal weapons and armor wielded or worn by creatures within 15 feet of him to glow red-hot. Each affected creature must succeed on a DC 18 CON save or take 9 (2d8) fire damage and have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the Forgotten Smith’s next turn. 137 F F Fey Lord, Luminous Lord The tall fey lord—dark complexion and long, white hair—wears rich garments of white and gold and a rapier at his hip. Motes of golden light surround his head like a crown, and the hint of a smile pulls at his lips.

legendary.name: Willing Exile
entries: An oddity among the fey, the Luminous Lord holds honesty and truth in highest regard, and he opposes the use of trickery and illusion. He lives on the edges of fey society, far from its scheming courts, and is often viewed with disdain by those of the courts.

legendary.name: Radical Beliefs
entries: The Luminous Lord believes the illusion and transformation magics that saturate the faerie realms are unnecessary and hold the fey back from even greater heights. He has seen the Labyrinth and the dangers of the Void, and he feels his kith are too blinded by their schemes to see the threats that lie beyond the courts. He often gathers likeminded individuals to his side to hunt out such incursions into the mortal realms—for if the mortal realms fall, the faerie realms aren’t long behind.

legendary.name: Luminant Lancers
entries: The Luminous Lord’s most loyal followers are paladins known as the Luminant Lancers. They are pledged to his service and carry out his most important missions, often targeting Void incursions and doomsday cult activity.

trait.name: Dedicated Tunneler
entries: If the formicbane burrows at half its burrowing speed, it can leave a 5-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The formicbane has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the formicbane’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

trait.name: Spiked Mane
entries: A creature that touches the formicbane or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage. A creature that starts its turn grappling or grappled by the formicbane takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The formicbane makes two Mandible Scythe or Spit Acid attacks.

action.name: Mandible Scythe
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage.

action.name: Spit Acid
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (3d4 + 2) acid damage.

bonus.name: Tail Swipe
entries: The formicbane swipes its long tail at the feet of a creature it can see within 10 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or be knocked prone.

reaction.name: Distracting Spit
entries: When a hostile creature the formicbane can see within 20 feet of it attacks a friendly creature the formicbane can see, the formicbane can spit a short burst of acid toward the creature. The attacker must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or have disadvantage on the attack roll. 145 F F Fungi, Firedrop A field of cream-colored mushrooms stands in a warm, dank cavern. Upon approach, they suddenly swell to twice their size, wisps of steam rising from their bulbous caps.

reaction.name: Heat-Loving Fungus
entries: Firedrop fungi are commonly found in areas of volcanic activity, where the heat and ash can feed their growth cycles. Some dwarf and duergar settlements keep gardens of the fungus, growing it near their forges and similar sites. Mushroom tenders in these settlements are well-regarded and compensated for their dangerous job. The fungus is considered a delicacy among many subterranean cultures, but surface dwellers tend to find its sulfurous taste unpleasant.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The genie has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The genie’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Nebulous (Cloud Form Only)
entries: The genie’s Stealth is 21, can’t manipulate objects or attack, and it can pass through any space air can pass through without squeezing. In addition, it can enter and hide in any Tiny or larger container.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The undead doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The undead is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The forsaken genie makes three Dark Claw or Corrupted Bolt attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Dark Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (4d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 18 (4d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Corrupted Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +10 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (the genie’s choice) plus 18 (4d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Ravenous Breath (Recharge 6)
entries: The forsaken genie inhales lifeforce in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area that isn’t a Construct or Undead must make a DC 17 CON save, taking 54 (12d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The genie regains HP equal to half the total damage dealt.

bonus.name: Genie Shape
entries: The genie magically transforms into a Medium cloud of darkness filled with glittering particles of the element it once embodied or back into its bipedal form.

bonus.name: Its statistics are the same in each form
entries: Any equipment it is wearing or carrying transforms with it. It reverts to its bipedal form if it dies. The genie can’t use this bonus action to transform into its bipedal form while inside a Medium or smaller container.

reaction.name: Dark Wish (136 HP or Fewer)
entries: When a creature the forsaken genie can see within 60 feet of it makes an attack roll or save, the genie can twist the strands of reality, forcing the target to reroll the attack or save with disadvantage. 147 G G Genie, Ice Sila

reaction.name: A stocky humanoid emerges from a pillar of ice
entries: Its body glitters as the ambient light reflects off its many facets.

reaction.name: Surprising Warmth
entries: Ice silas are genies who call frozen realms home. They often mimic the appearance of humanoids they have encountered or especially trust, and they often prove friendlier than most genies. They do still have a roguishly playful side and enjoy pranks, like icing over walkways or growing icicles in the shape of massive teeth over doorways and cave entrances.

reaction.name: Icy Polearms
entries: Ice silas wield large fauchards, meticulously crafted from solid ice, primarily reserving them for defense.

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The fractidron doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The fractidron is immune to poison and psychic damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The fractidron deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Sure Treaded
entries: Difficult terrain doesn’t cost the fractidron extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fractidron makes two Scrap Slam or Burning Goo attacks.

action.name: Scrap Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the fractidron’s choice).

action.name: Burning Goo
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) fire damage. Each creature within 5 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) fire damage.

action.name: Sparking Eye Beam (Recharge 6)
entries: The fractidron emits a bolt of electricity in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 13 DEX save, taking 12 (5d4) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. 201 M M

bonus.name: Shrapnel Catapult
entries: The fractidron sprays shrapnel on a point on the ground it can see within 60 feet. The area within 10 feet of that point is difficult terrain.

bonus.name: Patch Up (2/Day)
entries: The fractidron repairs itself with scrap materials, regaining 5 (2d4) HP.

reaction.name: Jolt
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of the fractidron hits it with an attack, the fractidron can send a short jolt of electricity at the creature. The attacker must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 2 (1d4) lightning damage.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The frost giant jarl is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Ice Walk
entries: The jarl can move across icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

trait.name: Snowsight
entries: The jarl can see through areas obscured by snowfall, sleet, and other wintry precipitation without penalty.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The frost giant jarl makes two Icy Battleaxe or Ice Boulder attacks.

action.name: Icy Greataxe
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 7) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) cold damage.

action.name: Ice Boulder
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage.

action.name: Avalanche (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The jarl sends out a wave of snow in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 21 (6d6) bludgeoning damage and 18 (4d8) cold damage and is buried. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t buried. A buried creature is restrained, unable to breathe or stand up, and takes 4 (1d8) cold damage at the end of each of its turns. A creature, including the buried creature, can take its action to free the buried creature by succeeding on a DC 17 STR check.

bonus.name: Icy Glare
entries: The jarl glares at a creature it can see within 120 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or be incapacitated with fear for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target is immune to the frightened condition, it is immune to this effect. If the target succeeds on its initial save, it is immune to this jarl’s Icy Glare for 24 hours.

bonus.name: Rally (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The frost giant jarl bellows a rallying cry to its allies. Each friendly creature within 60 feet of the jarl that can hear the jarl has advantage on the next attack roll and the next save it makes before the start of the jarl’s next turn. 153 G G Giant, Hill Giant Chieftain The long, scraggly beard of the powerful giant is encrusted with days-old food. It brandishes a spiked club the size of a tree trunk and opens its mouth to emit a sound—half belch, half roar.

bonus.name: Giant Brutes
entries: Hill giant settlements are ruled by chieftains, typically already the largest and toughest giant around but also the most aggressive and domineering. A tendency toward violence isn’t strictly necessary, but a chieftain who loses the confidence of their people opens themselves up to challenges from rivals, which often lead to violence with the winner claiming the role.

bonus.name: Opposing Drives
entries: To display their status among already gluttonous hill giants, chieftains consume more than is typical, even going so far as to gorge themselves to capacity. This constant feeding primes their digestive tracts to be able to regurgitate the acidic contents of their stomach with ease.

bonus.name: Symbols of Leadership
entries: Chieftains often sport bushy beards, bind their hair into tall mounds, wear large shoulder pads, or otherwise attempt to enlarge their profile in an effort to intimidate underlings and rivals. They wield massive clubs carved from ancient trees and studded with jagged pieces of stone or metal.

trait.name: Ethereal Sight
entries: The ghostweed can see 30 feet into the Ethereal Plane when it is on the Material Plane, and vice versa.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The ghostweed is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions. P P 240

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ghostweed makes three Vine attacks. It can replace one Vine attack with Drink Life.

action.name: Vine
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) necrotic damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13) if it is a Medium or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained. The ghostweed can have up to two creatures grappled at a time.

action.name: Drink Life
entries: The ghostweed drains vitality from one creature grappled by it. The target must make a DC 13 CON save, taking 13 (3d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The ghostweed then regains HP equal to half that amount.

bonus.name: Etherealness
entries: The ghostweed enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Ethereal Plane, and vice versa, yet it can’t affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

bonus.name: Pollen Cloud (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The ghostweed emits a 10-foot-radius cloud of sparkling, ghostly pollen around itself. The cloud’s area is lightly obscured until the end of the ghostweed’s next turn. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. A creature that dies within 24 hours of failing this save rises as a specter 1d4 hours later.

monster.name: Ghoul Lord
languages: the languages it knew in life

trait.name: Hungry Dead Nature
entries: The ghoul lord doesn’t require air or sleep. In addition, it must consume at least 2 pounds of raw meat every 24 hours, or it loses its immunity to exhaustion and risks starvation until it does so. While it has any levels of exhaustion from starvation, the ghoul lord can’t remove levels of exhaustion until it consumes at least 4 pounds of raw meat.

trait.name: Impenetrable Ego
entries: While the ghoul lord is conscious and wearing no armor and wielding no shield, it adds its CHA modifier to its AC (included above).

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: As the zombie lord. U U 296 Spider Climb. The ghoul lord can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on the ceiling, without needing to make a skill check.

trait.name: Turning Defiance
entries: As the zombie lord.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: As the zombie lord.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ghoul lord makes two Rapier attacks or three Necrotic Bolt attacks. It can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead, it must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or contract the ghoul hunger disease (see Monster Vault ).

action.name: Rapier
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Necrotic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Inspire Servants
entries: The ghoul lord inspires up to three friendly

bonus.name: Undead it can see within 30 feet of it
entries: Each target has advantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the start of the lord’s next turn.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The ghoul lord moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Consume (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The ghoul lord makes one Bite attack against a creature within its reach. If the attack hits, it deals damage as normal, and the lord regains HP equal to the necrotic damage dealt.

legendary.name: Goad (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The ghoul lord goads up to three hostile creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or use its reaction to move up to half its speed in a straight line toward Undead the lord chooses. Targets don’t ignore opportunity attacks or damaging terrain when moving in this way.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The girtablilu is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Speak with Scorpions
entries: The girtablilu can communicate with scorpions and similar stinging desert insects as if they shared a language.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The girtablilu makes two Claw attacks and one Sting attack, or it makes two Longbow attacks.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). The girtablilu has two claws, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Sting

reaction.name: Opportunistic Predator
entries: A mudflow ooze resembles a shallow drinking hole or mud puddle when stationary, waiting patiently for birds or other small creatures to approach for a drink or bath. When prey does come close enough, the ooze lashes out with its pseudopods and entangles the unfortunate creature, dragging it down and digesting it over the course of several days.

reaction.name: Seasonal Hibernation
entries: During the dry season, the mudflow ooze lies dormant, resembling dry, cracked mud. When the rainy season comes, it awakens and skulks along riverbanks and lakesides in search of prey.

A creature immune to the charmed condition is immune to Whine. 159 G G Gnoll, Bone-Brewer An elderly gnoll, bent by age, tilts back her head and cackles cruelly. She wears thick, colorful clothing in layers, and rune- carved bones dangle alongside jewelry and tassels.

reaction.name: Keepers of Ceremony
entries: Bone-brewers are witches woven into the fabric of gnoll societies. They maintain the long oral traditions of their people, focusing on mystical ceremonies and religious rites, especially during momentous events and holy days. Though rarely the most powerful spellcasters in a gnoll settlement, they’re often among the most respected. When tribes go to battle, the bone-brewers join the warriors to bolster allies and terrorize enemies with their magic.

reaction.name: Secrets of Carved Marrow
entries: Bone- brewers draw their magic from the ritually prepared bones of dead animals. They carve runes into the bones to trap magic within the marrow and then shatter them to release that magic. The bones of more impressive and magical creatures, such as bulettes or dragons, can store more magic, driving the gnolls to embrace regular, ritualistic hunts to better prepare for the ever- looming battles with their neighbors.

action.name: Grave Allies (1/Day)
entries: The grave hag magically calls 1 ghast , 2 ghouls , or 2d6 skeletons or zombies . They arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the hag and obeying its spoken commands. The Undead remain for 1 hour, until the hag dies, or until the hag dismisses them as a bonus action.

bonus.name: Illusory Appearance
entries: The grave hag covers itself and anything it is wearing or carrying with a magical illusion that makes it look like another creature of its general size and Humanoid shape. The illusion ends if the hag takes a bonus action to end it or if the hag dies. The changes wrought by this effect fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, the hag could appear to have smooth skin, but someone touching it would feel its rough flesh. Otherwise, a creature must take an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC 20 INT (Investigation) check to discern the hag is disguised.

reaction.name: Hunger for the Lost
entries: Personifications of darkness and cruelty, shadow hags subsist on the hopelessness and panic that come with being lost and unable to find your way. Bullies and cowards, they patiently lie in wait for travelers unfamiliar with the area and slowly weave the shadows to tangle paths and lead their prey in circles.

reaction.name: Terrified Regions
entries: Left unopposed in a region, a coven of shadow hags can foster an environment where the locals live in constant fear of the night and what lies beyond the borders of their communities. This can sometimes backfire for the coven, forcing them to move on, for those afraid to leave their homes are less capable of sustaining the hags with their preferred diet of hopeless fear that comes with being lost and away from home.

The new gray thresher is Medium, deals only half the force damage with its Pseudopod attack, and doesn’t have the Devouring Ooze trait or this bonus action. The new thresher otherwise has the same statistics as its parent and is an ally of its parent. A new thresher grows into a full thresher after it finishes a long rest. Gremlin, Spellbane A gremlin in ill-fitting wizard robes sits atop a stool, cackling. The remnants of a miscast spell flow around it, striking nearby objects at random.

bonus.name: Mischievous Saboteurs
entries: Spellbane gremlins are gremlins born of failed and ill-considered magical experiments or accidents. They embrace the magic that spawned them and are driven to prove themselves better than other spellcasters and gremlins. Being gremlins, this primarily takes the form of inveterate and minor sabotage. They eat reagents, redirect scrying spells, urinate in unwatched potion cauldrons, and generally cause misery for their victims until their ego is appeased or they are driven out.

bonus.name: Arcanist’s Bane
entries: Spellbane gremlins can both sense and warp magic around them. They can’t cast spells, but they can sabotage the spellcasting of even expert spellcasters, redirecting or duplicating the magic with wild abandon. These gremlins live to pester spellcasters and often infest towers and academies. A common task for apprentices is to search out and dispatch any nearby gremlin infestations.

bonus.name: Egotistical Guardians
entries: Groups of spellbane gremlins quickly grow into narcissistic cults of personality with the most charismatic and successful of them—or more often, the one having stolen the largest hat—declaring themselves “archmagus” and forcing the others into line. These leaders claim ruins as their “arcane towers,” and they spend their days feeding on any lingering magical energies and tormenting those who defile the sanctity of their domains without the appropriate tribute and praise. Like the arcane communities they mimic, these groups are inherently unstable and prone to factionalism and infighting over minor disagreements and clashes in personality.

entries: When a creature the greater pseudodragon can see targets it with an attack, the dragon can move up to 10 feet away from the attacker without provoking opportunity attacks. If this moves the dragon outside the range of the attack, the attack misses. Dragonette, Pelagic The limbless blue body of this tiny fish-like dragon is ridged with frilled spines. Its pearlescent eyes appear blind, but the creature swims with sinuous and eel-like grace through the water.

reaction.name: Aquatic Dragons
entries: Though it can breathe air and move on land, a pelagic dragonette’s natural environment is the sea, and they are typically found swimming through the open ocean, though occasionally can be found in brackish river deltas and salt marshes. When on land, the dragonette moves by slithering like a snake.

reaction.name: Endless Curiosity
entries: Pelagic dragonettes are extremely curious and seek out new objects and experiences, whether that be investigating those traveling the water’s surface or rooting around the sandy seafloor or muddy marsh bottom. Though cautious with larger creatures, their curiosity often still draws them into engagement— with those not overtly hostile, anyway.

reaction.name: Venomous Spines
entries: A pelagic dragonette has small venom sacs at the base of their spines used to deter predators, and in times of extreme duress, they can expel the venom in a burst.

entries: Melee Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) force damage plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.

bonus.name: Impart Energy
entries: The hammergeist throws some of its energy into a weapon or toward a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target is a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4 (1d8) radiant damage on each hit until the start of the hammergeist’s next turn. If the target is a creature, it must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 9 (2d8) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one, as a spectral hammer flies at it.

reaction.name: Absorb Energy
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of the hammergeist that it can see casts a spell or uses a feature that inflicts force damage or radiant damage, the hammergeist can absorb the energy. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 CHA save or lose the spell or use of the feature. The hammergeist can then choose to regain 9 (2d8) HP or deal an extra 4 (1d8) force or radiant damage (whichever type was absorbed) with the next Ghostly Hammer attack it makes before the end of its next turn. 175 H H

trait.name: Cuteness
entries: If the owlbear hasn’t attacked a creature in the last 24 hours, creatures that can see the owlbear must succeed on a DC 12 CHA save or be compelled to pet, admire, praise, or give treats to the owlbear for 1 minute. If a creature’s save is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the owlbear’s Cuteness for the next 24 hours.

trait.name: Heightened Sight and Smell
entries: The owlbear’s Perception is 16 when perceiving by sight or smell.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The owlbear is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Beak
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Fleeing Bound
entries: The owlbear takes the Disengage or Hide action.

bonus.name: Hatchling’s Cry (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The owlbear releases a cry audible to 300 feet. Each hostile creature within 30 feet of the owlbear that can hear the cry must succeed on a DC 12

bonus.name: WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn
entries: If the owlbear’s caretaker can hear the cry, that creature can Dash on its next turn as a bonus action.

trait.name: Spiked Body
entries: A creature that hits the giant hedgehog with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4)piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant hedgehog makes one Bite attack and one Slam attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be knocked prone.

action.name: Roll (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The giant hedgehog curls up in a ball and rolls through creatures. It moves up to 20 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Medium or smaller creature without provoking opportunity attacks. The first time it enters a creature’s space during this move, that creature must make a DC 12 STR save. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (4d4) piercing damage, is knocked prone, and is pushed up to 10 feet away from the hedgehog’s path. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knocked prone or pushed.

reaction.name: Curl Up
entries: When a creature the giant hedgehog can see within 30 feet of it targets it with an attack, the hedgehog can quickly curl up, making itself a smaller target. The attacker has disadvantage on the attack roll.

trait.name: Poisonous Flesh
entries: The hellworm’s body is toxic. A creature that touches the hellworm or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 11 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn. H H 176

action.name: Burrowing Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: + 4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage, and the hellworm attaches to the target. While attached, the hellworm can’t attack, and at the start of each of the hellworm’s turns, the target takes 5 (2d4) acid damage. The attached hellworm moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the hellworm’s movement. It can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement on its turn. It does so after inflicting 15 HP of damage to the target or the target dies. A creature, including the target, can use its action to detach the hellworm.

action.name: Acid Spit
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) acid damage.

reaction.name: Burrow Deeper
entries: When a creature attempts to remove the hellworm while it is attached to a creature, the hellworm can burrow deeper into the creature’s flesh. If it does so, the creature attempting to remove the hellworm must succeed on a DC 11 STR check or the hellworm remains attached.

trait.name: Augmented Weapons
entries: The high mechanist uses its INT modifier when calculating weapon attack rolls. When the mechanist hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 3d8 lightning damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: The mechanist is proficient with tinker tools and doubles its proficiency bonus for any ability check it makes with tinker tools.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The high mechanist makes three Wrench or Light Crossbow attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, the target can’t take reactions and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. 333 Wrench. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) lightning damage.

action.name: Light Crossbow
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) plus 13 (3d8) lightning damage.

action.name: Charged Probe (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The high mechanist lobs a charged probe at a point it can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must make a DC 17 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 31 (7d8) lightning damage and is incapacitated and charged with lightning until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated or charged with lightning. A creature charged with lightning bursts with lightning at the end of its next turn, spreading to each creature within 5 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Quick Creation (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The high mechanist imbues magic into various machine parts it is carrying and creates a Medium Construct. The Construct appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mechanist and obeys the mechanist’s spoken commands. It uses the statistics of a fractidron (found in this book) but it isn’t a mechadron. The mechanist can have up to two such Constructs under its control at one time. Each Construct remains for 1 minute, until the mechanist dies, or until the mechanist uses this bonus action again to dismiss one or both of them.

bonus.name: Repair (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The mechanist touches one friendly Construct it can see. The target regains 10 (4d4) HP.

reaction.name: Magnetic Pulse
entries: When a creature the high mechanist can see attacks it with a weapon made at least partially of metal while within 5 feet of it, the mechanist can release a magical, magnetic pulse. The attacker must succeed on a DC 17 DEX save or have disadvantage on the attack roll.

trait.name: Bulky Might
entries: The hill giant chieftain can use CON instead of CHA when making CHA (Intimidation) checks.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The hill giant chieftain is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Stalwart
entries: If the hill giant chieftain starts its turn afflicted by an ongoing effect that allows for a repeated save to end the effect, such as the hold spell or the poison from an ettercap’s Bite, the giant can make the save at the start of the turn instead of the end and has advantage on the save. G G 154

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hill giant chieftain makes two Spiked Club attacks or three Rotten Snack attacks.

action.name: Spiked Club
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) piercing damage.

action.name: Rotten Snack
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Belch
entries: The hill giant chieftain belches, releasing a wave of foul, fetid stench in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Acidic Bile
entries: When the hill giant chieftain is attacked by a creature it can see within 10 feet of it, it can regurgitate some of the contents of its stomach. The attacker must make a DC 16 DEX save, taking 7 (2d6) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Giant, Mud The hulking giant seems half-finished, its skin sagging and malleable. With the help of its other hand, it shapes an arm into a monstrous sword.

reaction.name: Unfinished Giants
entries: Mud giants view themselves as imperfect works, the unfinished project of a now-dead god. Their bodies are malleable, a trait that draws them to live in swamps and other areas with ever-changing terrain. They are typically solitary or else live in small, tight-knit families. Fire lets them bake their bodies into a more rigid shape for a time, but excessive exposure can cause the giant’s form to become too rigid and crumble. This complex relationship with fire leads many mud giants to become skilled potters.

reaction.name: Kin to Rejects
entries: Mud giants have sympathy for those they view as similarly imperfect, and many develop a coterie of such rejects. The kindest take in orphans, exiles, and wounded animals, forming an ersatz family, and the cruelest build a following of bandits, outcasts, and brutes who also disdain the world.

trait.name: Frightful Injuries
entries: The injuries dealt by the hippalektryon resist being healed by magic. A creature that has taken damage from one of the hippalektryon’s attacks recovers only half the HP from spells and potions until it finishes a short rest.

trait.name: Flying Leap
entries: The hippalektryon’s long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start. In addition, it can fly up to 30 feet on its turn, but it must start and end its movement on a solid surface, such as a roof or the ground. If it is flying at the end of its turn, it falls to the ground and takes falling damage.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The hippalektryon is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hippalektryon makes one Bite attack and one Claws attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: Melee Weapon Attack. +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.

bonus.name: Neighing Crow (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The hippalektryon tosses its head back and crows. Each creature within 30 feet of the hippalektryon that can hear it must make a WIS save. On a failure, a creature is deafened and frightened until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature is only deafened until the end of its next turn. 177 H H

monster.name: Hoard Golem
languages: understands the languages of its creator

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The golem doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Enchanted Weapons
entries: The golem’s weapon attacks are magical. When the golem hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 force damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Golem Resilience
entries: The golem is immune to poison and psychic damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to exhaustion and to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poison conditions.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hoard golem makes two Slam or Throw Treasure attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) force damage.

action.name: Throw Treasure
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the golem’s choice) plus 18 (4d8) force damage. Thrown treasure teleports back to the golem at the end of its turn.

action.name: Thieving Whirlwind (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The hoard golem partially disperses into a whirlwind of treasure then recoalesces. Each creature within 20 feet of the golem must make a DC 17 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 44 (8d10) bludgeoning damage and loses one object it is wearing or carrying. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and doesn’t lose an object. Each object must weigh no more than 20 pounds and not be wrapped around or firmly attached to a creature. The object becomes part of the golem’s body and can’t be retrieved until the golem dies.

bonus.name: Strike With Awe
entries: The golem shifts and exposes valuable treasure to one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or be incapacitated and have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn, as it stands and stares at the glittering treasure. 161 G G Golem, Keg An ornate keg—complete with arms, legs, and a stern dwarven face—walks about the tavern, dispensing drink to any and all.

bonus.name: Dwarven Creation
entries: Keg golems are created by dwarven rune masters. Given a full keg of strong ale, the creator carves magical runes into it and outfits it with forged limbs and a face affixed to the front, often a replica of the creator’s own face. The process requires two weeks in its entirety. When activated, the runes glow with arcane power, ranging from faint blues to dark reds. Often, the brewer’s logo or slogan (or the establishment’s name or mascot, if commissioned) is carved into the keg.

bonus.name: Mobile Guardian
entries: These constructs are often used on long journeys, ensuring a mug of ale is always close at hand. When its master is threatened, the golem can also help to incapacitate foes with its powerful ale blast. Enterprising non-dwarves have taken to using refurbished keg golems at their taverns: for security but also to attract customers.

trait.name: Animal Affinity
entries: No Beast or creature with the Animal tag can willingly attack the hobfoot. They can be forced to do so through magical means. If the hobfoot attacks the creature, this effect ends for that creature.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The hobfoot is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Speak with Beasts
entries: The hobfoot can communicate with Beasts and creatures with the Animal tag as if they shared a language. H H 178

action.name: Shepherd’s Crook
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d12 + 2) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 12).

action.name: Sickle
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage, and the target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet for 1 minute. This effect ends early if the target receives magical healing.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The hobfoot can cast the mending cantrip at will, requiring no material components and using WIS as the spellcasting ability.

bonus.name: Whistle (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The hobfoot whistles to issue one of the following commands to one Beast or creature with the Animal tag it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 12 WIS save or obey the command. • Attack. The target uses its reaction to make one melee or ranged attack (the hobfoot’s choice) against one creature the target can see within its weapon’s range. • Come. The target uses its reaction to move up to its speed toward the hobfoot. It doesn’t avoid opportunity attacks or damaging terrain when moving. • Go. The target uses its reaction to move up to its speed directly away from the hobfoot. It doesn’t avoid opportunity attacks or damaging terrain when moving.

action.name: Sting
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 12 CON save, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the poison damage reduces the target to 0 HP, the target is stable but poisoned for 1 hour, even after regaining HP, and is paralyzed while poisoned in this way.

reaction.name: Distressed Dance
entries: When the giant honey bee is attacked by a creature it can see, it can perform a distressed dance. The attacker has disadvantage on the attack roll.

trait.name: Droning Swarm
entries: A creature in the swarm’s space is surrounded by buzzing insects that disrupt the creature’s ability to hear and speak. The creature has disadvantage on

trait.name: WIS (Perception) checks that rely on hearing
entries: If the creature casts a spell with a verbal component, it must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or the spell fails to cast, expending the action required to cast it but not the spell slot or daily use.
