BEE DANCE LANGUAGE A character who has established peaceful contact with giant honey bees can learn Bee Dance as a language as outlined in the Training downtime (see Player’s Guide ). While any character who learns it can understand Bee Dance, a creature other than a giant honey bee can only convey basic concepts. A character who assumes the shape of a giant honey bee can communicate fully using the language.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny bee. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

action.name: Sting
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage if the swarm is at half its hit points or fewer. The target must make a DC 14 CON save, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

trait.name: Bound Minion
entries: The hooded one is magically bound to a powerful creature. It is resistant to one of the following damage types associated with its patron: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant, thunder. In addition, the hooded one’s patron can communicate with it telepathically regardless of distance or plane of existence.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The hooded one has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the hooded one’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

trait.name: Relentless Devotion (Recharge 6)
entries: If the kobold takes 10 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 HP, it is reduced to 1 HP instead.

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, the hooded one has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its Perception is 6 when perceiving by sight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hooded one makes two Patron’s Gift attacks.

action.name: Patron’s Gift
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) damage of the type chosen with Bound Minion. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be pushed 10 feet away from the kobold and knocked prone.

bonus.name: Hidden Scurry
entries: The hooded one moves up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, and if it moves into a lightly or heavily obscured area, it takes the Hide action. If the hooded one is aware of traps in the area, the kobold can choose if this movement triggers any of them.

reaction.name: Patron’s Rebuke
entries: When a creature damages it, the hooded one can release a backlash of its patron’s power. That creature takes 3 (1d6) damage of the type chosen with Bound Minion. 189 K K Kobold, Truescale From behind the mob of angry kobolds steps a larger, beefier kobold. Their muscles bulge as they flex for show, and their snout twists in a terrible grin.

reaction.name: A Beast Among Kobolds
entries: The truescale is the brute of the kobold world, a hulking specimen among its smaller, slimmer kin. Roughly the height of a dwarf but much wider, their rippling muscles presage a ferocious strength. In contrast to the sneakiness and cunning of many other kobolds, the truescale is straightforward and devastating in combat.

reaction.name: Draconic Bearing
entries: Truescales are a rarity among kobolds, happening only once every dozen or so clutches, and their natural hardiness and size lead many scholars to believe them as evidence that kobolds do indeed descend from dragons, as they often claim.

reaction.name: Armored Wrestlers
entries: Truescales prefer to wrestle and crush their foes, rather than stabbing and scuttling like their smaller kin. Their girth makes fitting into armor sized for other kobolds difficult, and their preference for wrestling leaves them wanting a greater range of motion than most armor affords. Most would rather outfit themselves in piecemeal armor: scraps of metal plates held over vital areas with bits of leather or rope.

reaction.name: Kobold Vanguard
entries: One or two truescales may accompany a larger force of kobolds, acting as the vanguard and serving as battering rams and demolitionists—enabling smaller kobolds to use their ranged attacks and traps to the greatest effect.

trait.name: Blood Sense
entries: The hungering tangle can pinpoint, by scent, the location of creatures that aren’t Constructs or Undead and that don’t have all of their HP within 60 feet of it and can sense the general direction of such creatures within 1 mile of it.

trait.name: Painful Thorns
entries: The hungering tangle has hooked thorns that painfully latch onto creatures. For each hungering tangle attached to a creature, the creature’s speed is reduced by 5 feet. If a creature has three or more hungering tangles attached to it, the creature has disadvantage on weapon attack rolls.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The hungering tangle is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Thirsty Leap
entries: While a creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead and that doesn’t have all its HP is within 30 feet of the hungering tangle, the tangle’s long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

action.name: Hooked Thorns
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage, and the hungering tangle attaches to the target. While attached, the hungering tangle can use only the Deep Pull action, and it moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the tangle’s movement. The tangle can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement on its turn. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the tangle by succeeding on a DC 13 STR check.

action.name: Deep Pull
entries: The hungering tangle’s thorns sink into a creature it is attached to, and it deeply drinks the creature’s blood. The target loses 13 (3d8) HP.

reaction.name: Hungry Pursuit
entries: When a creature with blood moves within 30 feet of the hungering tangle, the tangle can move up to half its speed toward the creature. 179 H H

trait.name: Natural Tracker
entries: The huntmaster has advantage on WIS (Survival) checks to track creatures in farmland, forest, and grassland terrain. In addition, difficult terrain composed of nonmagical plants doesn’t cost the huntmaster extra movement.

trait.name: Point-Blank Hunter
entries: When the huntmaster makes a ranged attack with a bow, it doesn’t have disadvantage on the attack roll from being within 5 feet of a hostile creature, though it may still have disadvantage from other sources.

trait.name: Precise Archer
entries: A ranged weapon deals one extra die of its damage when the huntmaster hits with it (included in the attack).

trait.name: Unflappable
entries: The huntmaster can’t be surprised.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The huntmaster makes three Longbow attacks.

action.name: Longbow
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn. A creature can use its action to free itself by succeeding on a DC 15 STR check.

bonus.name: Hit and Run
entries: The huntmaster takes the Disengage action.

bonus.name: Pack Leader
entries: The huntmaster issues a command to up to two friendly Beasts it can see within 60 feet of it that can hear it. Each target can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks and has advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the huntmaster’s next turn.

reaction.name: Lead the Hunt
entries: When a friendly creature the huntmaster can see within 30 feet of it fails a save, the huntmaster can call out a command, allowing the target to roll again. The target must take the new result.

reaction.name: Swift Dodge
entries: When a creature the huntmaster can see targets it with an attack, the huntmaster can move up to 10 feet away from the attacker without provoking opportunity attacks. If this movement moves it out of range of the attack, the attack misses.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The ice sila can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Ice Glide
entries: The ice sila can burrow through only nonmagical ice and snow. While doing so, the sila doesn’t disturb the material through which it moves.

trait.name: Nebulous (Cloud Form Only)
entries: The ice sila’s Stealth is 19, it can hover while flying, can’t manipulate objects or attack, and it can pass through any space air or snow can pass through without squeezing. In addition, it can enter and hide in any Tiny or larger container, such as a pouch, lamp, backpack, or barrel.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ice sila makes three Icy Fauchard or Icy Burst attacks. If two Icy Burst attacks hit one creature, the target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Icy Fauchard
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage plus 13 (2d12) cold damage.

action.name: Icy Burst
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +10 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) cold damage.

action.name: Create Ice Elemental (1/Day)
entries: The ice sila magically creates one or more ice-based Elementals with a total CR no higher than 5 in unoccupied spaces the sila can see within 30 feet of it. The Elementals act as allies of the sila, obeying its spoken commands. The Elementals remain for 1 hour, until the sila dies, or until the sila dismisses them as a bonus action. G G 148 Travel the Planes (1/Day). The ice sila transports itself to a different plane of existence. This works like the plane shift spell, except it can affect only itself and can’t use this action to banish an unwilling creature.

bonus.name: Flash Freeze
entries: The ice sila magically freezes a point it can see within 60 feet of it, creating a 10-foot cube of frozen water or a 20-foot-radius patch of icy ground. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 18 DEX save or be restrained and unable to breathe (if in frozen water) or fall prone (if on the icy ground). A creature, including the restrained creature, can take its action to free the restrained creature by succeeding on a DC 18 STR check. The ice sila can have only one of each effect active at a time.

bonus.name: Genie Shape
entries: The ice sila magically transforms into a Medium cloud of ice and snow or back into its bipedal form.

bonus.name: Its statistics are the same in each form
entries: Any equipment it is wearing or carrying transforms with it. It reverts to its bipedal form if it dies. The sila can’t use this bonus action to transform into its bipedal form while inside a Medium or smaller container. Genie, Samum

bonus.name: A monstrous genie steps from the sandstorm
entries: Its hands end in brutish claws, and leopard spots dot its hide—along with a mismatched collection of jewelry.

bonus.name: Corrupted Genies
entries: When a djinni betrays those closest to it for its own selfish benefit, it might transform into a samum—exchanging many of its genie powers for more fiendish ones. Samums are embodiments of betrayal and desperation. They are twisted by their failures and determined to prove that mortals are as base and self- serving as they are. They plot especially to incite civil wars, succession crises, and similar conflicts that pit nominally noble peoples against one another.

bonus.name: Poisoned Gifts
entries: Samums lair in deserts, badlands, and remote wastes where they hunt for stranded travelers, especially after sandstorms or near local hazards, where the desperate are more readily found. Then, playing the role of a helpful genie, it will offer the travelers just what they need to survive—but only if they betray their companions. If a traveler rejects the offer, the genie leaves the person to die but offers their companions the same deal. If they accept, the genie rescues them from their predicament and claims their soul as payment. Unlike many other fiends, samums sometimes offer to relinquish their hold on a soul if the victim is able and willing to further the genie’s schemes.

trait.name: Cold Aura
entries: At the start of each of the demon’s turns, each creature within 5 feet of it takes 4 (1d8) cold damage and is subjected to the demon’s Ravenous Cold trait.

trait.name: Demonic Resilience
entries: The demon is resistant to cold, fire, and lightning damage. In addition, it is immune to poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The demon has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Ravenous Cold
entries: A creature that takes cold damage from the icerift demon must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or suffer a curse of lingering hunger. Every 24 hours that elapse, the cursed creature must consume double its normal daily nourishment requirement or suffer one level of exhaustion at the end of the day. The curse and the exhaustion it causes last until removed by the remove curse spell or similar magic.

trait.name: Snow Walk
entries: The demon can move across icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The icerift demon makes three Ice Shard attacks.

action.name: Ice Shard
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) cold damage, and the target is subjected to the demon’s Ravenous Cold trait.

action.name: Icicle Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The icerift demon exhales a plume of ice in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 10 (4d4) piercing damage and 18 (4d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Each creature is then subjected to the demon’s Ravenous Cold trait.

bonus.name: Ice Rift
entries: The icerift demon creates an icy crack in the ground centered on a point it can see within 30 feet of it. The crack is 5 feet wide, 10 feet long, and 20 feet deep. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or fall into the crack, taking falling damage as normal and landing prone. The sides of the crack are slippery and require a DC 15 STR (Athletics) or DEX (Athletics) check to climb out. The crack remains for 1 minute, until the demon uses this bonus action again, or until the demon dies. When the crack ends, its floor rises up to the level of the ground, harmlessly pushing any creatures in the crack back to the surface. 91 D D Demon, Shanlayu The scaled demon holds aloft its spear, channeling lightning from the gathering storm.

bonus.name: Storm Demons
entries: Shanlayu demons inhabit portions of the Abyss that border the Plane of Air, an area where storms constantly churn and crackle with energy. Their proximity to such raw elemental forces has imbued them with an innate affinity for lightning and the ability to manipulate and even create storms.

bonus.name: Servitors of Chaos
entries: Shanlayus serve demon lords and deities of chaos and storms. They are often sent on missions where quick and decisive victories are critical—or else are first strikers in larger-scale conflicts. Their ability to teleport allows them to hit multiple targets hard and fast, sowing confusion and panic on the battlefield.

trait.name: Frozen Body
entries: A creature that touches the iceskitter or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 4 (1d8) cold damage.

trait.name: Ice Walk
entries: The iceskitter can move across and climb icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The iceskitter makes four Icy Leg attacks. If two Icy Leg attacks hit one creature, the iceskitter impales the target on one of the legs, grappling it (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained. The iceskitter can have no more than two creatures impaled at a time.

action.name: Icy Leg
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) cold damage.

action.name: Frigid Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The iceskitter projects a blast of frigid air in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 27 (6d8) cold damage and its speed is reduced by 10 feet for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and its speed isn’t reduced.

bonus.name: Vent Cold
entries: The iceskitter vents extremely cold air at one creature it can see within 10 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Fiendish Weapons
entries: The infernal dreg’s weapon attacks are magical. When the dreg hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 fire damage (included in the attack).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The infernal dreg makes two Spiked Chain attacks or three Hurl Flame attacks.

action.name: Spiked Chain
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained, and the dreg can’t make a Spiked Chain attack against another target.

action.name: Hurl Flame
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 150 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) fire damage.

bonus.name: Heat Whirl
entries: The infernal dreg whirls its chain, superheating the area around it. Each creature within 15 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or have disadvantage on weapon attack rolls and on CON saves until the start of the dreg’s next turn.

reaction.name: Burning Leap
entries: When the infernal dreg takes damage from a creature it can see within 60 feet of it, the dreg can teleport, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, in a burst of flame to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of that creature. Each creature within 5 feet of the space the dreg teleports to must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) fire damage. 181 I I

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: As the fractidron .

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: As the fractidron .

trait.name: Ever-Changing Vulnerability
entries: At the start of each of the integron’s turns, roll a d20. Until the start of the integron’s next turn, when a creature makes an attack roll against the integron and the result on the d20 is that number, the attack roll is a critical hit, regardless of the result of the attack total. The integron isn’t resistant to damage from this attack.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the integron fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Unerring Mind
entries: The integron can perfectly recall information it has seen or heard in the past 180 days.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The integron makes five Electrified Tendril or Eye Beam attacks. If three Electrified Tendril attacks hit one creature, the target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Electrified Tendril
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 15 ft. one target. Hit: 20 (4d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) lightning damage.

action.name: Eye Beam
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +12 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) force damage.

action.name: Concussive Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The integron releases a wave of thunderous force in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 20 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 72 (16d8) thunder damage and is pushed up to 30 feet away from the integron. On a success, the creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed.

action.name: Mechadron Servitors
entries: The integron magically calls 4d6 solodrons , 4d4 dupladrons , or 2 tripladrons . The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the integron and obeying its spoken commands. The Constructs remain for 1 hour, until the integron dies, or until the integron dismisses them as a bonus action. The integron can have any number of mechadrons under its control at one time, provided the combined total CR of the mechadrons is no higher than 10.

bonus.name: Machine Vigor
entries: The integron ends one spell, magical effect, or condition affecting it.

bonus.name: Tactical Coordination
entries: The integron sends one of the following commands to up to two mechadrons it can see within 60 feet of it: • Protect the Plan. Each target has advantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saves until the start of the integron’s next turn. • Reconfigure. Both targets combine into a new mechadron, provided the targets are within 10 feet of each other: two solodrons become a dupladron, a solodron and a dupladron become a tripladron, two dupladrons become a tetradron, or a solodron and a tripladron become a tetradron. The new mechadron’s HP total is equal to the combined HP of the targets. • Reposition. Each target can use a reaction to move up to half its speed in a direction of the integron’s choice. This movement is unaffected by difficult terrain and doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

reaction.name: Project Shield
entries: When a mechadron the integron can see within 60 feet of it, excluding itself, is attacked, the integron can project a magical shield, increasing the target’s AC by 6 until the start of the integron’s next turn.

legendary.name: Teleport
entries: The integron magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

legendary.name: Call Mechadrons (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The integron uses Mechadron Servitors.

legendary.name: Bolster Mechadrons (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: Up to three mechadrons the integron can see within 60 feet of it gain 14 (4d6) temporary HP. 203 M M Mephits A chunk of obsidian unfurls, a plume of mud rises, and lightning strikes to form three imp-like creatures with mischievous grins.

legendary.name: Living Glass
entries: Composed of earth and fire, glass mephits look like moving chunks of obsidian and are typically found in areas of volcanic activity. They tend to be more difficult to anger than their magma mephit cousins (see Monster Vault ), but when wronged, they never forget it.

legendary.name: Muddy Nuisance
entries: Sludge mephits are formed of earth and water, and they are mercurial in personality. While stubborn and argumentative, they also get bored easily and attempt to spice up any debate with thrown balls of muck. They love to make a mess and take any opportunity they can to leave muddy prints in clean areas.

legendary.name: Storm Elementals
entries: Composed of the lightning, precipitation, and thunder of a raging storm, storm mephits are more energetic and livelier than other mephits, speaking quickly and jumping between topics.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The isazix can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Frozen Weapons
entries: The isazix’s weapon attacks are magical. When the isazix hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d6 cold damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Reap Soul
entries: If a Humanoid is reduced to 0 HP while within 30 feet of the isazix, the isazix’s Soul Scream recharges.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The isazix makes one Bite attack and two Trident attacks, or it makes four Ice Bolt attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, that creature’s speed is reduced by 10 feet.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) cold damage. The target’s HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the cold damage taken. The reduction lasts until the target I I 182 finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

action.name: Trident
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage, or 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack, plus 14 (4d6) cold damage. If the target is wielding a weapon or shield, it must succeed on a DC 17 DEX save or drop the weapon or shield (the isazix’s choice if the target is wielding both).

action.name: Ice Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) cold damage.

bonus.name: Soul Scream (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The isazix releases a wail generated by the souls it has captured in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or be stunned until the end of its next turn. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more is stunned for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The isherrar can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The fey is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Shape Water
entries: Unless it is in an arid climate, the isherrar can spend 1 minute creating an orb of water or ice in its hand, shaping the liquid into a nonmagical weapon, set of tools, or other mundane item. The item can be no larger than a 5-foot cube and lasts for 1 hour. The isherrar can have no more than three weapons, sets of tools, or other items created in this way at one time.

trait.name: Swim By
entries: The isherrar doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks when it swims out of an enemy’s reach.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The isherrar makes two Ice Blade or Water Blast attacks.

action.name: Ice Blade
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) cold damage.

action.name: Water Blast
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) cold damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The isherrar can cast the minor illusion cantrip at will, requiring no material components and using CHA as the spellcasting ability.

bonus.name: Binding Gaze
entries: The isherrar turns its charming gaze on one

bonus.name: Beast or Humanoid it can see within 30 feet of it
entries: The target must succeed on a DC 14 WIS save or be charmed until the end of its next turn. While charmed, its speed is reduced to 0.

reaction.name: Watery Displacement
entries: When a creature the isherrar can see targets it with an attack, the isherrar can temporarily liquefy itself, imposing disadvantage on the attack roll. 183 I I

trait.name: Charge
entries: If the issgandr moves at least 15 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Ram attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 4 (1d8) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be knocked prone.

trait.name: Elemental Nature
entries: The issgandr doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: The issgandr is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, and unconscious conditions. I I 184 Ice Glide. The issgandr can burrow through only nonmagical ice and snow. While doing so, the issgandr doesn’t disturb the material through which it moves.

trait.name: Ice Walk
entries: The issgandr can move across icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The issgandr makes one Ram attack and one Tail Whip attack.

action.name: Ram
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.

action.name: Tail Whip
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.

reaction.name: Icy Jet
entries: When the issgandr takes damage from a creature within 10 feet of it, it can release a jet of super-chilled water. That creature must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be pushed up to 15 feet away from the issgandr, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The joy thief is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Emotionless
entries: The joy thief is immune to the charmed and frightened conditions, and it is immune to effect that would change its emotional state.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The joy thief makes two Scratch or Psychic Bolt attacks. If two Psychic Bolt attacks hit a creature, the target is frightened until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Scratch
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Steal Emotion
entries: The joy thief tries to consume an emotion from one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 CHA save or suffer one of the following effects, based on the chosen emotion: • Anger. For 1 minute, the target has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes each round, and the thief has advantage on the first attack roll it makes each round. Until this emotion is restored, the target has disadvantage on initiative checks and on saves against being frightened. • Joy. For 1 minute, the target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet, and the thief’s speed is increased by 10 feet. Until this emotion is restored, the target can’t benefit from Bardic Inspiration or spells that bolster the target’s ability checks, attack rolls, or speed, such as bless , enhance ability , or haste . • Love. For 1 minute, the target can’t use the Help action, and spells the target casts that restore HP restore 3 (1d6) fewer HP. For the duration, the thief takes 2 (1d4) less damage from all sources, as it magically evokes affection from enemies. Until this emotion is restored, the target’s allies are considered hostile creatures for the purposes of determining how the target’s spells, class features, and other effects interact with the target’s allies. Until it finishes a long rest, the target can’t feel the stolen emotion, and the joy thief can’t steal that emotion from the target again. 185 J J

trait.name: Devil’s Sight
entries: Magical darkness doesn’t impede the devil’s darkvision.

trait.name: Devilish Resilience
entries: The devil is resistant to cold damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to fire damage and poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The devil has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The devil makes two Hellish Lash attacks.

action.name: Hellish Lash
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing plush 27 (6d8) fire damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 18 DEX save or catch fire. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, a creature on fire takes 5 (2d4) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

action.name: Litany of Order (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The devil recites from its scroll of laws at up to three creatures that can hear it within 60 feet of it. Each target must make a DC 17 WIS save. On a failure, a creature takes 42 (12d6) psychic damage and is paralyzed for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. A paralyzed creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Prohibit Action
entries: The devil passes judgment on a creature within 60 feet of it that can hear it. The target must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or be unable to take an action of the devil’s choice, such as Attack or Cast a Spell, until the start of the devil’s next turn.

reaction.name: Sudden Guilt
entries: When a creature the jurist devil can see within 60 feet of it deals damage to it, the devil can fill the creature with sudden guilt. The creature must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or take 7 (2d6) psychic damage. 99 D D Devil, Waxworker The tall, red-skinned devil wears a bronze mask with an unnerving leer. Its too-long fingers—at the end of its too-long arms—delicately hold a thin, cruel knife. Behind it stands a row of wax figures, their features warped into horrifying visages.

reaction.name: Lost Beauty
entries: Waxworker devils have been forced, or have willingly chosen, to sacrifice their beauty for power, usually in service to devils high in the infernal hierarchy. As a result, they have the power to trade in souls. Most never get over the loss of their beauty and develop a deep hatred for places and creatures considered beautiful. The majority of waxworker devils wear masks to hide their hideous faces, even from themselves. Occasionally, they arise from the souls of powerful and extremely vain people.

reaction.name: Waxwork Curators
entries: Those who forfeit their souls to a waxworker devil become like waxwork sculptures of themselves, now part of the devil’s collection—warped and disfigured for the devil’s enjoyment. Such souls are unable to act or move but are aware of their condition and can witness the distorted visages of the other wax figures around them.

reaction.name: Waxy Minions
entries: Using a long and taxing ritual, waxworker devils sometimes animate figures from their collection, whether as laborers or soldiers or something else. These figures become loyal and obedient wax golems (also in this book), though they retain their distorted and warped appearances.

trait.name: Heightened Sight and Smell
entries: The owlbear’s Perception is 17 when perceiving by sight or smell.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The owlbear is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The owlbear makes one Beak attack and one Claw attack. If both attacks hit a Small or smaller target, the target is grappled (escape DC 13).

action.name: Beak
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.

bonus.name: Hunter’s Bound
entries: The owlbear moves up to half its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

bonus.name: Rend
entries: The owlbear violently wrenches a Small or smaller creature it is currently grappling. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or take 2 (1d4) slashing damage. 231 O O

monster.name: Keg Golem
languages: understands the languages of its creator but can’t

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The golem doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Empty Keg
entries: The keg golem holds 20 gallons of ale. If it runs out of ale, such as from using the Ale Blast action, the golem’s speed is reduced to 0, and it has disadvantage on all attack rolls until it is refilled with at least 1 gallon of ale.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the golem remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal keg or barrel.

trait.name: Golem Resilience
entries: The golem is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage. In addition, G G 162 it is immune to exhaustion and to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The keg golem makes two Slam or Ale Splash attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Ale Splash
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d10 + 1) poison damage. This attack expends half a gallon of ale.

action.name: Ale Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The keg golem releases 1 gallon of ale in a 15-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 13 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 22 (4d10) poison damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Barrel Roll
entries: The golem rolls up to 20 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Medium or smaller creature. The first time it enters a creature’s space during this move, that creature must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be knocked prone. The golem can use this bonus action even if it is empty. Golem, Pebble A group of pebble people carry a ruby between them.

bonus.name: Component Collectors
entries: Pebble golems were created to harvest fungi, crystals, and other materials, fitting into tiny cracks or holes underground. Less scrupulous creators might send them into shops or rivals’ homes to acquire components.

bonus.name: Creator Connection
entries: Each pebble golem is infused with a drop of blood from its creator, tying it intrinsically to a specific arcane practitioner.

trait.name: Celestial Resilience
entries: The kel essuf is resistant to radiant damage.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The kel essuf has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The kel essuf’s weapon attacks are magical.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The kel essuf makes one Bite attack and one Fiery Tail attack, or it makes two Celestial Bolt attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Fiery Tail
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage. If the target is a creature or a flammable object, it ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the target takes 3 (1d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

action.name: Celestial Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) fire damage plus 4 (1d8) radiant damage.

reaction.name: Warding Flare
entries: When a creature the kel essuf can see within 30 feet of it, which can include itself, is attacked, the kel essuf can release a flare of silvery fire from its ears. Roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll.

monster.name: Kelp Wight
languages: the languages it knew in life

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the kelp wight remains motionless and prone, it is indistinguishable from a pile of kelp.

trait.name: Kelp Slough
entries: The wight has advantage on checks it makes to escape a grapple, leaving nothing but kelp in the grip of its attacker if it escapes.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The kelp wight doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The kelp wight is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Zombie Spawn
entries: A Humanoid killed by the kelp wight or that drowns while being grabbled by the wight rises 24 hours later as a zombie with a swimming speed of 30 feet under the wight’s control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed. The kelp wight can have no more than ten zombies under its control at one time. If the kelp wight is destroyed, each zombie has a 10 percent chance to transform 24 hours later into an independent kelp wight with control of the remaining zombies.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The kelp wight makes one Kelp Strand attack and one Slam attack.

action.name: Kelp Strand
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d4 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16) if it is a Medium or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the wight can automatically hit the target with its Kelp Strand. The wight can have up to two targets grappled at a time.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Strangle
entries: The kelp wight squeezes the air from the lungs of one creature it is grappling. The target must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be unable to breathe, speak, or cast spells with verbal components, and it begins suffocating. This effect lasts until the grapple ends. 313 W W Wight, Wrath Rage burns in the eyes of this deathly pale figure, and dark energy seeps from a wound in its chest.

bonus.name: Fueled By Vengeance
entries: When a person of strong will dies unjustly, they may return as a wrath wight. These wronged parties seek vengeance against those that caused their deaths, resting only when they feel the scales have been balanced. This balance is different for each wrath wight. Some feel satisfied and go to their eternal rest after taking the life of the person who took theirs, while others will rest for nothing short of the destruction of the city that persecuted them. A wrath wight’s rage can usually be quelled only by violence, but its vengeful hand can be stayed if true justice is meted out to the guilty, or if the guilty are truly penitent and make suitable atonement for their actions.

bonus.name: Shared Pain
entries: The wrath wight’s rage spills over into its strikes, flooding its victims’ psyche with the anger and pain the wrath wight feels at the injustice done to it. This flood can sometimes fill victims with rage and cause them to go on their own rampages.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the killsward remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a grassy mound or hillock.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The killsward is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Shielding Sward
entries: The killsward can use the grass-like growth on its back to shield riders, covering them and allowing creatures to ride the killsward while it burrows. The killsward can protect up to 1 Medium rider or 2 Small riders in this way. Creatures riding the killsward while it burrows are blinded, restrained against the killsward, and unable to breathe until the killsward returns to the surface.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The killsward makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Dirt Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The killsward exhales a blast of dirt and small stones in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 13 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t blinded or knocked prone.

bonus.name: Ingest Dirt
entries: The killsward burrows up to 20 feet. The next time it rolls a die to recharge Dirt Blast, it can roll two dice and take the better result. 187 K K

monster.name: Kineater
languages: understands the languages it knew in life but

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The kineater is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Blood Sense
entries: The kineater can pinpoint, by scent, the location of creatures that aren’t Constructs or Undead and that have blood within 120 feet of it and can sense the general direction of such creatures within 1 mile of it. K K 188 Sand Camouflage. The kineater’s Stealth is 17 while in sandy terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The kineater makes four Bite attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, the target must make a DC 15 CON save. On a failure, a creature loses 5 (2d4) HP, and the kineater regains HP equal to that amount, as it drinks the target’s blood.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the target also suffers from paranoid hallucinations, can’t take the Help action, and considers all creatures as hostile for the purposes of determining how the target’s spells and features interact with them. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Invoke Paranoia
entries: The kineater enhances the paranoia afflicting a creature it can see within 60 feet of it that is suffering from its poison. One creature poisoned by the kineater must succeed on a DC 15 INT save or immediately use its reaction to make a weapon attack against a creature of the kineater’s choice within the weapon’s range. Kobold, Hooded One From beneath a large hood, a rasping voice hisses out a few words. Scaly hands pull back the hood to reveal a wizened kobold’s face with the fiery eyes of a fanatic.

bonus.name: Servitors of Monsters
entries: Hooded ones are kobold zealots that have pledged service to some powerful entity, most often a fiend or ancient dragon. This connection gives them some magical power and allows their patron to observe through their eyes and ears. They receive the words of their patron with religious fervor and often serve as the only religious leader in remote kobold settlements. They see themselves as the hands of their patron, foregoing an individual identity and caring little for anything that doesn’t serve their patron’s goals.

bonus.name: Ambition and Ego
entries: Kobold chieftains and hooded ones rarely see eye to eye about matters of leadership, for as the mouthpiece of a greater power, the hooded one expects all their clan mates, including the clan leader, to heed their urgings. Clever and calculating, they use flattery and persuasion to become the power behind thrones, leading communities along their patron’s goals in secret. Those who become overzealous are usually killed before they can make too much trouble for local leaders.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The shrike doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The shrike is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lamentine shrike makes two Beak attacks.

action.name: Beak
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Mind-Piercing Shriek
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Captivating Song
entries: The shrike sings a melody that reverberates in the mind of one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The creature must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be compelled to use a reaction to move half its speed in a straight line in a direction of the shrike’s choice. While moving, the target doesn’t avoid opportunity attacks or damaging terrain, but this movement ends early if the target falls, becomes restrained, or is otherwise no longer able to move.

reaction.name: Soul Feast
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of the shrike is reduced to 0 HP, the shrike can consume a small portion of the creature’s fleeing soul, regaining 5 (2d4) HP. 191 L L

trait.name: Burning Body
entries: A nimbus of heat clings to the lava sprite. A creature that touches the sprite or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 3 (1d6) fire damage. At the start of its turn, the sprite chooses if this effect is active.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The lava sprite is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Illumination
entries: The lava sprite sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lava spire makes two Burning Hammer or Fire Orb attacks.

action.name: Burning Hammer
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Fire Orb
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) fire damage.

action.name: Lava Geyser (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The lava sprite stamps its foot on the ground, causing a fountain of molten lava to erupt from a spot on the ground the sprite can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of the lava geyser must make a DC 14 DEX save, taking 17 (5d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Fireheal
entries: If the lava sprite is within 5 feet of a Small or larger source of fire, it regains 7 (2d6) HP.

bonus.name: Sulfurous Cloud
entries: The ground cracks on a point the lava sprite can see within 60 feet of it, and a 10-foot-radius cloud of reeking sulfur appears centered on that point. The cloud spreads around corners, and its area is heavily obscured. A creature that enters the cloud’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. The cloud lasts for 1 minute, until the sprite dies, or until the sprite uses this bonus action again.

trait.name: Unstable Guts
entries: When the drake dies, the alchemical slurry in its belly explodes. Each creature within 10 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 7 (2d6) fire damage and be poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The least drake makes two Bite attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

action.name: Sulfurous Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The drake exhales fire in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 13 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 14 (4d6) fire damage and is poisoned by sulfurous fumes until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. Then, the drake is pushed up to 10 feet in the opposite direction of the line.

reaction.name: Sulfurous Fumes
entries: When the least drake takes fire damage, it can burp flammable fumes, and each creature within 5 feet of the drake takes 3 (1d6) fire damage, as the fire briefly spreads. Drake, Mirror A shimmering silver drake explodes from the sand dune, smelling of ozone and death. Its cat-like eyes fix on the horizon as blinding sunlight reflects off its scales.

reaction.name: Dune Hunters
entries: Mirror drakes stalk the deep desert, sliding through the sand in the search for prey. They are solitary hunters, ambushing camels and even entire caravans. They attack with the sun at their backs, erupting from the sand in a burst of searing light before charging their prey.

reaction.name: Sun-Bright Scales
entries: Mirror drakes take their names from their silver scales, polished to a mirror-like sheen as they move through the sand. The scales allow them to focus the light of the sun, either to defend themselves or to emit a searing flare of concentrated sunlight that can melt sand into glass. They rely upon external light sources to make use of their scales so prefer hunting in the day. Unable to use many of their defenses without light, they sleep beneath the sand at night to avoid potential predators.

reaction.name: Raider Mounts
entries: Some particularly daring desert bandits tame mirror drakes. They attach harnesses and sand sleds, enabling them to skim across the dunes. So long as the drake has a steady supply of food and isn’t treated unfairly, it is often more than willing to comply. Those bandits who fail to fulfill these simple needs tend to find themselves abandoned in the desert or even devoured.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The leoformic’s perception is 17 when perceiving by smell.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The leoformic is resistant to exhaustion and the frightened condition.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The leoformic has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the leoformic’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The leoformic makes one Bite attack and one Sting attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Sting
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) poison damage. The target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Drag Down
entries: The leoformic pulls a Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet of it to the ground. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be knocked prone. If the target is within 5 feet of another leoformic and that leoformic isn’t incapacitated, the target has disadvantage on the save. 193 L L

trait.name: Aspect-Powered Weapons
entries: The leshnydukh’s weapon attacks are magical. When it hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 2d8 acid (sylvan protector aspect) or fire (primal rage aspect) damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The leshnydukh is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Forest Aspect
entries: Difficult terrain composed of plants doesn’t cost the leshnydukh extra movement and can’t harm or slow it.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The leshnydukh has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Shield of Wisdom
entries: Each friendly creature within 30 feet of the leshnydukh can’t be charmed or frightened and has a +2 bonus to its AC while the leshnydukh isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The leshnydukh makes two Claw attacks and two Entangling Vines attacks, or it makes four Screeching Bolt attacks. It can replace one attack with Aspect Howl, if available. L L 194 Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) acid or fire damage.

action.name: Entangling Vines
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) acid or fire damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 19). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained.

action.name: Screeching Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +11 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) thunder damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage.

action.name: Aspect Howl (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The leshnydukh releases a howl or calls toward up to three creatures it can see within 60 feet of it. If primal rage is active, each target must succeed on a DC 19 WIS save or be frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If sylvan protector is active, each target regains 30 (6d8 + 3) HP.

bonus.name: Change Aspect
entries: The leshnydukh changes its aspect from Sylvan Protector to Primal Rage or vice versa.

reaction.name: Stunning Screech
entries: When the leshnydukh takes damage, the owl face on its shoulder can let out a piercing screech. Each hostile creature within 15 feet of the leshnydukh that can hear the screech must succeed on a DC 19 CON save or be stunned until the end of the leshnydukh’s next turn.

trait.name: Forgetful Bursts
entries: The lethblooms constantly release puffballs, battering creatures in the space with their petals and pollen. A creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space must succeed on a DC 15 INT save or be unable to add its PB to its ability checks, attack rolls, and saves until the start of its next turn, as it briefly forgets aspects of its training.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The lethbloom swarm is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The lethbloom swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny lethbloom. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The lethbloom swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lethbloom swarm makes two Memory Leech attacks.

action.name: Memory Leech
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. Hit: 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage, or 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (1d10) psychic damage if the swarm has half of its HP or fewer. If the target currently suffers the effects of the swarm’s Forgetful Bursts, its INT score is reduced by 1d4. The target dies if this reduces its INT to 0. Otherwise, the reduction lasts until the target finishes a short or long rest.

reaction.name: Cognitive Disruption
entries: When a creature the lethbloom swarm can see that currently suffers the effects of the swarm’s Forgetful Bursts deals damage to the swarm, the swarm can psychically call to the pollen dulling the creature’s memory. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 INT save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Blessed Weapons
entries: The lilium’s weapon attacks are magical. When it hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 2d6 radiant damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The lilium has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The lilium is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lilium makes two Slam or Bladed Leaf attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) radiant damage.

action.name: Bladed Leaf
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) radiant damage.

action.name: Radiant Acorn (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The lilium throws an acorn at a point it can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must make a DC 14 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 21 (6d6) radiant damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t blinded.

action.name: Healing Sap (2/Day)
entries: The lilium touches another creature. The target magically regains 10 (2d8 + 1) HP and is freed from any disease or poison. 241 P P

bonus.name: Pollen Burst
entries: The lilium releases a burst of glowing pollen. Each creature within 10 feet of it must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or be coated in the pollen and poisoned until the start of the lilium’s next turn. While coated, the creature can’t benefit from being invisible and sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius.

monster.name: Lingering Shade
languages: any languages it knew in life

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: The lingering shade can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, the lingering shade has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its perception is 8 when perceiving by sight.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The lingering shade doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The lingering shade is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The shade makes three Draining Burst attacks.

action.name: Draining Burst
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) necrotic damage. A Humanoid slain by this attack rises 24 hours later as a shadow under the shade’s control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life. The shade can have no more than eight shadows under its control at one time.

bonus.name: Reaper’s Insight
entries: The lingering shade delivers one of the following commands at up to two friendly Undead, other than itself, that it can see within 30 feet of it: • Find Death’s Door. Each target uses its reaction to move up to half its speed in a direction of the shade’s choice. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks. • Join the Dying. Each target has advantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the start of the lingering shade’s next turn. • Stave Off Final Death. Each target gains 5 (2d4) temporary HP until the start of the shade’s next turn.

reaction.name: Join Us
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of the lingering shade makes a death save, the shade can pull at that creature’s soul, imposing disadvantage on the save. If the creature fails the save, the shade regains 7 (2d6) HP. 195 L L

trait.name: Elemental Nature
entries: The living loam doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: The living loam is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Verdant Camouflage
entries: The living loam’s stealth is 14 while in any terrain with ample, obscuring plant life.

trait.name: Speak with Beasts and Plants
entries: The living loam can communicate with Beasts, creatures with the Animal tag, and Plants as if they shared a language. L L 196

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The living loam makes two Root-Covered Fist attacks. If both attacks hit one creature, the target is restrained by roots until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Root-Covered Fist
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Invigorate
entries: One friendly Beast, creature with the Animal tag, or Plant the living loam can see within 30 feet of it gains one of the following benefits: • The target gains 5 (2d4) temporary HP until the start of the loam’s next turn. • The target has advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the loam’s next turn. • The target is cured of the poisoned condition.

reaction.name: Circle of Life (Recharge 4–6)
entries: When a Beast, creature with the Animal tag, or Plant is reduced to 0 HP within 30 feet of the living loam, the loam can cause the earth around the creature to welcome it, burying the body and creating a burst of life. The area within 20 feet of that creature becomes difficult terrain.

monster.name: Living Quicksand
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The living quicksand can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Ooze Nature
entries: The quicksand doesn’t require sleep.

trait.name: Ooze Resilience
entries: The living quicksand is resistant to the grappled and restrained conditions, and it is immune to exhaustion and to the blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, and prone conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The living quicksand makes four Impaling Pseudopod attacks, or it uses Wet Sand twice. It can replace one attack with Engulf.

action.name: Impaling Pseudopod
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). If the target attempts to escape the grapple and fails, it takes 4 (1d8) piercing damage. The living quicksand has four Impaling Pseudopods, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Engulf
entries: One Medium or smaller creature grappled by the living quicksand and within 5 feet of it is pulled into the ooze’s body, and the grapple ends. While engulfed, the target is blinded, restrained, and unable to breathe, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the ooze, and it takes 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the ooze’s turns. When the ooze moves, the engulfed creature moves with it. The living quicksand can have only one creature engulfed at a time. An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 15 STR check. On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within 5 feet of the ooze.

action.name: Wet Sand
entries: The living quicksand throws a gob of wet sand at a point it can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature within 5 feet of that point must make a DC 15 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage, and its speed is halved. On a success, a creature takes half the damage, and its speed isn’t reduced.

bonus.name: Reel
entries: The living quicksand pulls each creature impaled by its pseudopods up to 15 feet straight toward it.

reaction.name: Reactive Crystal
entries: When a creature the living quicksand can see within 5 feet of it attacks it, the ooze can harden its outer surface, adding 3 to its AC against that attack.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The luciva can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Celestial Resilience
entries: The luciva is resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The luciva has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The luciva’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Strobing Bioluminescence
entries: The lights beneath the luciva’s skin flash and flicker in a disorienting array. When a hostile creature that can see the luciva starts its turn within 30 feet of the luciva, the creature must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or be visually overwhelmed by the display until the start of its next turn. A creature overwhelmed in this way is blinded, and when it moves, it moves in a random direction. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the save at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can’t see the luciva until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the luciva in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. L L 198

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The luciva makes four Tentacle attacks.

action.name: Tentacle
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) radiant damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 15) if it is a Large or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained. The luciva can have up to four creatures grappled at a time.

action.name: Stunning Pulse (Recharge 4–6)
entries: Each creature grappled by the luciva must make a DC 16 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 31 (7d8) radiant damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated.

bonus.name: Tidal Surge
entries: The luciva flaps its wings, creating a 60-foot line of water that is 10 feet wide and 10 feet tall. Each creature in the line must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be pushed 15 feet directly away from the luciva. The luciva can use this bonus action only while underwater.

reaction.name: Retributive Strike
entries: When a creature within 15 feet of the luciva hits it with an attack, the luciva can call down radiant retribution. The attacker must succeed on a DC 16 DEX save or take 4 (1d8) radiant damage.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The Luminous Lord is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Luminous
entries: The Luminous Lord sheds bright light in a 5- to 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. At the start of his turn, he can choose the radius, choose if the bright light is sunlight, or choose to not shed light.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The Luminous Lord has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Radiant Weapons
entries: The Luminous Lord’s weapon attacks are magical. When the Luminous Lord hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d6 radiant damage (included in the attack). F F 138

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Luminous Lord makes three Rapier or Radiant Bolt attacks.

action.name: Rapier
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) radiant damage.

action.name: Radiant Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (5d6 + 5) radiant damage.

action.name: Blinding Flare (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The Luminous Lord releases a flare of scorching sunlight in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) fire damage and 17 (5d6) radiant damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t blinded.

bonus.name: Radiant Corona
entries: The Luminous Lord flares with inspiring light. Each friendly creature within 15 feet of the Luminous Lord and that can see him has advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of his next turn.

reaction.name: Castigating Flare
entries: When a creature the Luminous Lord can see targets him with an attack, he can send a blinding beam at the creature. The attacker must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or be blinded until the start of the Luminous Lord’s next turn.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The lustralichen spider is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Spore Coat
entries: The spider is covered in hallucinogenic spores that make it appear blurry. Attackers that rely on sight have disadvantage on attack rolls against the spider. This effect is suppressed until the start of the spider’s next turn if the spider takes cold damage.

trait.name: Web Sense
entries: While in contact with a web, the spider knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web. S S 276 Web Walker. The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The lustralichen spider makes three Bite attacks.

action.name: Bite

action.name: Spore Cloud (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The spider releases hallucinogenic spores. Each creature within 15 feet of the spider must make a DC 18 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 45 (10d8) psychic damage and hallucinates for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half the damage and doesn’t hallucinate. A hallucinating creature rolls a d8 at the start of each of its turns and suffers a condition determined by that roll: 1–2 charmed, 3–4 frightened, 5–6 incapacitated, 7–8 stunned. A hallucinating creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

At the start of a restrained creature’s turn, roll a d8. The creature suffers an effect determined by that roll (see the Spore Cloud action). A creature, including the target, can take its action to free the target from the webbing by succeeding on a DC 18 STR check. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 12; HP 10; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

At the start of each of the knight’s turns, it chooses one of the following presences, which lasts until the start of the knight’s next turn. • Esoteric Presence. Each friendly creature that starts its turn within 15 feet of the knight increases the save DC by 1 for the next feature or spell it activates, casts, or uses before this presence ends. • Protective Presence. Hostile creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against friendly creatures within 5 feet of the knight. • Suppressing Presence. Each friendly creature within 15 feet of the knight is resistant to conditions inflicted by spells and magical effects.

Mechadrons A large, multifaceted metallic form hovers in the air, silvery tendrils extending from its mass. A serpentine machine composed of a dozen smaller machines scuttles from behind it.

bonus.name: Independent Constructs
entries: Sometimes a mechadron gets lost or otherwise separated from the collective, no longer able to hear the Plan. Forced to exist on their own, these fractidrons eventually begin to value their individuality, altering their forms then seeking out others of like mind. Many become convinced the Plan is a lie perpetrated upon all mechadrons to keep them subservient to some fell power. For their part, other mechadrons view fractidrons as broken and hunt them down to be recycled into serving the Plan.

bonus.name: Temporary Defenders
entries: In most instances, when mechadrons combine, it is a permanent transformation into a more powerful entity. However, when twelve dupladrons combine into a duodekadron, it is a brief union, lasting only until the threat or problem is resolved. The combination takes mere seconds but is very unstable and can collapse easily. But the power of duodekadrons is unmistakable, cutting through flesh, steel, and stone, routing armies, and destroying or driving away powerful enemies.

bonus.name: Mechadron Mastermind
entries: Integrons are the keepers of the Plan—that inscrutable goal all mechadrons serve— within a given region, world, or plane, and they directly coordinate mechadron activities for operations deemed of greatest significance. They are integral to the execution of the Plan, portions of which become emblazoned on the creature’s surface in a script decipherable only by other mechadrons. While all mechadrons can reconfigure themselves given sufficient cause and time, the influence of a nearby integron makes this almost instantaneous, forever ensuring the right mechadron for the job. However, the versatility required of an integron leaves minor, ever- changing gaps in its defenses.

Minotaur, Patternmaster One minotaur stands at the forefront of their warband, wielding a greatsword. A brand in the shape of a labyrinth is burned into its chest, and a matching symbol is etched into the gleaming blade.

reaction.name: Order from Chaos
entries: The maze has always been an important symbol and concept in minotaur society, embodying a fusion of chaos and order. Patternmasters are so named for their uncanny skills in leadership and strategy and are adept at navigating complexities, nurturing their people through challenges—physically, emotionally, and spiritually. They frequently command troops and hold positions of authority.

reaction.name: Maze Brands
entries: Once a minotaur is recognized as a patternmaster, they are magically branded with a unique maze glyph, a symbol of their role, responsibilities, and power. The patternmaster then inscribes this same glyph on their weapons, imbuing the items with power.

reaction.name: Private Meditation
entries: Patternmasters spend hours of each day in silent meditation, focused on their own unique maze, keeping their personal pattern in mind for as long as possible, gaining insight from its twists and turns and allowing it to guide decision-making.

The attacker must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or have disadvantage on the attack roll. 117 D D Drake, Razor The long, lean drake’s scales gleam like polished steel as it raises its scythe-like wing claws.

reaction.name: Dragon Friend and Foe
entries: Razor drakes and adamantine dragons (also in this book) share appetites and often territories, and the relationship between the two can be complicated. In some instances, an adamantine dragon will have a cooperative relationship with any razor drake neighbors: the drakes use their acid breath to unearth metallic ores for the dragon in exchange for a share of the spoils, one consuming the metal while the other collects it. Other times, the drakes are considered nuisances as they continually brave the dragon’s wrath by plundering their lair for refined metal objects or deposits of ore.

reaction.name: Metal Eaters
entries: A significant part of a razor drake’s diet is metal. They mainly eat ferrous metals to maintain their hides, but they also tend to develop tastes for specific metals, based solely on personal preference. They dig the metal ore out of the mountains throughout their territories, using their claws and acid. While raw ore is always preferred over refined metal, they aren’t above the often greater ease of access to the latter, so some razor drakes will raid humanoid settlements and caravans for such food.

reaction.name: Hired Mercenaries
entries: On occasion, certain humanoids might have need of a razor drake and enter into a bargain with one. Typically, such a deal would have the drake fight on behalf of said humanoids in exchange for metals. Given D D 118 the appetite and tastes of the razor drake, however, this can be an expensive arrangement and is usually only made by wealthy individuals or communities rich in such resources.

trait.name: Doom’s Herald
entries: If the mothman fails a save, it can succeed instead by ending a curse affecting one creature it can see within 120 feet of it.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The mothman is resistant to exhaustion and the frightened condition.

trait.name: Supernatural Awareness
entries: The mothman can’t be surprised.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The mothman makes two Unlucky Strike attacks.

action.name: Unlucky Strike
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or have disadvantage on the next attack roll or save it makes before the end of its next turn.

legendary.name: Bad Omen
entries: The mothman makes one Unlucky Strike attack.

legendary.name: Creeping Doom
entries: The mothman becomes invisible to cursed creatures until the end of its next turn, and it magically teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see within 10 feet of a cursed creature.

legendary.name: Induce Disaster (Costs 2 Actions)
