entries: Each creature within 15 feet of the mothman must succeed on a DC 17 CHA save or take 18 (4d8) psychic damage and be cursed (as per Cursed Gaze). A creature within range that is already cursed automatically fails this save and the curse’s die increases by one step, from a d4 to a d6, a d6 to a d8, and so on (to a maximum of d12). 209 M M

trait.name: Fire-Hardened
entries: When the mud giant takes fire damage, it gains one of the following effects of its choice until the end of its next turn: • Glazed Body. The giant’s AC increases by 3, and it loses its resistance to the grappled and restrained conditions. • Imperfect Edges. The next time the giant deals piercing or slashing damage with an attack, the target loses 5 (2d4) HP at the start of its next turn as the wound continues to bleed. • Sturdy Hammer. The next time the giant deals bludgeoning damage with an attack, the giant can choose for the target to be knocked prone or pushed up to 10 feet away from the giant.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The mud giant is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Muddy Body
entries: Creatures have disadvantage on checks made to escape the giant’s grapple. The giant loses this trait while benefiting from its Fire-Hardened trait.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant makes two Slam attacks or three Sling Mud attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, as determined by Mold Arm. If this attack was with a fist and not an arm shaped like a weapon, the target is also grappled (escape DC 16). The giant can have only one creature grappled for each fist it has, ending the grapple if it molds the fist into a weapon.

action.name: Sling Mud
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage, and the target is restrained in mud. A creature, including the target, can take its action to free the target by succeeding on a DC 16 STR check.

bonus.name: Mold Arm
entries: The mud giant reshapes one of its arms into a weapon or back into a fist. Its Slam attack deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, depending on the type of weapon chosen, until the giant uses this bonus action again. The giant can’t use this bonus action while benefiting from its Fire-Hardened trait. 155 G G Giant, War An armored giant strides forth—a dreadnaught of steel bearing a massive shield and battleaxe.

bonus.name: Trained for Combat
entries: War giants are the descendants of a martial order of giants who once served a fallen war god. Since the loss of their deity, they have passed down their training and techniques, aligning themselves to various communities as battlemasters.

bonus.name: Battle Commanders
entries: War giant training focuses on battlefield awareness and effective unit tactics. For a war giant, returning with as many soldiers as possible is almost as important as victory.

bonus.name: Worshipping War
entries: War giants typically view combat as a sacred duty, but some take a more secular view of military might. Whether stemming from faith or ambition, war giants gather and train various other creatures, uniting even disparate groups into cohesive armies.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The mudcrawler can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Charge
entries: If the mudcrawler moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Gore attack on M M 210 the same turn, the target takes an extra 5 (1d10) slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be knocked prone.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The mudcrawler is resistant to exhaustion and the frightened condition.

trait.name: Water Walker
entries: The mudcrawler can move across the surface of water as if it were harmless, solid ground. This trait otherwise works like the water walk spell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The mudcrawler makes one Gore attack and one Pincer Attack.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or have its speed halved until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Pincer
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained. The mudcrawler has two pincers, each of which can grapple only one target.

bonus.name: Crush
entries: One creature grappled by the mudcrawler must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or take 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage.

monster.name: Mudflow Ooze
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Amorphous
entries: The mudflow ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the mudflow ooze remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a natural mud puddle or area of cracked and dry earth.

trait.name: Flat Body
entries: The mudflow ooze can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, provided both are on the ground.

trait.name: Ooze Nature
entries: The ooze doesn’t require sleep.

trait.name: Ooze Resilience
entries: The ooze is resistant to the grappled and restrained conditions, and it is immune to exhaustion and to the blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, and prone conditions.

trait.name: Soft Earth Glide
entries: The mudflow ooze can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and mud. While doing so, the ooze doesn’t disturb the material through which it moves.

action.name: Pseudopod
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) acid damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13) if it is a Medium or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target takes 3 (1d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. The ooze can have up to two targets grappled at a time.

bonus.name: Drag Down
entries: The mudflow ooze sucks at the feet of one creature grappled by it and pulls the creature to the ground. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR check or be knocked prone and restrained until the grapple ends. A creature pinned in this way has disadvantage on checks made to escape the grapple. The ooze can have only one creature pinned in this way at a time.

reaction.name: Muddy Capture
entries: When a Medium or smaller creature enters or leaves the mudflow ooze’s space, it can grab the creature. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or be grappled if the ooze doesn’t have two other creatures grappled. 229 O O

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The musculi is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Speak with Beasts
entries: The musculi can communicate with Beasts as if they shared a language.

action.name: Needle Spear
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Throw Nail
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Dirty Trick
entries: The musculi performs one of the following tricks, using whatever materials are at hand, targeting one creature it can see within 15 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 12 DEX save or suffer the trick’s effects. • Cloudburst. The musculi tosses a puff of sand, dirt, or other substance at the target. The target’s space is lightly obscured, and it is blinded until the end of its next turn. • Frog in Your Throat. The musculi tosses an insect or similar small but harmless object into the target’s mouth or nose. The target briefly chokes or sneezes and is unable to speak or cast spells with verbal components until the end of its next turn. • Tangle Feet. The musculi throws a handful of small objects at the target’s feet. The target falls prone.

reaction.name: Nimble Dodge
entries: When a creature the musculi can see misses it with an attack, the musculi can move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. 211 M M

monster.name: Mycoptyx
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: Ant Haul
entries: The myrmeke is considered to be Medium for the purpose of determining its carrying capacity.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The myrmeke is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Dagger
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Steal Item
entries: The myrmeke steals an object from one creature it can see within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 12 DEX save or lose one object it is wearing or carrying of the myrmeke’s choice. The object must weigh no more than 10 pounds, can’t be a weapon, and can’t be wrapped around or firmly attached to the target.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The naavlashuk is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Psychic Parasite
entries: The naavlashuk’s attacks implant psychic parasites. Until the parasite is removed, the infected creature has disadvantage on INT, WIS, and CHA saves. Every 24 hours that elapse, the infected creature must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or reduce its INT, WIS, and CHA scores each by 1 and become a thrall of the naavlashuk for 24 hours, as if the creature failed a save against the dominate spell. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest after the parasite is removed. The creature dies if the parasite reduces one of these scores to 0. A creature that succeeds on three N N 214 of these saves expels the parasite from its body. Alternatively, the parasite can be removed with a greater restoration spell or similar magic. If the infected creature fails the save and the infecting naavlashuk has been slain, it becomes a thrall of the next nearest naavlashuk on the same plane. The naavlashuk ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a thrall.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The naavlashuk makes three Tentacle or Psychic Assault attacks. If two attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or be infected with a parasite (see Psychic Parasite).

action.name: Tentacle
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Assault
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) psychic damage.

action.name: Mind Leech (Recharge 6)
entries: The naavlashuk pulls at the minds of creatures in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 INT save. On a failure, a creature takes 28 (8d6) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t stunned. The naavlashuk then regains HP equal to half the total psychic damage dealt.

bonus.name: Parasite Screech
entries: The parasite within one creature the naavlashuk can see within 60 feet of it releases a burst of psychic energy. The target must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Naga, Enlightened The serpentine creature stands perfectly still, poised on the steps of the temple. The four arms of its humanoid torso are spread in ritualistic meditation. A third eye in its forehead opens.

bonus.name: Divine Agents
entries: Nagas have always had a connection to the Upper Planes, but those who attain enlightenment are often elevated as true celestials. These nagas are dispatched to remote locations to help their charges attain enlightenment.

bonus.name: Enigmatic Gurus
entries: Enlightened nagas’ teachings are seldom straightforward. Instead, they speak in riddles or parables for their charges to follow individualized paths.

bonus.name: Strict Teachers
entries: They often take their duties too seriously, interpreting even the smallest disruptions, like pausing an acolyte’s meditation, as a threat to spiritual progression.

trait.name: Celestial Resilience
entries: The nanuq is resistant to radiant damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The nanuq’s Perception is 22 when perceiving by smell.

trait.name: Ice Walk
entries: The nanuq can move across and climb icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The nanuq has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The nanuq’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Snowsight
entries: The nanuq can see through areas obscured by snowfall, sleet, and other wintry precipitation without penalty.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The nanuq makes one Battleaxe attack, one Bite attack, and one Claw attack, or it makes three Ice Bolt attacks.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 20 (3d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

action.name: Ice Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) cold damage.

action.name: Storm’s Fury (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The nanuq summons a blizzard around it. Each creature within 30 feet of it must make a DC 15 CON save, taking 24 (7d6) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Until the end of the nanuq’s next turn, the area within 5 feet of it is heavily obscured by snow and sleet.

bonus.name: Nanuq’s Curse
entries: One creature the nanuq can see within 60 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or be cursed for 24 hours. Until this curse ends, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls against bears and other ursine creatures, and it has disadvantage on WIS (Survival) checks to track or hunt Beasts. The nanuq can curse only creatures that have dealt damage to ursine creatures within the last 1 minute.

bonus.name: Snow Step
entries: The nanuq teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. The origin and destination spaces must contain snow. 217 N N

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The negalzyn is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Void Dweller
entries: The negalzyn doesn’t require air, food, drink, sleep, or ambient pressure, and it is immune to the effects of Void terrain. N N 218

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The negalzyn makes two Stinger or Psychic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Stinger
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage. The target must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) psychic damage.

action.name: Mind Shred (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The negalzyn unleashes nightmarish visions of the Void in a burst of mind-bending psychic energy. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 14 WIS save. On a failure, a creature takes 22 (5d8) psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated. Creatures with the Void Dweller trait or void tag (see Labyrinth Worldbook ) are unaffected.

bonus.name: Float
entries: The negalzyn can rise or descend vertically up to 5 feet above the ground and can remain suspended there. This bonus action works like the levitate spell, except there is no duration, the negalzyn can move up to half its speed horizontally while floating, and it doesn’t need to concentrate to continue floating each round.

bonus.name: Unnerving Gaze
entries: The negalzyn stares intently at one creature it can see within 30 feet of it, motes of pale blue twinkling in its deep-set black eyes. The target must succeed on a DC 14 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn. A creature that fails this save by 5 or more suffers a random, short-term dread effect for 1 minute.

trait.name: Clumsy
entries: While not flying, the nightwing is vulnerable to the grappled, prone, and restrained conditions.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The nightwing doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy’s reach.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The nightwing’s Perception is 17 while perceiving by smell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The nightwing makes two Bite attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage and 5 (2d4) acid damage.

bonus.name: Pinning Claws
entries: While flying, the nightwing reaches down with its claws at one Medium or smaller creature it can see within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or be knocked prone and pinned beneath the nightwing. While pinned, the target is prone and restrained until the nightwing moves or until a creature takes an action to free the restrained creature by succeeding on a DC 13 STR check. A freed creature is freed into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of where it was pinned if the nightwing still occupies that space.

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The nullifier doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Construct Resilience
entries: The construct is immune to poison and psychic damage, and it is immune to exhaustion and the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Limited Antimagic Aura
entries: A 60-foot-radius, spell - suppressing field emanates from the nullifier. Spellcasters in the area can sense the aura and are aware of when they are in it. A creature that casts a spell within the area must succeed on an ability check using its spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell’s circle. On a success, the spell is cast normally. On a failure, the spell fails to cast, expending the action required to cast it but not the spell slot or daily use. Cantrips are unaffected by this aura.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The nullifier makes three Tentacle Whip or Arcane Burst attacks.

action.name: Tentacle Whip (While Not Anchored Only)
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Arcane Burst
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) force damage.

bonus.name: Anchor
entries: The nullifier extends four of its metal tentacles to lock itself in place on the ground. While anchored in this way, the nullifier’s AC increases by 2, its speed is reduced to 0, and it can’t be knocked prone or moved against its will. The nullifier can use this bonus action again to end this effect.

reaction.name: Eldritch Feedback (While Anchored Only)
entries: When a creature successfully casts a spell while within the nullifier’s Limited Antimagic Aura, the nullifier can cause arcane feedback to explode on the spellcaster. The spellcaster must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or take 4 (1d8) force damage. 219 N N

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The nullphidian has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The nullphidian’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Sonorous Voice
entries: The nullphidian can’t be silenced.

trait.name: Unreadable
entries: The nullphidian can’t be detected by spells and features that detect Fiends, such as the detect evil and good spell or a paladin’s Divine Sense feature. The nullphidian has advantage on CHA (Deception) checks.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The nullphidian makes three Bellow attacks.

action.name: Bellow
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft., one creature. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) thunder damage. N N 220 Cacophony (Recharge 5–6). A chorus of clacking and shrieking voices erupts from the nullphidian. Each creature within 20 feet of the nullphidian must make a DC 16 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 31 (9d6) thunder damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t stunned.

bonus.name: Dark Urging
entries: The nullphidian whispers honeyed words and makes false promises to one creature it can see within 30 feet of it, while its mandibles clack subsonic tones that subvert the listener’s sense of self. The target must succeed on a DC 16 CHA save or be charmed until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Illusory Appearance
entries: The nullphidian covers itself and anything it is wearing or carrying with a magical illusion that makes it look like a Medium Humanoid. The illusion ends if the nullphidian takes a bonus action to end it or if the nullphidian dies. The changes wrought by this effect fail to hold up to physical inspection. Otherwise, a creature must take an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC 15 INT (Investigation) check to discern that the nullphidian is disguised.

reaction.name: Mute Voice
entries: When a creature deals damage to or otherwise harms the nullphidian with a spell or other magical effect, the nullphidian can clack a silencing command. That creature must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or be unable to speak or cast spells with verbal components until the end of its next turn. Observer The tall, long-limbed creature floats with a strange, bobbing grace. Its massive head bears a single violet eye. Blisters form on its body, splitting open to reveal additional smaller eyes.

reaction.name: Ocular Mastery
entries: Observers are aberrations with visual powers beyond understanding—and their abilities are not limited to their own eyes. An observer can usurp control over the vision of other creatures, forcing them to see whatever it wills. It also creates extra eyes across its body that it can detach for remote reconnaissance. Perhaps its most chilling power is its ability to devour the eyes of a dead creature and incorporate images the creature has seen into its own memories.

reaction.name: Confident yet Paranoid
entries: Observers’ intelligence and ability to gather information typically make them both bold and paranoid. They are assured by all they see yet worry about what remains unseen. Observers hate the idea of secrets to which they are not privy so will maintain regular surveillance on the area surrounding their lairs and on any neighbors. Little of interest escapes their notice.

reaction.name: Sorcerous Creations
entries: Observers were originally created by ancient magic users to be spies, interrogators, and advisors. The creatures chafed under their masters’ yoke, however, and ultimately threw off their chains, using their powers to discover their masters’ weaknesses. Old grudges die hard, and today, observers innately distrust those who wield magic. Despite this, they often hire themselves out as spies, lead secret spy organizations, and sell information to the highest bidders—often to those bidders with the juiciest information to offer in return. AN OBSERVER’S LAIR Observers prefer lairs in dark, underground locations near humanoid settlements, such as abandoned mines or sewers. Their lairs typically play with light, shadows, and reflections, incorporating mirrors and similar reflective surfaces to visually disorient and confuse visitors, allowing the observer to watch or communicate with visitors from afar or while cleverly “hidden” within a reflection. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the observer can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the observer can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Disorienting Reflections. Reflective surfaces within 15 feet of a point the observer can see within 120 feet of it shift subtly, bending reflected shapes and disrupting depth perception. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 17 INT save or have its speed halved until the end of its next turn. • Eye Vortex. Tiny eyes fly around and study up to two creatures the observer can see within 120 feet of it. The observer has advantage on the next attack roll it makes against each target or on the next save it makes against each target’s spells or other effects. • Nauseating Overload. Light and shadows rapidly blink and twist around up to three creatures the observer can see within 120 feet of it, overstimulating each creature’s vision. Each target must succeed on a DC 17 INT save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn. REGIONAL EFFECTS An observer’s lair is warped by its psychic power, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Exposed Secrets. Secrets regularly come to light through random happenstance within 1 mile of the lair, from a dancer stumbling into a hidden assassin just before it strikes to a local dog playfully snatching a secret message from a messenger. 221 O O • Eyes Everywhere. The observer can choose to see through the eyes of any Beast or Humanoid within 1 mile of the lair. The affected creature experiences a brief bout of dizziness or double vision when it does so. • Observant Observers. Creatures within 3 miles of the lair that are actively seeking hidden information or details, such as a guard on a watchtower or a detective on a case, have advantage on the first INT (Investigation) or WIS (Perception) check they make each hour. If the observer dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The observer is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Eyelink
entries: The observer ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a creature that has one of the observer’s eyes attached to it. The two don’t even need to be on the same plane of existence.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the observer fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Many Eyes
entries: The observer’s Perception is 22 while perceiving by sight, and it is resistant to the blinded condition. In addition, if the observer isn’t blinded, creatures attacking it can’t benefit from traits and features that rely on a creature’s allies distracting or surrounding the observer, such as the Pack Tactics trait or Sneak Attack class feature.

trait.name: Wandering Eyes
entries: The observer has one main eye and can have up to 20 smaller eyes active at a time. Each smaller eye is Tiny, can be attacked (AC 20; 1 HP; immune to psychic damage), has truesight out to 60 feet, has a flying speed of 60 feet, can hover, and can’t be knocked prone. Destroying an eye deals no damage to the observer, which can extrude a replacement eye on its next turn. The eyes are telepathically controlled by the observer and can’t move more than 1 mile away from it unless attached to a creature O O 222 or object. The observer can take its action to see through any number of its eyes, can switch between them without requiring an action, and can end the effect as a bonus action. While seeing through its small eyes, the observer is blinded and deafened to its surroundings. If the observer reabsorbs an eye, it learns everything the eye has observed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The observer makes four Claw or Psychic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 hit, range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) psychic damage.

action.name: Eye Beam (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The observer unleashes a beam of pure, psychic energy from its central eye in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a DC 17 INT save, taking 42 (12d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Attach Eye
entries: The observer sends eyes toward up to two creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 17 DEX save or the eye attaches to it. At the start of the creature’s next turn, it must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or forget the eye is attached to it, and the eye blends into the creature’s flesh, becoming hidden with a Stealth of 18. A creature that can see the eye can take its action to cut the eye off the creature with a weapon that deals piercing or slashing damage, destroying the eye and dealing one die of the weapon’s damage to the creature.

legendary.name: Attach Eye
entries: The observer uses the Attach Eye bonus action.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The observer flies up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Manipulate Eyes (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The observer manipulates the eyes attached to up to three creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 17 INT save or have disadvantage on attack rolls and saves until the end of its next turn, as its mind is bombarded with images from the attached eye.

legendary.name: Reabsorb Eyes (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The observer calls up to three eyes attached to creatures it can see within 30 feet of it to return to it, detaching them from those creatures, reabsorbing them, and regaining 10 (3d6) HP. The observer also learns everything each creature saw within the last 8 hours.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The oculo swarm has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Many Eyes
entries: The oculo swarm’s Perception is 20 while perceiving by sight, and it is resistant to the blinded condition. In addition, if the swarm isn’t blinded, creatures attacking it can’t benefit from traits and features that rely on a creature’s allies distracting or surrounding the swarm, such as the Pack Tactics trait or Sneak Attack class feature.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The oculo swarm can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny eyeball. The swarm can’t regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The oculo swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The oculo swarm makes two Extract Eye attacks. If both attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 14 STR save or the swarm removes one of its eyes. While missing half or fewer of its total number of eyes, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls and WIS (Perception) checks that rely on sight. While missing more than half its total number of eyes, the target is blinded until its sight is restored. If the target’s eye is recovered from the defeated swarm, it can be reattached with a successful DC 12 WIS (Medicine) check, provided the eye is reattached within 1 hour of the target losing the eye.

action.name: Extract Eye
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. Hit: 21 (6d6) piercing damage, or 10 (3d6) piercing damage if the swarm has half its HP or fewer.

bonus.name: Disorienting Gaze
entries: The oculo swarm’s many eyes turn toward one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The eyes then quickly shift to look in different directions, pulling the target’s gaze with them, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 CHA save or be disoriented until the end of its next turn. A disoriented creature moves in a random direction when it moves. 223 O O Ogre, Bog A hulking humanoid with knobbly skin and dark, lanky hair chews on a haunch of meat. A tree-branch club is clutched in the other huge fist.

bonus.name: Swamp Giants
entries: Making their homes deep in swampy locales, bog ogres are often solitary creatures, though they might also live in small communities—which they protect fiercely. They live comfortably in partially submerged environs, and they often build hidden underwater entrances to their homes to keep out unwanted visitors. Some bog ogres have taken up basic animal husbandry, keeping various swamp creatures in small enclosures for food or as guards or even pets.

bonus.name: Gruff Sellswords
entries: Bog ogres often fight with trolls over choice territory, but they tolerate green hags (see Monster Vault for both), occasionally working as guards, mercenaries, or other hired muscle for the fey. They distrust most other sentient creatures, though they aren’t immediately aggressive unless their home is threatened. Bog ogres can often be hired as guides if given an offering of fresh meat or mead.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The oliphaunt deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Terrifying Siege
entries: If the oliphaunt destroys a Small or larger object, each hostile creature within 10 feet of the oliphaunt must succeed on a DC 16 CHA save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Trampling Charge
entries: If the oliphaunt moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Gore attack on the same turn, the target must succeed on a

trait.name: DC 16 STR save or be knocked prone
entries: If the target is prone, the oliphaunt can make one Stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The oliphaunt makes one Gore attack and one Stomp attack, or it makes two Gore attacks.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (4d6 + 6) slashing damage.

action.name: Stomp
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 feet, one prone creature. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Trunk Sweep
entries: The oliphaunt sweeps its trunk in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be knocked prone.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The opossum’s Perception is 15 while perceiving by smell.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Feign Death
entries: When the opossum takes damage, it can fall over, release a foul odor, and reduce its breathing to appear dead. While feigning death, the opossum is prone and incapacitated. A creature must take an action to visually inspect the opossum and succeed on a DC 10 INT (Investigation or Nature) or WIS (Medicine or Perception) check to discern the opossum isn’t dead. The opossum remains in this state for 1 minute, but it can make a DC 11 CON save at the end of each of its turns, reviving itself from its torpor on a success.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The giant opossum’s Perception is 16 while perceiving by smell.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The giant opossum makes one Bite attack and one Claws attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage.

bonus.name: Tail Sweep
entries: The giant opossum sweeps its tail in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be knocked prone.

reaction.name: Feign Death (22 HP or Fewer)
entries: When the giant opossum takes damage, it can fall over, release a foul odor, and reduce its breathing to appear dead. While feigning death, the opossum is prone and incapacitated. A creature must take an action to visually inspect the opossum and succeed on a DC 12 INT (Investigation or Nature) or WIS (Medicine or

reaction.name: Perception) check to discern the opossum isn’t dead
entries: The opossum remains in this state for 1 minute, but it can make a DC 12 CON save at the end of each of its turns, reviving itself from its torpor on a success. If it takes damage, it immediately breaks out of its torpor.

monster.name: Oromur
languages: understands Deep Speech but can’t speak

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The aberration is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Slippery Slime
entries: The oromur’s body is coated in a faint sheen of slippery slime. A creature attempting to grapple the oromur has disadvantage on the check.

trait.name: Standing Leap
entries: The oromur’s long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start. O O 230

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The oromur makes one Impale attack and one Tail Slap attack, or it makes two Tail Slap attacks.

action.name: Impale
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) piercing damage. The target must succeed on a DC 14 DEX save or the oromur is impaled in the target’s flesh. The target has disadvantage on the save if the oromur moved at least 10 feet before making this attack. While impaled, the oromur can use only the Tail Slap action and Paralyzing Venom bonus action, it moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the oromur’s movement, and the target takes 7 (2d6) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. The oromur can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the oromur by succeeding on a DC 14 STR check.

action.name: Tail Slap
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.

bonus.name: Paralyzing Venom
entries: The oromur expels a paralytic poison at a creature it can see within 10 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or be paralyzed for 1 minute. If the oromur is impaled in the target, the target has disadvantage on the save. A paralyzed creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

reaction.name: Parrying Head
entries: The oromur adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the oromur must see the attacker and not be impaled in a creature. Owlbears A massive roar echoes in the distance—just as a small creature wobbles out from the brush on unsteady ursine legs that end in powerful talons.

reaction.name: Vulnerable Young
entries: Owlbears typically have two to four cubs every four years. They reach adulthood at around three years, and most stay with their parents for at least two. For the first year, the cubs are mere hatchlings, extremely reliant on their parents for food. Juvenile owlbears are at least a year old and range as far from the nest as their parents allow.

reaction.name: Rarely Alone
entries: Young owlbears are rarely without a parent keeping watching nearby, but that doesn’t stop them from getting into mischief, like climbing through barn windows to feast on small livestock.

trait.name: Charge
entries: If the patternmaster moves at least 10 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Gore attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the patternmaster and knocked prone.

trait.name: Imbued Weapons
entries: The patternmaster’s weapon attacks are imbued with its psychic power and are magical. When the patternmaster hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 psychic damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Inspiring Leader
entries: While the patternmaster is conscious, each friendly creature within 10 feet of it is resistant to the charmed and frightened conditions.

trait.name: Labyrinthine Recall
entries: The patternmaster can perfectly recall any path it has traveled.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The patternmaster is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The patternmaster deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The patternmaster makes one Gore attack and one Greatsword attack, or it makes three Psychic Bolt attacks.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Greatsword
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Psychic Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Dizzying Maze
entries: The patternmaster calls on the power of its maze and projects the maze’s confusing pattern into the mind of a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or become dizzy until the end of its next turn. While dizzy, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls, and its speed is halved. 207 M M

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The peak warden is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Lord of the Mountain Peaks
entries: The peak warden can move across and climb icy and rocky surfaces without needing to make an ability check. In addition, difficult terrain composed of ice, rocks, or snow doesn’t cost it extra movement.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The peak warden has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Snowsight
entries: The peak warden can see through areas obscured by snowfall, sleet, and other wintry precipitation without penalty.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The peak warden makes two Headbutt attacks or three Frost Bolt attacks. If both Headbutt attacks hit one Medium P P 232 or smaller creature, the target is pushed up to 15 feet away from the warden.

action.name: Headbutt
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) cold damage.

action.name: Frost Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) cold damage.

action.name: Mountain’s Wrath (Recharge 6)
entries: The peak warden creates a blizzard in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point it can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 24 (7d6) cold damage, is thrown up to 30 feet in a random direction, and knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t thrown or knocked prone. A creature that fails this save by 5 or more also suffers a level of exhaustion. If a thrown creature strikes an object, the creature takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

bonus.name: Freezing Voice
entries: The peak warden exhales a torrent of chilling cold in a 60-foot line that is 10 feet wide. Each creature in that line must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn.

monster.name: Pebble Golem
languages: understands the languages of its creator

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The golem doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Golem Resilience
entries: The golem is immune to poison and psychic damage and resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to exhaustion and to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

action.name: Bash
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Resonant Hum (Recharge 6)
entries: The golem hums toward one target it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 10 WIS save or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Each magic item within 5 feet of the target glows blue until the start of the golem’s next turn.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The pelagic dragonette can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Underwater Camouflage
entries: The pelagic dragonette’s Stealth is 19 while underwater.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Venom Burst (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The pelagic dragonette releases a burst of venom from its spines. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragonette must make a DC 14 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 14 (4d6) poison damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t poisoned. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

reaction.name: Poisoned Spines
entries: When a creature the pelagic dragonette can see within 5 feet of it hits it with an attack, the dragonette can twist its body and shove its spines into the attacker. The attacker takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) poison damage. PELAGIC DRAGONETTE FAMILIARS Some pelagic dragonettes are willing to serve spellcasters, especially if that spellcaster promises to expose the dragonette to novel experiences. Such dragonettes have the following trait.

reaction.name: Familiar
entries: The dragonette can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the dragonette senses as long as they are within 1 mile of each other. While the dragonette is within 10 feet of its companion, the companion can magically breathe both air and water. At any time and for any reason, the dragonette can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond. 115 D D Drake, Least The small potbellied dragon is about the size of a cat and has dull- yellow scales that seem vaguely slimy. Its rheumy eyes droop—as if the creature was on the verge of bursting into tears—and a wisp of sulfurous smoke drifts from its oversized nostrils.

reaction.name: Draconic Embarrassment
entries: Least drakes resemble miniature though oddly proportioned dragons: tiny limbs, too-small wings, potbellies, enormous snouts, and sickly yellow scales. They have only animalistic intelligence and are less magical than typical dragons. However, their potbellies house an alchemically fascinating and complex digestive tract.

reaction.name: Swampy Opportunists
entries: Least drakes live in sodden wetlands where they feed on anything they can catch and swallow, fueling the alchemical nightmare in their bellies. Though most of their diet consists of small animals, rotten wood, and various swamp plants, they are not averse to adding humanoids that trespass on their ill-hidden nests to the list. Lizardfolk, kobolds, and even the occasional noble keep domesticated least drakes as prestige pets and guard animals .

reaction.name: Sulfurous Bellies
entries: In the least drake’s stomach, the mélange of scavenged foods is purified into a highly flammable slurry, which it can exhale through its nose in a plume of noxious flame that propels the drake in the opposite direction and sickens surviving victims. This unstable concoction is prone to spontaneous detonation, especially when a drake is slain, and territorial displays between least drakes occasionally devolve into a chain of explosions and small brushfires. D D 116

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The phantasmid is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Forest Camouflage
entries: The phantasmid’s Stealth is 22 while in forest terrain.

trait.name: Terrifying Predator
entries: The phantasmid has advantage on melee attack rolls against frightened creatures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The phantasmid makes two Hooked Claw attacks and one Mandibles attack.

action.name: Hooked Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage. If this attack was against a surprised creature or a creature that didn’t see the phantasmid before this attack, the target takes an extra 3 (1d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Mandibles
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

action.name: Clattering Terror (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The phantasmid clicks its numerous legs together in a terrifying cacophony. Each creature within 30 feet of the phantasmid that can hear it must make a DC 15 WIS save. On a failure, a creature takes 28 (8d6) psychic damage and is frightened for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t frightened. A frightened creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Melt into Shadow
entries: The phantasmid teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see and takes the Hide action. The origin and destination must be in dim light or darkness. 233 P P

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The phibbit can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The phibbit is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Jumper
entries: The phibbit can fly up to 20 feet on its turn, but it must start and end its movement on a solid surface, such as a tree branch or the ground. If it is flying at the end of its turn, it falls to the ground and takes falling damage.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The phibbit has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The phibbit makes two Claw attacks and one Tongue attack, or it makes two Sparkle Bolt attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage. P P 234 Tongue. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.

action.name: Sparkle Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) radiant damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The phibbit casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using CHA as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13). At will: dancing lights , minor illusion 3/day each: invisibility (self only), silent image 1/day each: major image

bonus.name: Hypnotic Stare
entries: The phibbit’s eyes flash and ripple with bright colors in a hypnotic display. One creature within 30 feet of the phibbit that can see it must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be charmed for 10 minutes. The charmed creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the creature’s save is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the phibbit’s Hypnotic Stare for the next 24 hours.

reaction.name: Reactive Leap
entries: When a creature the phibbit can see attacks it, the phibbit can leap up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space it can see without provoking opportunity attacks. If this moves the phibbit out of range of the attack, the attack fails. Phoenix The air becomes suddenly thick with an intense heat as a massive, flaming bird lands, obsidian talons clacking on the ground. It lets out a piercing screech.

reaction.name: Future in the Flames
entries: Within its swirling, opalescent eyes, the phoenix beholds visions of the future. An oracle and purifier, it seeks a balance and harmony in nature and celebrates sustainable order. And it’s willing to kill in order to keep and expand such an environment.

reaction.name: Complicated Provincial Overseer
entries: Forever believing it has a right to guide events, the immortal phoenix often seeks to affect or adjust events in the region it inhabits. It grants boons to those who perform tasks in support of the desirable futures it sees and punishes those who act in opposition to them. A phoenix might serve as a potent ally to adventurers, but it can easily turn if the futures it sees make it necessary.

reaction.name: Curative Pinions
entries: Distinctly aware of its talents, the phoenix sometimes offers its feathers as boons. The feathers are known for their curative and protective properties, but they often prove ineffective if claimed from the ashes of a phoenix killed in combat. A PHOENIX’S LAIR A phoenix typically has multiple hidden nests high on mountaintops, plateaus, or rocky spires, and it regularly moves between them, keeping constant vigil over its territory. Because of this, a phoenix doesn’t have a true lair, but its presence still has an impact on the area it claims as its territory. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region a phoenix claims as its territory is suffused with its magic, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Healing Presence. Creatures in the phoenix’s territory have advantage on saves against diseases and poisons. • Oracular Mastery. When a creature casts a divination ritual spell within the phoenix’s territory, the casting time is halved, and if the ritual has a duration longer than Instantaneous, its duration is doubled. • Shared Rebirth. When a creature casts a ritual spell that returns a creature to life, such as the raise dead spell, within the phoenix’s territory, the casting time and material component cost are halved. These effects fade 1d10 days after the phoenix or its egg leaves the area. 235 P P

trait.name: Fiery Rebirth
entries: When it dies, the phoenix bursts into ashes and leaves behind a Small cinder-like egg deep within the ashes. The egg hatches after 24 hours, regaining all the phoenix’s memories and becoming active again. For the next 30 days, it uses the statistics of a fire-infused giant eagle (see Templates in Game Master’s Guide ) with this trait and the Fire Aura trait, then grows into an adult phoenix. Only a wish spell can prevent this trait from functioning.

trait.name: Fire Aura
entries: At the start of each of the phoenix’s turns, each creature within 10 feet of it takes 7 (2d6) fire damage, and flammable objects in the aura that aren’t being worn or carried ignite. The phoenix decides whether this aura is active at the start of its turn.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The phoenix doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy’s reach.

trait.name: Heightened Sight
entries: The phoenix’s Perception is 24 when perceiving by sight.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the phoenix fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The phoenix has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The monstrosity is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Read the Future
entries: The phoenix can spend 1 minute communing with the world and fate on behalf of a creature (which can include itself) within 10 feet of it or on an object within 10 feet of it. The creature can ask up to three questions concerning up to three specific goals, events, or activities to occur within 7 days. At the end of the minute, the phoenix pronounces the results of the creature’s inquiries. For creatures, this trait works like the divination spell, except it can’t be used to answer a specific creature’s questions more than once every 3 days. For objects, this trait works like both the identify and legend lore spells.

trait.name: Unquenchable Fire
entries: Creatures resistant to fire damage aren’t resistant to the fire damage dealt by the phoenix. A creature immune to fire damage is still immune to the phoenix’s fire damage. P P 236

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The phoenix makes one Beak attack and two Talon attacks, or it makes three Fire Spit attacks.

action.name: Beak
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) fire damage.

action.name: Talon
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Fire Spit
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (5d6 + 5) fire damage. If the target is a flammable creature or object, it ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the target takes 3 (1d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

action.name: Flame Wave (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The phoenix flaps its wings, releasing a wave of wind and fire in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 STR save. On a failure, a creature takes 52 (15d6) fire damage and is pushed up to 15 feet away from the phoenix. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed.

bonus.name: Restorative Pinion (Recharge 4–6)
entries: The phoenix touches another creature within 15 feet of it with the tip of its outstretched wing. The target magically regains 20 (4d8 + 2) HP and is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

reaction.name: Saw it Coming
entries: When a creature the phoenix can see attacks it, the phoenix can call on its prescience to see the movement of the attack before the attack hits, imposing disadvantage on the attack roll.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The phoenix automatically detects every creature and trap within 30 feet of it, pinpointing the current location of each.

legendary.name: Flaming Wing Buffet (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The phoenix beats its wings. Each creature within 15 feet of the phoenix must succeed on a DC 18 DEX save or take 10 (3d6) fire damage and be knocked prone. The phoenix can then fly up to half its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Prescient Screech (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The phoenix screeches a fragment of the thousands of futures it has beheld into the minds of up to three creatures it can see within 60 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 18 CHA save or be stunned until the end of its next turn, as its mind is overwhelmed by these fragments of knowledge.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The phytotitan is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Sticky Dew
entries: The phytotitan excretes a sticky dew from the fronds along its sail and back. A Medium or smaller creature that touches the phytotitan adheres to it and is also grappled (escape DC 17). Until this grapple ends, the creature moves with the phytotitan when it moves. The phytotitan can have up to four Large or smaller creatures adhered to it at one time. Ability checks made to escape this grapple have disadvantage.

trait.name: Withering Fronds
entries: Each time the phytotitan takes poison damage, one creature grappled by it is freed, as the fronds holding it wither. The phytotitan can choose which creature is freed if it is grappling more than one.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The phytotitan makes two Claw attacks and one Tail attack.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target.

action.name: Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) slashing damage
entries: If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is subjected to the phytotitan’s Sticky Dew trait.

action.name: Tail
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 17 STR save or be pulled up to 10 feet closer to the phytotitan.

bonus.name: Decomposing Fronds
entries: The phytotitan wraps life-draining fronds around one creature it is grappling. The target must succeed on a DC 17 STR save or be restrained by the fronds until the grapple ends. While restrained in this way, the target loses 5 (2d4) HP at the start of each of its turns, and the phytotitan regains HP equal to that amount.

reaction.name: Sticky Fronds
entries: When a Medium or smaller creature hits the phytotitan with an attack while within 10 feet of it, the phytotitan can twist its body to expose its sticky fronds. The attacker must succeed on a DC 17 STR save or be subjected to the phytotitan’s Sticky Dew trait. 237 P P Piranha Lotus A cluster of blue-green lily pads floats atop the lake’s surface. Long, delicate stems rise from the pads, ending in bright, colorful lotus flowers seemingly made of sharp glass.

reaction.name: Toothy Flowers
entries: Those unfamiliar with piranha lotuses might consider themselves lucky to stumble upon a patch of these plants. Stunningly beautiful, their wide, vine-fringed circular leaves of green and blue float on the water while their long, vertical stems end in colorful, iridescent flowers that could be made of glass. The lotuses are harmless on their own, but when they gather in groups, they can devastate an area. Those who approach for a closer look are swiftly taught the error of their ways as the lotuses cluster around, using their vines to pull prey toward the flowers—and to the sharp-edged petals surrounding the toothy maw at the center of each.

reaction.name: Feeding Frenzy
entries: Piranha lotuses can detect blood in the water around them, which sends them into a frenzy, primed to devour any creature within reach. Though the lotuses don’t move swiftly, they will follow any blood trail they sense.

reaction.name: Warm Environments
entries: The piranha lotus is usually found in warm and slow-moving coastal or swampy environments where they can float on the water, attracting prey without being disturbed. They are also especially sensitive to extreme cold, which can rupture their water - filled tissues and shatter their petals.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The planewort can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Elemental Adaptation
entries: If the planewort spends at least 1 minute in a particular type of terrain or plane of existence, such as swamp or Plane of Fire, its body adapts to that location’s dangers. It becomes immune to one of the following damage types, whichever is most appropriate for the location: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder. In addition, it gains a burrowing, climbing, flying, or swimming speed of 40 feet, or it gains two of those at 20 feet each. If it gains a flying speed, it can hover and is immune to the prone condition. P P 242 Elemental Traveler. Difficult terrain composed of nonmagical material native to the terrain the planewort is currently adapted to (see the Elemental Adaptation trait) doesn’t cost the planewort extra movement.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The planewort is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The planewort makes two Slam or Elemental Bolt attacks. If both Slam attacks hit one creature, the target is pushed up to 10 feet away from the planewort or restrained by the surrounding terrain until the end of its next turn (the planewort’s choice).

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning plus 7 (2d6) damage of the type noted in the Elemental Adaptation trait.

action.name: Elemental Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) damage of the type noted in the Elemental Adaptation trait.

bonus.name: Call to Terrain
entries: The planewort hums a tune from the birth of the planes, causing the terrain to rumble or swirl. The area within 10 feet of the planewort becomes difficult terrain until the start of its next turn, moving with it when it moves. The planewort can use this only if it is in the terrain associated with its Elemental Adaptation (see trait).

reaction.name: Terrain Meld
entries: When a creature the planewort can see attacks it, the planewort can meld with the terrain beneath or around it, reducing the damage from the attack by 5 (2d4). It can use this only if it is in the terrain associated with its Elemental Adaptation (see trait). Psylocite The limbs extending from the creature’s glowing, crystalline form seem to consist of some form of ectoplasm. Calming blue light spills from its body, drawing the eye and dulling the senses.

reaction.name: Astral Psychics
entries: Psylocites are psychic aberrations from the Astral Plane, where they find or create small portals into the Material Plane near humanoid settlements, drawn by the chaotic thoughts and dreams of its inhabitants. From there, the psylocites grow their colony, sending splinters and shards out to slowly and subtly take over the populace. They seek to restructure chaotic humanoid societies to match their own idealized hierarchies, even going so far as to rewrite local history. Their revisionist efforts emphasize events and figures that promote order and homogeneity while also diminishing chaotic and individualistic elements—and of course painting psylocites in the most beneficent light.

reaction.name: Rigid Colonies
entries: Psylocite colonies are rigidly hierarchical: each is led by a single star, who is served directly by no more than one hundred shards, each of which is in turn served by no more than one hundred splinters. If a shard becomes a star through its advancement, it breaks away from the colony and travels to form a new colony elsewhere in the Astral Plane, opening a connection to a different humanoid settlement on any of the countless possible worlds. In rare cases, multiple colonies will cooperate in a loose network led by a council composed of each colony’s star. Experiential Growth. Psylocite advancement is based on the knowledge and complex experiences gained through the telepathic bonds they create with humanoids. A splinter grows and advances to become a shard after it spends sixty full days bonded to at least ten different humanoids. A shard advances into a star after it spends three years bonded to at least one thousand different humanoids. Once a psylocite reaches the apex of its evolution as a star, it ceases growing and instead can choose to break off a new splinter after every hundred days of being bonded to at least one humanoid, provided its colony has fewer than ten thousand splinters. While stars can regularly create splinters, many splinters and stars can go years connected to only a handful of humanoids, experiencing all they can with those humanoids before moving on. This tendency keeps most colonies relatively small and slow growing, and it often endears those humanoids to the psylocites, viewing the aberrations less as mental invaders and more as close friends who share in their deepest secrets.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The chuul is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The chuul can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Sense Magic
entries: The chuul senses and can pinpoint the location of magic within 120 feet of it. If it senses magic and can see the creature or object bearing the magic it senses, it sees a faint aura around that creature or object.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The chuul potentate makes three Magic-Infused

action.name: Pincer or Force Bolt attacks
entries: If two Magic-Infused Pincer attacks hit one creature that isn’t grappled by the potentate, the target is knocked prone.

action.name: Magic-Infused Pincer
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) force damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 17). The potentate has two pincers, each of which can grapple only one target.

action.name: Force Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +10 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) force damage.

action.name: Force Bomb (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The chuul potentate sends a surge of arcane energy into a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target emits a dim glow that pulses rhythmically, pulsing faster as the target’s turn approaches. At the end of the target’s next turn, the energy explodes out from it, and the target must make a DC 17 CON save. On a failure, it takes 66 (12d10) force damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half the damage and isn’t frightened. The damage the target takes is split evenly between the target and each creature within 10 feet of it that isn’t an Aberration.

bonus.name: Paralyzing Tentacles
entries: One creature grappled by the chuul potentate must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute. Until this poison ends, the creature is paralyzed. A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

reaction.name: Magic-Hardened Shell
entries: When a creature the chuul potentate can see attacks it, the potentate can shift some of its magical power to its shell, reinforcing its body. It adds 5 to its AC against the attack. 73 C C Clockworks Though seemingly composed entirely of brass and iron, the subtle ticking from the mechanical being’s body is likely the only warning a victim might ever get.

reaction.name: Ticking Servants
entries: Clockwork creatures are constructs commonly found in urban areas supporting large populations of tinkerers, crafters, and mechanists. Though requiring great skill, they can be fairly inexpensive to make and maintain, and unlike with many constructs, they can learn to serve new masters or even strike out on their own—depending on their level of autonomy and self- awareness. Clockwork constructs are typically able to at least follow orders, make judgment calls within the bounds of those orders, and report back to their superiors.

reaction.name: Valued Guardians and Killers
entries: Clockwork creatures are commonly used as supplemental members of a city watch, particularly for assignments or shifts their humanoid counterparts don’t want. Some wealthier individuals hire mechanists to create more elaborate and deadly constructs as personal bodyguards and assassins, and many alchemists make or commission clockwork guards filled with dangerous substances.

reaction.name: Wondrous Crafting and Labor
entries: While many clockwork constructs are built for vigilance and violence, they are also finding a growing aptitude for skilled labor. This is possibly most notable in the rise of the use of clockwork constructors for construction and demolition. Even such specialized constructs can be repurposed and they are often prime targets for criminal use, such as constructors being hijacked to rip apart buildings or crush squads of guards.

monster.name: Psylocite Shard
languages: understands Common but can’t speak, telepathy

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: As the splinter.

trait.name: Calming Light
entries: As the splinter, except the radius is 20 feet, the die is a d6, the save DC is 16, and the creature is soothed for 1 minute. The affected creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The psylocite shard makes three Psychic Blast attacks.

action.name: Psychic Blast
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) psychic damage. Instead of dealing damage, the shard can learn a piece of information or memory from the target’s mind, such as where it lives or the face of its beloved. P P 244 Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6). The shard sends out a pulse of psychic energy, rattling the minds of those nearby. Each creature within 20 feet of the shard must make a DC 16 WIS save. On a failure, a creature takes 24 (7d6) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t stunned.

bonus.name: Psychic Bond
entries: As the splinter, except the save DC is 16, and the target must be more than 1 mile away from the shard to attempt to end the bond. The shard can have up to three Humanoids bonded to it at a time.

bonus.name: Psychic Study
entries: The shard studies the mental patterns of one creature it can see within 60 feet of it, gaining advantage on the next attack roll against the target or the next save against the target’s features and spells before the start of the shard’s next turn. Alternatively, the shard can attempt to erase or rewrite a memory, if the target is a Humanoid. The target must succeed on a DC 16 CHA save or the shard erases or modifies up to 1 minute of the target’s memory of an event it experienced within the last 24 hours. A bonded target automatically fails this save. Once the shard has erased or modified a creature’s memory, it can’t do so to that creature again for the next 24 hours. A remove curse or greater restoration spell cast on the target restores the creature’s true memory.

reaction.name: Darting Escape
entries: When the shard takes damage, it can fly up to half its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

monster.name: Psylocite Splinter
languages: understands Common but can’t speak, telepathy

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The splinter is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Calming Light
entries: The psylocite sheds a dim, blue light in a 10-foot radius that calms and dulls the senses of nearby Humanoids. Each Humanoid that starts its turn in the light must succeed on a DC 13 CHA save or be soothed by the light until the start of its next turn. While soothed in this way, the creature has disadvantage on WIS (Perception) checks, and when it makes an attack roll, it rolls a d4 and subtracts the number rolled from the attack roll. At the start of each of its turns, the psylocite chooses if this light is active.

action.name: Psychic Spark
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) psychic damage. Instead of dealing damage, the splinter can learn one small piece of information or memory from the target’s mind, such as its favorite color or its childhood pet. 243 P P

bonus.name: Psychic Bond (3/Day)
entries: The splinter forms a psychic bond with a Humanoid it can see within 30 feet of it that is affected by its Calming Light. The target must succeed on a DC 13 WIS save or be psychically bonded to the splinter for 24 hours or until the splinter dies. A creature can choose to fail this save. While bonded, the splinter ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with the target—provided the two are on the same plane of existence—adds its PB to any ability check the target is proficient in, and learns any information the target learns while bonded. In addition, the target automatically succeeds on saves against any psylocite’s Calming Light, and it views the splinter as a trusted ally. While more than 30 feet away from the splinter, the target can take its action to forcefully end the bond early by succeeding on a DC 13 WIS save. The splinter can have only one Humanoid bonded to it at a time. If it bonds with another, the bond on the previous target ends.

reaction.name: Darting Escape
entries: When the splinter takes damage, it can fly up to half its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

monster.name: Psylocite Star
languages: understands all languages but can’t speak,

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: As the splinter.

trait.name: Calming Light
entries: As the splinter, except the radius is 30 feet, the die is a d8, the save DC is 19, and the creature is soothed as long as it remains in the light and for 1 minute after leaving the light. If it is outside the light, it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The star makes three Psychic Blast attacks.

action.name: Psychic Blast
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 34 (8d6 + 6) psychic damage. Instead of dealing damage, the star can learn a hidden piece of information, deep secret, or cherished memory from the target’s mind, such as the target’s deepest fear or the last time it saw a dying loved one.

action.name: Controlled Bond
entries: The star attempts to take full control of a Humanoid it can see within 60 feet of it that is bonded to it. The target must succeed on a DC 19 CHA save or be under the star’s complete control for 24 hours. This effect otherwise works like the greater dominate spell, except the target can repeat the save to end this effect only if it receives a suicidal command or if it takes damage while below half its HP maximum. The star can have full control over only one of its bonded Humanoids at a time.

action.name: Telekinesis
entries: The star casts the telekinesis spell (spell save DC 19), requiring no verbal components and using INT as the spellcasting ability.

action.name: Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The star sends out a pulse of psychic energy, rattling the minds of those nearby. Each creature within 30 feet of the shard must make a DC 19 WIS save. On a failure, a creature takes 56 (16d6) psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t stunned. A stunned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Astral Leap (3/Day)
entries: The star transports itself to the Astral

action.name: Plane from the Material Plane or vice versa
entries: This works like the plane shift spell, except it can affect only itself and can’t use this action to banish an unwilling creature.

bonus.name: Psychic Bond
entries: As the splinter, except the save DC is 19, the bond lasts indefinitely, and the target must spend at least 7 days more than 1 mile away from the star to attempt to end the bond. The star can have up to ten Humanoids bonded to it at a time.

bonus.name: Psychic Study
entries: As the shard, except the save DC is 19, and it can erase or modify up to 10 minutes of the target’s memories of an event it experienced within the last 7 days.

reaction.name: Preserve the Colony
entries: When the star takes damage, it can magically teleport, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. 245 P P

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The Pumpkin King is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.
