entries: The ant makes two Bite attacks. If both attacks hit one creature and that creature is poisoned after both attacks resolve, the target is also paralyzed for the duration.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) poison damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13

action.name: CON save or be poisoned for 1 minute
entries: A poisoned creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

bonus.name: Drain Larvae
entries: The vampire ant siphons lifeforce from a swarm of vampire ant larvae within 5 feet of it. If the swarm has temporary HP, it loses up to 5 (2d4) temporary HP, and the ant regains HP equal to that amount.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The veiled passenger is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Closed Mind
entries: The veiled passenger is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts.

trait.name: One with the Masses
entries: When hiding or blending into urban areas, the veiled passenger uses its CHA instead of DEX for a Stealth of 16.

trait.name: Psychic Veil
entries: While not incapacitated or actively threatening or harming another creature, the veiled passenger projects a psychic aura around itself that makes it seem mundane. If the veiled passenger doesn’t look the part, the observer’s mind fills in any gaps, such as justifying odd attire as standard foreign clothing. A creature that observes the veiled passenger for at least 1 minute can take its action to see the truth by succeeding on a DC 14 INT check.

trait.name: Telekineticist
entries: The veiled passenger can psychically move and manipulate objects that aren’t being worn or carried within 30 feet of it, weighing up to 285 pounds and moving an object no more than 15 feet each round. It can’t move creatures, but it can use this to slow or stop its fall or to float through the air at half its speed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The veiled passenger makes three Psychic Blade attacks.

action.name: Psychic Blade
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) psychic damage.

action.name: Mindwave (Recharge 5–6)
entries: A shockwave of psychic energy bursts from the veiled passenger. Each creature within 15 feet of it must make a DC 14 CHA save. On a failure, a creature takes 21 (6d6) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t stunned.

reaction.name: Psychic Grab
entries: When a creature the veiled passenger can see within 60 feet of it attacks it with a weapon, the passenger can lash out psychically at the weapon, imposing disadvantage on the attack roll. 301 V V

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The veilworm is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Obscuring Fog
entries: The veilworm emits a fog within 1 mile of it that follows it, moves with it, and lightly obscures the area. Creatures within 60 feet of the veilworm can’t see beyond 20 feet, and the veilworm can sense the general direction of any creature in the fog. If dispersed, the fog reappears at the start of the veilworm’s next turn. V V 302 Otherworldly Bond. Veilworms share a magical bond while within 60 feet of each other. If one veilworm succeeds on a save, all bonded veilworms also succeed, and if one veilworm senses something, all bonded veilworms sense it. In addition, a veilworm can’t be banished, teleported, or similarly moved away from its bonded allies unless that effect targets all bonded veilworms.

trait.name: Otherworldly Nature
entries: The veilworm doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Protecting Fog (54 HP or Fewer)
entries: The fog within 5 feet of the veilworm thickens, and it’s heavily obscured.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The veilworm makes three Gore attacks. If two Gore attacks hit a Medium or smaller creature, the veilworm impales the target with its horn, grappling the target (escape DC 15). The veilworm can have only one creature impaled at a time.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Swift Hunter
entries: The veilworm moves up to half its speed toward a hostile creature it can see. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

bonus.name: Throw
entries: A creature impaled by the veilworm is thrown up to 30 feet in a random direction and knocked prone. If a thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

reaction.name: Bonded Guard
entries: When a bonded ally the veilworm can see is attacked, the veilworm can move up to 20 feet toward that ally without provoking opportunity attacks. If it ends this movement within 5 feet of the ally, the veilworm becomes the target of the attack instead.

trait.name: Divine Blessing
entries: The priest is resistant to necrotic damage or radiant damage, as appropriate for the priest’s deity.

trait.name: Divine Weapons
entries: The venture priest’s weapons are shrouded in dark or golden flames, as appropriate for the priest’s deity. When the venture priest hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 3d8 necrotic damage or radiant damage (included in the attack), the priest’s choice.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The venture priest makes two Morningstar or Divine Bolt attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Morningstar
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage or radiant damage (the priest’s choice).

action.name: Divine Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) necrotic damage or radiant damage (the priest’s choice).

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The venture priest casts one of the following spells, using WIS as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15). At will: guidance , light , thaumaturgy 3/day each: bane , bless , command , cure wounds 2/day each: dispel magic , hold 1/day each: freedom of movement

bonus.name: Divine Castigation
entries: The venture priest presents its holy symbol, calling down divine wrath upon one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 WIS save or attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of the priest’s next turn.

reaction.name: Protective Blessing
entries: When a creature the venture priest can see within 30 feet of it attacks it, the priest can call out to its deity for aid, increasing its AC by 3 against that attack. If the attack hits, the attacker takes 4 (1d8) necrotic damage or radiant damage (the priest’s choice).

trait.name: Pounce
entries: If the dragon moves at least 15 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Claw attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the dragon can make one Claw attack against it as a bonus action.

trait.name: Woodland Walk
entries: Difficult terrain composed of nonmagical plants doesn’t cost the dragon extra movement. In addition, the dragon can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Pollen Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The dragon exhales a cloud of pollen in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 11 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 18 (4d8) poison damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Distracting Breath (Recharge 6)
entries: The dragon exhales a sweet-smelling gas in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 11 CHA save or be distracted for 1 minute. When a distracted creature casts a spell, it must succeed on a DC 11 CHA save or be unable to cast the spell, using the action, bonus action, or reaction to cast the spell but not expending the spell slot.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The vikalver can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: The vikalver is resistant to the charmed and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Shape Water
entries: Unless it is in an arid climate, the vikalver can spend 1 minute creating an orb of water or ice in its hand, shaping the liquid into a nonmagical weapon, set of tools, or other mundane item. The item can be no larger than a 5-foot cube and lasts for 1 hour. The vikalver can have no more than three weapons, sets of tools, or other items created in this way at one time.

trait.name: Watery Weapons
entries: The vikalver's weapon attacks are magical. When the vikalver hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 3d6 cold damage (included in the attack).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The vikalver makes two Handaxe or Water Bolt attacks.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) cold damage.

action.name: Water Blast
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.

bonus.name: Wind Burst
entries: The vikalver sends a burst of wind at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the vikalver and knocked prone.

reaction.name: Underhanded Riposte
entries: The vikalver adds 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the vikalver must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon. If the triggering attack misses and the attacker is within 5 feet of it, the vikalver can kick, punch, or headbutt the attacker, dealing 5 (2d4) bludgeoning damage. 303 V V

monster.name: Viridian Queen
languages: understands Deep Speech but can’t speak,

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The viridian queen is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Corrupt Apportation
entries: A creature within 120 feet of the viridian queen that casts a conjuration spell takes 10 (3d6) force damage, or twice as much damage if the spell teleports a creature.

trait.name: Portal Sense
entries: The viridian queen can pinpoint the location of planar portals, teleportation circles, or similar magical gateways within 100 miles of it.

trait.name: Otherworldly Nature
entries: The viridian queen doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The viridian queen makes four Tentacle attacks. It can replace one attack with Dissolution. V V 304 Tentacle. Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) force damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 18), if it is a Medium or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and has disadvantage on CON saves to maintain concentration on spells. The queen can have up to four creatures grappled at a time.

action.name: Dissolution
entries: The viridian queen sends reality-rending energy through one creature grappled by it. The target must make a DC 18 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 28 (8d6) force damage and can’t cast spells until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and can still cast spells. A creature reduced to 0 HP is disintegrated, reducing the creature and everything it is wearing or carrying, except magic items, to a pile of dust. The creature can be restored to life only by means of a true resurrection or wish spell.

bonus.name: Liminal Step
entries: The viridian queen teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. If the origin or destination space is within 5 feet of a corner, threshold, or similar liminal space, the queen gains 10 (3d6) temporary HP.

reaction.name: Banish to Nowhere
entries: When a creature the viridian queen can see within 120 feet of it deals damage to it, the queen can banish that creature to a harmless demiplane. The target must succeed on a DC 18 CHA save or be banished and incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Void Harbinger

reaction.name: A tall, gray figure stands atop a promontory
entries: Its onyx eyes weep black, oily tears, and its overlarge mouth opens to reveal too many needle-sharp teeth. Shadowy tendrils rise from its back like wings, and four arms stretch out, holding an immense maul and void energy.

reaction.name: Precedes the Void
entries: The creature generally known as the void harbinger has many names: The Last Cacophony, the Final Chorus, the Twilight Mourner, and the Devastator of Light. Void harbingers appear on worlds about to be consumed by the Void to prepare the way and, some say, to mourn for the world’s eventual end, which many believe to be the cause of the oily, black tears the harbinger constantly weeps. Though the Void is silent, the harbinger is accompanied by a ghostly chorus of disembodied, horrifying sounds that maddeningly move and shift—a susurrus of whispers, chittering, pain-filled screams, the sound of weeping, and more. Some call these the last gasp of the world about to be consumed while others think them the remnants of those already consumed by the Void.

reaction.name: Devastation Personified
entries: Void harbingers facilitate a world’s fall to the Void by combatting and slaying its greatest defenders, supported by a host of void-touched creatures that swarm the populace. The harbinger also wreaks havoc on the landscape, weakening a world’s planar boundaries with rifts to the Void.

reaction.name: Void Rifts
entries: The void harbinger’s key power is its ability to tear open rifts to the Void. Minor tears stay open briefly, allowing the harbinger to channel Void energy at its enemies, summon void-touched servitors, or destroy local terrain. After establishing a foothold, a void harbinger can summon larger forces and cause expanding damage to the surrounding terrain. When all resistance on a world has been eliminated, the harbinger causes the rifts to grow and proliferate, a process that ultimately ends with the utter consumption of the world. REGIONAL EFFECTS A void harbinger has no true lair, but the region where it secures a foothold in a world is altered by its void energy, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Before the Silence. Unsettling sounds randomly echo within the area claimed as the harbinger’s foothold. These sounds spook wildlife, making hunting nearly impossible in the area, and unnerve most humanoids. • Sudden Decay. Nonmagical plants within the area claim as the harbinger’s foothold shrivel and decay within 7 days of the foothold being established, losing their color and vitality. • Void Patches. Areas of darkness and extreme cold measuring 100 feet to a side accumulate throughout the area claimed as the harbinger’s foothold. Nonmagical light doesn’t work in these areas, and a creature that spends at least 1 hour in such an area suffers the effects of extreme cold (see Player’s Guide ). These effects fade 1d6 days after the void harbinger dies or leaves the area for at least 24 hours.

trait.name: Embodiment of the Void
entries: Creatures resistant to necrotic damage aren’t resistant to necrotic damage dealt by the void harbinger. A creature immune to necrotic damage is still immune to the harbinger’s necrotic damage.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the void harbinger fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Unsettling Cacophony
entries: The void harbinger is surrounded by disturbing sounds. A creature that can hear that starts its turn within 60 feet of the void harbinger must succeed on a DC 20 WIS save or be frightened until the start of its next turn. Unless surprised, a creature can cover or plug its ears to avoid the save at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can’t hear, and while covering its ears with its hands, it can’t use its hands for other tasks, such as wielding weapons or casting spells. A creature can plug its ears with cloth or similar material as a bonus action. If the creature stops covering or plugging its ears while within 60 feet of the harbinger, it must immediately make the save.

trait.name: Void Dweller
entries: The void harbinger doesn’t require air, food, drink, sleep, or ambient pressure, and it is immune to the effects of Void terrain. While traveling in space, the harbinger magically glides on solar winds, covering immense distances in short times.

trait.name: Void-Touched Weapons
entries: The void harbinger’s weapon attacks are magical. When the void harbinger hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 3d8 necrotic damage (included in the attack). 305 V V

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The void harbinger makes two Maul attacks and two Claw attacks, or it makes four Void Bolt attacks. If two Claw or Void Bolt attacks hit a creature, the target’s HP maximum is reduced by 13 (3d8). This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Maul
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (4d6 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Void Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +13 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 29 (5d8 + 7) necrotic damage.

action.name: Void Servitors
entries: The void harbinger magically calls 3 lesser voidlings or negalzyn , 1 golmana demon , or 1 voidling (all found in this book or Monster Vault ). The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the void harbinger and obeying its spoken commands. The called creatures remain for 1 hour, until the void harbinger dies, or until the void harbinger dismisses them as a bonus action. The void harbinger can have any number of called creatures under its control at one time, provided the combined total CR of the creatures is no higher than 12.

action.name: Void Conduit (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The void harbinger claws open a small rift to the Void, releasing

action.name: Void energy in a 60 - foot cone
entries: Each creature in that area must make a DC 20 DEX save, taking 63 (14d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 HP, it is disintegrated, reducing the creature and everything it is wearing or carrying, except magic items, to a pile of dust. The creature can be restored to life only by means of a true resurrection or a wish spell.

bonus.name: Void Visions
entries: The void harbinger fills the mind of a creature it can see within 60 feet of it with jumbled visions of the Void. The target must succeed on a DC 20 WIS save or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Void Warp
entries: The void harbinger teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. A void rift opens at the origin and destination when it uses this bonus action.

reaction.name: Void Blessing
entries: When a friendly creature the void harbinger can see within 30 feet of it hits another creature with a weapon attack, the void harbinger can cause that attack to deal an extra 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. V V 306

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The void harbinger automatically detects every creature and trap within 60 feet of it, pinpointing the current location of each.

legendary.name: Call Servitors (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The void harbinger uses Void Servitors.

legendary.name: Wing Tendrils (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The void harbinger spreads its shadowy wing tendrils, lashing out at nearby creatures. Each creature within 15 feet of the harbinger must succeed on a DC 20 DEX save or take 9 (2d8) necrotic damage and have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

legendary.name: Void Incursion (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The void harbinger summons the taint of the Void on a point on the ground it can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 20 CON save or take 7 (2d6) cold damage and 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. The area then permanently becomes difficult terrain.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The void troll is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The void troll’s Perception is 18 while perceiving by smell.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The void troll has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The void troll regains 10 HP at the start of its turn. If the troll takes fire or radiant damage, this trait doesn’t function at the start of the troll’s next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 HP and doesn’t regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The void troll makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks, or it makes three Void Bolt attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

action.name: Void Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (5d6 + 3) necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Leaking Void (76 HP or Fewer)
entries: The void troll’s wounds leak void energy, and the troll channels it in one of the following ways: • Void Fatigue. One creature the void troll can see within 15 feet of it must succeed on a DC 16 CON save or its speed is halved until the start of the troll’s next turn. • Void Glimpse. One creature the void troll can see within 15 feet of it must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or be frightened until the start of the troll’s next turn. • Void Shroud. Melee attacks against the troll are made with disadvantage until the start of its next turn. 293 T T

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The voltaic newt can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The voltaic newt is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The voltaic newt makes one Bite attack and one Tail Slap attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Tail Slap
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) lightning damage.

action.name: Electric Discharge (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The newt releases an electrical charge. Each creature within 10 feet of it (if on land) or 20 feet of it (if in water) must make a DC 13 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (3d6) lightning damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated.

reaction.name: Spark
entries: When a creature deals damage to the voltaic newt while within 15 feet of it, the newt can send a spark of lightning at the creature. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) lightning damage. VARIANT: RADIANT NEWT During a trip to the Material Plane long ago, an angel fell in love with the adorable voltaic newt and brought dozens back home as pets. The angel was eventually commanded to return the newts, who had unknowingly been changed by the celestial realms’ radiant power. Radiant newts typically inhabit river deltas and oases in sun-soaked regions. A radiant newt is resistant to the blinded condition instead of incapacitated and replaces all instances of lightning damage in its statistics with radiant damage. In addition, it replaces the voltaic newt’s Electric Discharge action with the following: Blinding Beam (Recharge 5–6). The newt exhales brilliant energy in a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 13 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (3d6) radiant damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t blinded. 307 V V

trait.name: Abrasive Body
entries: A creature that touches the vulkeen or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 2 (1d4) slashing damage.

trait.name: Elemental Nature
entries: The vulkeen doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: The vulkeen is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Fragile Weapon
entries: The vulkeen’s obsidian blade is fragile. If the vulkeen makes an attack with the blade and the die’s roll is a 1, the blade shatters and can’t be used again until the vulkeen forges a new one.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The vulkeen makes one Obsidian Blade attack and one Slam attack or two Slam attacks. Alternatively, it makes three Molten Rock attacks.

action.name: Obsidian Blade
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) slashing damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Molten Rock
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

bonus.name: Lava Burst
entries: The vulkeen calls lava to bubble up from a point on the ground it can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature on the ground within 10 feet of that point must make a DC 16 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 7 (2d6) fire damage and is restrained until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t restrained.

reaction.name: Seeping Smoke
entries: When the vulkeen takes damage, it can force smoke to briefly seep from its wounds. Each creature within 10 feet of the vulkeen must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, as it chokes on the smoke.

trait.name: Giant Attributes
entries: The giant is resistant to the stunned condition, and it is vulnerable to the prone condition.

trait.name: Unshakeable Command
entries: Each friendly creature within 30 feet of the giant can’t be charmed or frightened while the giant isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The war giant makes two Battleaxe attacks and one Shield Smash attack.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 20 (3d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.

action.name: Shield Smash
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 STR save or be pushed up to 15 feet away from the giant and knocked prone.

action.name: Scatter Rocks (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The war giant tosses a handful of stones at a point on the ground it can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 24 (7d6) bludgeoning G G 156 damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The area then becomes difficult terrain for Large or smaller creatures for 1 minute.

bonus.name: Commander’s Orders
entries: The war giant calls out one of the following commands to up to three friendly creatures within 30 feet of it that can hear it: • Charge! Each target can immediately move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks and has advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the giant’s next turn. • Defensive Formation! Each target can immediately move up to half its speed toward the war giant without provoking opportunity attacks. Each target that ends this movement within 5 feet of the giant or another target of this command gains a +2 bonus to its AC until the start of the giant’s next turn. • Hold Steady! Each target can’t be pushed or knocked prone until the start of the giant’s next turn, and each target gains 7 (2d6) temporary HP.

trait.name: Charge
entries: If the war pig moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Gore attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 5 (2d4) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 12 STR save or be knocked prone.

trait.name: Heightened Smell
entries: The war pig’s Perception is 16 while perceiving by smell.

action.name: Gore
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage.

bonus.name: Frightful Squeal
entries: The war pig emits a loud, high-pitched squeal. Each Beast and Humanoid within 10 feet of the war pig must succeed on a DC 12 WIS save or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

monster.name: Warmwreath Lichen Swarm
senses: keensense 30 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the warmwreath lichen swarm remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary patch of lichen.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The warmwreath lichen swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny patch of lichen. The swarm can't regain HP or gain temporary HP.

trait.name: Swarm Resilience
entries: The swarm is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it is immune to the charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned conditions.

trait.name: Warmth Aura
entries: The warmwreath lichen swarm radiates heat. Creatures within 30 feet of the swarm are protected from the effects of extreme cold and similar frigid environmental hazards. A creature that starts its turn in the swarm’s space must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or take 4 (1d8) fire damage.

action.name: Tendrils
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm’s space. Hit: 14 (4d6) piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) fire damage, or 7 (2d6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) fire damage if the swarm has half of its HP or fewer. The target must succeed on a DC 14 CON save or contract a disease. Until the disease is cured, the target has disadvantage on DEX checks and saves. Every 24 hours that elapse, the infected creature must repeat the save, reducing its HP maximum by 7 (2d6) on a failure. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. The creature dies if the disease reduces its HP maximum to 0, and a new swarm emerges from the corpse after 7 days. The creature automatically succeeds on the save if it took cold damage within the past 24 hours. 309 V V Wasteborn Despoiler A figure with a humanoid torso astride an arachnid body emerges from the wastes. Its four arms each end in a three - fingered claw. A metal mask obscures all but its eyes.

action.name: Badlands Survivors
entries: There are ancient, otherworldly things hidden in the wastes of the world. The wastes are also home to outcasts and wanderers. When a wasteland wanderer stumbles upon one of these ancient entities, that entity awakens to whisper in the dark, offering power beyond the scraps the badlands provide. A person that agrees emerges transformed and burning with a hunger for conquest and destruction.

action.name: Two in One
entries: A wasteborn despoiler is a humanoid transformed by joining with an ancient intelligence trapped in badlands or magic-blasted wastelands. These ancient entities might have been wizards trapped by their own magical folly or forgotten deities trapped by rivals. This transformation leads to the two becoming one new entity. The ancient intelligence whispers in the back of the mind of the humanoid, driving the person to conquer and destroy while reveling in its new freedom.

action.name: Wasteland Commanders
entries: A wasteborn despoiler’s otherworldly power attracts other badlands denizens, forming them into a band of marauders. A powerful runner, the despoiler encourages its followers to build great vehicles or tame mighty mounts to keep the band highly mobile. In this way, the despoiler and its marauders can strike settlements and escape in a cloud of dust. The despoiler assumes a prominent position during raids so its followers, and its enemies, can see it and know their doom rides toward them . A WASTEBORN DESPOILER’S LAIR A wasteborn despoiler makes its lair in badlands, forming a remote encampment for it and its followers. The encampment is typically close to rocky outcroppings with a view of the surrounding area. When encountered in its lair, a wasteborn despoiler has a challenge rating of 21. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the wasteborn despoiler can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the wasteborn despoiler can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Castigating Terrain. The ground erupts on a point the wasteborn despoiler can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 20 DEX save or take 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The area then becomes difficult terrain until initiative count 20 on the next round. W W 310 • Detritus Barrage. A barrage of rocks, debris, and makeshift weapons strike a point the wasteborn despoiler can see within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 20 feet of that point must make a DC 20 DEX save, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (the despoiler’s choice) on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. • Dust Squall. A 30-foot-radius cloud of swirling dust coalesces centered on a point the wasteborn despoiler can see within 120 feet of it. The cloud spreads around corners. A creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 20 CON save or take 5 (2d4) slashing damage and be blinded until the end of its next turn. The despoiler can choose for any number of its allies to not be affected. The dust cloud lasts for 1 minute, until the despoiler uses this lair action again, or until the despoiler dies. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region containing a wasteborn despoiler’s lair is warped by its presence, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Dust Storms. Dust constantly swirls in storms within 3 miles of the despoiler’s lair. Creatures in the area, other than the despoiler’s followers, have disadvantage on WIS (Perception) checks that rely on vision. • Roiled Wildlife. Beasts and creatures with the Animal tag within 10 miles of the despoiler’s lair become excessively aggressive and randomly attack Humanoids. Such creatures that have been tamed by the despoiler or its followers aren’t affected. • Uncovered Secrets. Entrances leading to long-buried objects and creatures randomly open within 5 miles of the despoiler’s lair. If the wasteborn despoiler dies, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The wasteborn despoiler is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Badlands Strider
entries: Difficult terrain composed of sand, mud, or rock doesn’t cost the wasteborn despoiler extra movement. In addition, the despoiler leaves no tracks or other traces of its passage when moving through sandy, muddy, or rocky terrain.

trait.name: Eldritch Weapons
entries: The wasteborn despoiler’s weapon attacks are magical. When the despoiler hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 2d8 force damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the wasteborn despoiler fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The wasteborn despoiler has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Mighty Commander
entries: Each friendly creature within 30 feet of the wasteborn despoiler has advantage on the first attack roll it makes each round and can’t be charmed or frightened while the despoiler isn’t incapacitated.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The wasteborn despoiler can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wasteborn despoiler makes one Bite attack, one Pike attack, and two Leg attacks, or it makes four Eye Beam attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) force damage.

action.name: Pike
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) force damage.

action.name: Leg
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d12 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) force damage.

action.name: Eye Beam
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +12 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (5d8 + 6) force damage.

action.name: Scourging Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The wasteborn despoiler exhales otherworldly energy in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 20 DEX save, taking 72 (16d8) force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonus.name: Battlefield Maneuvers
entries: The wasteborn despoiler commands up to three friendly creatures it can see within 60 feet of it to move. Each target can use a reaction to move up to half its speed in a direction of the despoiler’s choice. This movement is unaffected by difficult terrain and doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

reaction.name: Brutal Backhand
entries: When a creature the wasteborn despoiler can see within 5 feet of it hits it with an attack, the despoiler can strike the attacker. The attacker must succeed on a DC 20 STR save or be knocked prone or pushed up to 15 feet away from the despoiler (the despoiler’s choice).

legendary.name: Empower Follower
entries: The wasteborn despoiler empowers the weapons of one friendly creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The next time that creature hits with a weapon attack before the end of its next turn, the weapon deals an extra 9 (2d8) force damage.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The despoiler moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Swiping Blitz (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wasteborn despoiler charges, swiping wildly with its claws. It moves up to 30 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Large or smaller creature without provoking opportunity attacks. Each creature in a space it moves into or within 5 feet of such a space must make a DC 19 STR save. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (3d6) slashing damage and is pushed up to 15 feet away from the despoiler’s path and knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t pushed or knocked prone. 311 W W

monster.name: Wax Golem
languages: understands the languages of its creator but can’t

trait.name: Construct Nature
entries: The golem doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: If the wax golem shares the likeness of a specific Humanoid, it is indistinguishable from that Humanoid while it remains motionless.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The golem’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Wax Golem Resilience
entries: The golem is immune to poison damage and resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to exhaustion and to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned conditions.

trait.name: Wax Splash
entries: When the golem takes fire damage, hot wax splashes on nearby creatures. Each creature within 5 feet of the golem must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or take 3 (1d6) fire damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wax golem makes two Slam attacks Slam. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Lob Wax
entries: The wax golem throws a gob of wax at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or its speed is halved until it or another creature takes an action to wipe off the wax. 165 G G Goreling s Bits and pieces of flesh and bone shuffle insistently forward.

bonus.name: Leftover Parts
entries: Gorelings are a necromancer’s answer when there just isn’t enough flesh around to create a full zombie. Since they are made of whatever is lying around, they come in a variety of shapes and sizes. When created, gorelings possess a tormented fragment of the dead creature’s soul, driving them to kill the living.

bonus.name: Uncontrolled Danger
entries: Gorelings tend to gather in swarms, but when they do, they are also harder to control. Necromancers often limit themselves to creating only a handful of gorelings at a time to avoid being overrun.

trait.name: Devil’s Sight
entries: Magical darkness doesn’t impede the waxworker devil’s darkvision.

trait.name: Devilish Resilience
entries: The waxworker devil is resistant to cold damage and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. In addition, it is immune to fire damage and poison damage and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The waxworker devil has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects. D D 100

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The waxworker devil makes three Sculpting Knife attacks or four Hurl Flame attacks.

action.name: Sculpting Knife
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

action.name: Hurl Flame
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) fire damage.

bonus.name: Waxify
entries: The waxworker devil infuses one creature it can see within 30 feet of it with wax. The target must succeed on a DC 17 CON save or begin to turn to wax for 1 minute. While turning to wax, the target’s speed is halved, and it is vulnerable to fire damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target can repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target fails this save three times, it stops making the save, and it is petrified in wax.

reaction.name: Horrifying Visage
entries: When a creature targets the waxworker devil with an attack while within 15 feet it, the devil can briefly remove its mask, revealing its ravaged face. The attacker must succeed on a DC 17 WIS save or take 5 (2d4) psychic damage and be frightened until the end of its turn.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The weeping treant is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Siege Monster
entries: The weeping treant deals double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Speak with Plants
entries: The weeping treant can communicate with plants and Plants as if they shared a language. T T 290 Weep Acid. Thick tears of dark, acidic sap stream continuously down the treant’s face and trunk. A creature that touches the weeping treant or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 DEX save or take 2 (1d4) acid damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The weeping treant makes two Slam or Fling Acid attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) acid damage, and the target takes 2 (1d4) acid damage at the end of its next turn unless it or another creature takes an action to wipe off the acid.

action.name: Fling Acid
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (4d4 + 5) acid damage, and the target takes 5 (2d4) acid damage at the end of its next turn unless it or another creature takes an action to wipe off the acid.

reaction.name: Acid Splatter (70 HP or Fewer)
entries: When a creature deals damage to the weeping treant, it can force acid to splash out from the wound in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 15 DEX save, taking 5 (2d4) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Troll, Fiery Phantom A large, ghostly figure looms into view, its hunched, translucent body shrouded in pale, orange flames. The phantom has the ugly features, fanged maw, and long talons of a troll, and it screams as if in terrible pain as it approaches.

reaction.name: Burning Birth
entries: When a troll is burned to death in a place of unholy energy, its spirit doesn’t always pass into the afterlife as it should. Instead, the troll becomes a fiery phantom that forever burns in agony from spectral flames until it is finally laid to rest.

reaction.name: Driven by Violent Hatred
entries: Fiery phantom trolls haunt the cursed ruins and dreadful dungeons where they met their demise, unleashing the flames that destroyed their mortal forms on those who dare to enter these places. They often step through walls and release a bloodcurdling scream to terrify their hapless victims before setting the victims alight.

reaction.name: Surprising Countermeasures
entries: Unlike mortal trolls, fiery phantoms are immune to the flames that infuse their ghostly forms, and neither fire nor acid can stop their spectral regeneration. Instead, quenching the flames or calling on holy power is needed to slay it. The trolls’ undead existence is so miserable that those who have fought and destroyed a fiery phantom say a blissful smile appears on its face as its spirit dissipates.

trait.name: Aberrant Resilience
entries: The weirwood sower is resistant to the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions, and it has advantage on saves against spells or effects that would alter its form.

trait.name: Forest Camouflage
entries: The weirwood sower’s Stealth is 17 while in forested terrain.

trait.name: Weirwood Shingles
entries: Characterized by bark-like patches that erupt across the victim’s body, weirwood shingles is a disease that infects creatures attacked by a weirwood sower. Until the disease is cured, the creature suffers one level of exhaustion that can’t be removed, and it is plagued by nightmares of an immense, terrifying tree. At the end of each long rest, the infected creature must make a DC 13 CON save. On a failure, its movement speeds are reduced by 5 feet each, as the wooden patches grow. On a success, its speeds increase by 5 feet, up to their base values. If the creature’s walking speed is reduced to 0 feet, it becomes petrified in wood. A creature that finishes two long rests with its speeds at their base values is cured of the W W 312 disease. Alternatively, weirwood shingles or its petrification can be cured with a greater restoration spell or similar magic.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The weirwood sower makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or contract the weirwood shingles disease (see the Weirwood Shingles trait).

action.name: Lob Sap
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) poison damage, and the target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet.

reaction.name: Spine Scrape
entries: When a creature hits the sower with an attack while within 5 feet of it, the sower can twist its body to scrape its spines against the attacker. The attacker must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or contract the weirwood shingles disease (see the Weirwood Shingles trait) and be paralyzed until the end of its next turn. Wight, Kelp Strands of kelp wrap around and drag behind this walking corpse, blue and bloated as if from drowning. The creature, which smells like rotting sea vegetation, twitches an arm, and one of the longer strands of kelp reaches out in response.

reaction.name: Horrific Genesis
entries: Kelp wights were humanoids who got caught in seaweed or kelp and drowned. Most of these deaths are tragic accidents, but sometimes sentient aquatic plants cause them. Regardless of the cause, kelp wights rise from death to perpetuate the strangulations and drownings they suffered.

reaction.name: Shoreline Dwellers
entries: When not actively hunting for victims, kelp wights lair along shorelines where their disguises as mounds of seaweed become more plausible. They prefer to drag their prey to the water to drown it, but they take wicked pleasure from surprising hapless prey going for a stroll along the shoreline or a midnight swim. When the wights’ notoriety grows locally in areas that offer a strong response, they relocate somewhere else along the shore.

reaction.name: Watery Minions
entries: As kelp wights claim their victims, the wretched creatures arise as shambling zombies under the wights’ control. The wights use the zombies to besiege coastal towns or to lure more prospective victims to their shoreline lairs.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The wind leech is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wind leech makes three Tail Slap or Fling Mucus attacks. It can replace one Tail Slap attack with a Bite attack. If two Tail Slap or Fling Mucus attacks hit one creature, the target becomes slightly buoyant until the end of its next turn. While buoyant, its speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it has disadvantage on attacks and checks that use DEX.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) acid damage, and the wind leech attaches to the target. While attached, the wind leech can’t make Bite attacks, its Tail Slap attacks against the target have advantage, its Fling Mucus attacks don’t have disadvantage from being within 5 feet of the target, and it moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the leech’s movement. The leech can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. A creature, including the target, can take its action to detach the leech by succeeding on a DC 14 STR check.

action.name: Tail Slap
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) acid damage.

action.name: Fling Mucus
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) acid damage.

bonus.name: Hypnotic Display
entries: The wind leech causes colorful patterns to ripple across its body hypnotically. Each creature within 30 feet of the leech that can see the display must succeed on a DC 14 WIS save or be able to take either an action or bonus action on its next turn, not both, as it is distracted by the display. 315 W W Withered Elder The gaunt figure could be mistaken for a statue carved of petrified wood if not for its sickly yellow glowing eyes. It raises a gnarled club in its hands, the head of which is surrounded in a grim ochre miasma.

bonus.name: Harbingers of Decay
entries: In life, withered elders were druids devoted to decay and blight. They reveled in despoiling nature and turning that rot against farming communities and settlements isolated by the wilderness. These druids devised a ritual to continue their activities after the end of their appointed lifespans. The ritual involves using blight and decay to murder one thousand dryads and one hundred treants, then replacing the druid’s own heart with a blight-rotted treant’s heart.

bonus.name: Deacons of Rot
entries: Withered elders see themselves as agents of the natural order. They act only in service of ruin, and they can’t be convinced to turn from that path. They are canny, and often ancient, opponents, and they aren’t prone to underestimating an enemy. When a withered elder downs a foe, it takes the time to ensure that foe is dead and rife with decay before moving on to the next one. A WITHERED ELDER’S LAIR Seeing themselves as unparalleled masters of the wilds, withered elders shun the company of any that might see themselves as an equal. They lair in underground complexes overrun with fungi or the ruins of settlements destroyed by nature’s wrath. Their lairs are filled with blight-altered plants and animals, natural traps, and obstructing topography. When encountered in its lair, a withered elder has a challenge rating of 15. LAIR ACTIONS On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the withered elder can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the withered elder can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row: • Absorb Life. One Beast or Plant the withered elder can see within 90 feet of it withers and dies, restoring 10 HP per that creature’s CR to the withered elder. Nonmagical plants in a 5-foot radius centered on a point the withered elder can see within 90 feet of it wither and die. The elder then regains 10 (3d6) HP. If that area includes a Beast, Humanoid, or Plant, the elder regains 13 (3d8) HP instead. When the elder regains HP from an area of nonmagical plants, it can’t regain HP from that same area of nonmagical plants again with this lair action. • Foul Miasma. A cloud of corruption billows from a point the withered elder can see within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must succeed W W 316 on a DC 19 CON save or take 7 (2d6) poison damage, be poisoned, and be vulnerable to poison damage until initiative count 20 on the next round. • Wither Flesh. The flesh of up to three creatures that aren’t Constructs or Undead the withered elder can see within 60 feet of it withers. Each creature must succeed on a DC 19 CON save or take 9 (2d8) necrotic damage and gain only half the HP from effects that restore HP until initiative count 20 on the next round. REGIONAL EFFECTS The region housing a withered elder’s lair is wounded by its presence, which creates one or more of the following effects: • Heavy Air. The air is thick and heavy within 3 miles of the withered elder’s lair. Flying speeds are halved in this area. • Sense Life. The withered elder can detect the presence of creatures that aren’t Constructs, Plants, or Undead within 1 mile of its lair. If such a creature comes within half a mile of its lair, the withered elder immediately knows the type, size, and CR or level of the creature. • Shifting Topography. The land within 5 miles of the withered elder’s lair slowly and subtly shifts throughout the day. Formerly reliable trails and passages end abruptly or in a different location. Landmarks change position. A creature that attempts to navigate through the area has disadvantage on checks to do so. If the withered elder is destroyed, these effects fade in 1d10 days.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the withered elder fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Turn Resistance
entries: The withered elder has advantage on saves against any effect that turns undead.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The withered elder doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The withered elder is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Woodland Walk
entries: Difficult terrain composed of nonmagical plants doesn’t cost the withered elder extra movement. In addition, the elder can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The withered elder uses Petrifying Stare.

action.name: It then makes three Primal Burst attacks
entries: It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Primal Burst
entries: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (5d6 + 6) poison damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 19 CON save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Petrifying Stare
entries: The withered elder fixes its gaze on one creature that isn’t a Construct or Undead that it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must make a DC 19 CON save. On a failure, the target magically begins turning into petrified wood and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat the save at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified as stony wood on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

action.name: Recovery in Ruin (Recharge 6)
entries: The withered elder draws in the life force of creatures near it. Each creature within 15 feet of the elder must make a DC 19 CON save, taking 49 (11d8) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The withered elder regains HP equal to the single highest amount of necrotic damage dealt.

action.name: Spellcasting
entries: The withered elder casts one of the following spells, using WIS as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 19). At will: create or destroy water , gust of wind , spider climb 3/day each: alter self , entangle , fog cloud 2/day each: meld into stone , gaseous form , wind wall 1/day each: antilife shell , contagion

bonus.name: Broken Earth
entries: The withered elder magically disrupts the ground on a point it can see within 90 feet of it. The ground within 10 feet of that point is difficult terrain until the start of the elder’s next turn.

reaction.name: Rapid Retreat
entries: When the withered elder takes damage while standing on unworked ground, it can teleport, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet of it, provided that space includes unworked ground.

legendary.name: Fade from View
entries: The withered elder takes on the color and texture of its surroundings, becoming invisible until the end of its next turn or until it attacks, casts a spell, or uses a lair action.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The withered elder can move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Cast a Spell (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The withered elder uses Spellcasting.

legendary.name: Petrifying Wave (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 15 feet of the withered elder that isn’t a Construct or Undead must succeed on a DC 19 CON save or be restrained until the end of its next turn. A creature restrained by Petrifying Stare has disadvantage on its next save against the stare’s effect. 317 W W

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the wood flitkith remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a wooden doll.

trait.name: Fey Resilience
entries: As the cloth flitkith.

trait.name: Flitkith Resilience
entries: As the cloth flitkith.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wood flitkith makes two Slam or Throw Tool attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Throw Tool
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Manipulate Wooden Object
entries: The wood flitkith magically manipulates a piece of wood worn by a creature within 60 feet of it, causing one of the following effects: • Rearrange Supports. The wooden supports in the target’s backpack shift, throwing off balance. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn. • Unbutton Gear. Wooden buttons, toggles, and similar connectors disconnect pieces of clothing or equipment. The target must succeed on a DC 13 DEX save or its speed is halved until it takes an action to reconnect them. • Warp Weapon. The target must succeed on a DC 13 STR save or a wooden weapon it wields deals only half the normal damage until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Cavernous Mouth
entries: The wooly hippopotamus has an enormous mouth that can safely carry up to four Medium or smaller creatures. While inside the hippopotamus’s mouth, a creature has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the hippopotamus. A creature inside the mouth can spend 5 feet of movement to exit the mouth, exiting prone into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the hippopotamus. A creature inside the mouth has advantage on melee attack rolls against the hippopotamus, provided it isn’t wielding a two-handed weapon.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wooly hippopotamus makes two Slam attacks. If both attacks hit one creature, the target is knocked prone.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Spit
entries: The wooly hippopoptamus spits one creature or object of its choice within its mouth at a point it can see within 30 feet of it. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a DC 15 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knocked prone. The creature or object that was spit takes half the damage and lands prone in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the point.

bonus.name: Slurp
entries: The wooly hippopotamus pulls one Medium or smaller creature it can see within 5 feet of it into its mouth. An unwilling creature that succeeds on a DC 15 DEX save is unaffected.

reaction.name: Protective Scoop
entries: When a friendly creature the wooly hippopotamus can see within 5 feet of it is the target of an attack, the hippopotamus can scoop the creature into its mouth and become the new target of the attack. 329 APPENDIX: NPCS This appendix contains statistics for various humanoids. From diviners to master assassins, these NPCs can be used to add depth and life to your game world. The stat blocks are presented alphabetically and assume no lineage. To make an NPC of a specific lineage that is available to PCs, add that lineage’s traits, such as darkvision, to the stat block. NPC FEATURES TABLE When an NPC’s statistics include the note “Humanoid (Any Lineage)” as the creature type, you can adjust those statistics as described in the NPC Features table to create an NPC of the type of Humanoid detailed in the table. The base statistics for the Humanoids in this table can be found in this book, Monster Vault , or The Old Margreve . For details on how to use this table, see Monster Vault .

monster.name: World Tree Sapling
senses: keensense 60 ft. (can’t sense beyond this radius)

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the world tree sapling remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.

trait.name: Nature’s Bounty
entries: The land is enriched by a world tree sapling’s prolonged presence. If the sapling remains in a location no larger than 500 feet to a side for at least 24 hours, plants and trees within five miles of that location can grow up to three times their normal size and yield three times the normal amount of food when harvested.

trait.name: Plant Resilience
entries: The world tree sapling is resistant to exhaustion and to the paralyzed, petrified, and unconscious conditions.

trait.name: Speak with Plants
entries: The world tree sapling can communicate with Plants and nonmagical plants as if they shared a language. W W 318

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The world tree sapling makes four Grasping Tendril attacks or two Exploding Seed attacks.

action.name: Grasping Tendril
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 30 ft., one creature. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Medium or smaller, it must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be pulled up to 15 feet closer to the sapling.

action.name: Exploding Seed
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) thunder damage. Each creature within 5 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be knocked prone.

action.name: Friends of the World Tree (1/Day)
entries: The world tree sapling magically calls 2d6 blood hawks , 1d4 giant owls , or 1 ratatosk (see Labyrinth Worldbook ). The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the sapling and obeying its telepathic commands. The creatures remain for 1 hour, until the sapling dies, or until the sapling dismisses them as a bonus action.

bonus.name: Entangling Roots
entries: The world tree sapling calls to the roots beneath up to two creatures on the ground it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be restrained by grasping roots until the end of its next turn. The sapling can’t target creatures in contact with a manufactured floor, such as the wooden floor of a building.

monster.name: Wrath Wight
languages: the languages it knew in life

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: The wrath wight doesn’t require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Undead Resilience
entries: The wrath wight is immune to poison damage, to exhaustion, and to the poisoned condition.

trait.name: Unstoppable Retribution
entries: Until it achieves justice for its death, a destroyed wrath wight returns in 30 days, regaining all its HP and becoming active again within 10 feet of where it died. If the wrath wight is presented with everything it needs to feel justice has been served, such as the death of its murderers or witnessing a lawful trial resolving the events that led to its death, the wrath wight permanently dies.

trait.name: Vengeful Determination
entries: The wrath wight has advantage on checks made to escape a grapple or against being restrained and on checks made to overcome barriers or obstacles that are directly preventing it from getting to creatures it wants to attack. W W 314

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wrath wight makes three Fist or Wrath Bolt attacks. If two Wrath Bolt attacks hit one creature, the target is overcome with a fit of rage until the end of its next turn, as described in Scream of Rage.

action.name: Fist
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Wrath Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 60 ft., one creature. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) psychic damage.

bonus.name: Scream of Rage
entries: The wrath wight vents its wrath in a mind- shaking scream at one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 16 WIS save or be overcome with a fit of rage on its next turn. While in a fit of rage, a creature has advantage on melee attack rolls, it is unable to distinguish friend from foe, and it must attack the nearest creature other than the wrath wight. If no other creature is near enough to move to and attack, the target stalks off in a random direction, seeking a target for its rage.

trait.name: Lock Down
entries: A prone creature within 5 feet of the wrestler must use all its movement to stand.

trait.name: Wrestler’s Stance
entries: While the wrestler is conscious and wearing no armor and wielding no shield, it adds its CON modifier to its AC (included above).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wrestler makes three Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 16) if it is a Large or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained, and the wrestler can’t grapple another target.

bonus.name: Takedown
entries: One Medium or smaller creature grappled by the wrestler must succeed on a DC 16 STR save or be knocked prone and unable to stand until the grapple ends.

reaction.name: Living Shield
entries: When a creature the wrestler can see hits it with an attack while it is grappling a creature, the wrestler can shift the grappled creature in front of the blow. The wrestler takes half the damage from the attack, and the grappled creature takes the other half.

trait.name: Desert Master
entries: Difficult terrain composed of sand, mud, or rock doesn’t cost the xenarth extra movement. In addition, when the xenarth uses its Rolling Doom action, the terrain in a 20-foot-wide path behind it turns into desert. Sand sprouts from the ground, nonmagical plants not native to deserts die, and natural water sources dry up. These effects last while the xenarth is within 1 mile of the path and for 1 hour afterward.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the xenarth remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a small rocky hill.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the xenarth fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The xenarth has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The xenarth’s weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Monstrosity Resilience
entries: The xenarth is resistant to exhaustion and to the frightened condition.

trait.name: Siege Behemoth
entries: The xenarth deals triple damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The xenarth makes one Bite attack and two Stomp attacks, or it makes four Desert Phlegm attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 72 (10d12 + 7) piercing damage.

action.name: Stomp
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 45 (7d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage, and each creature, other than the xenarth, within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 22 DEX save or be knocked prone.

action.name: Desert Phlegm
entries: Ranged Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (5d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) fire damage, and the target’s speed is halved until the end of its next turn, as sludgy sand clings to it. If the target is flying, it must succeed on a DC 22 STR save or immediately fall, taking falling damage as normal.

action.name: Rolling Doom (147 HP or Higher)
entries: The xenarth curls its body into a sphere and rolls. It moves up to 60 feet in a straight line and can move through the space of any Huge or smaller creature. The first time it enters a creature’s space during this move, that creature must make a DC 22 STR save. X X 320 On a failure, a creature takes 44 (8d10) bludgeoning damage and 36 (8d8) piercing damage and is knocked prone. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t knocked prone. A Large or smaller creature that fails the save is also impaled on the xenarch’s spiked armor plates. While impaled, a creature is restrained, moves with the xenarth when the xenarth moves, and takes 9 (2d8) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature, including the impaled creature, can take an action to free the impaled creature by succeeding on a DC 22 STR check.

action.name: Calcifying Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries: The xenarth exhales a breath of scouring wind and molten crystal in a 90- foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 22 DEX save. On a failure, a creature takes 42 (12d6) slashing damage and 45 (10d8) fire damage and begins to turn to crystal and is restrained. On a success, a creature takes half the damage, isn’t restrained, and doesn’t begin to turn to crystal. A creature turning to crystal must succeed on a DC 20 CON save at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified in sand crystal on a failure or ending the effect on itself on a success.

reaction.name: Sand Wave (180 HP or Fewer)
entries: When a creature the xenarth can see within 30 feet of it deals damage to it, the xenarth can perform a short hop, causing a wave of rippling sand. Each creature within 30 feet of the xenarth must succeed on a DC 22 DEX save or be knocked prone and buried. A buried creature is restrained and unable to breathe or stand up. A creature, including the buried creature, can take an action to free the buried creature by succeeding on a DC 22 STR check. The area then becomes difficult terrain.

legendary.name: Head Toss
entries: One creature within 10 feet of the xenarth must succeed on a DC 22 STR save or be thrown up to 40 feet in a random direction and knocked prone. If a thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 22 DEX save or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The xenarth moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

legendary.name: Blinding Sandstorm (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: A 20-foot-radius swirl of sand appears on a point the xenarth can see within 60 feet of it. A creature that enters the swirl of sand for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 22 DEX save or be blinded until the start of its next turn. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more also suffers one level of exhaustion. The swirl of sand lasts for 1 minute, until the xenarth uses this legendary action again, or until the xenarth dies.

trait.name: Adamantine Body
entries: As the adamantine dragon wyrmling.

trait.name: Unstoppable Blows
entries: When the adamantine dragon hasn’t unleashed its Needle Breath, its body accumulates adamantine. While the dragon’s Needle Breath is available, its attacks ignore the armor class granted by magical or nonmagical armor worn by a target when determining if its attacks hit that target.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks. It can replace its Bite attack with a use of Crushing Breath, if available.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage. 103 D D Needle Breath (Recharge 5–6). The dragon exhales sharp adamantine needles in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 DEX save, taking 65 (10d12) piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Crushing Breath (Recharge 6)
entries: As the adamantine dragon wyrmling, except it is a 30-foot cone, the save DC is 18, and the bludgeoning damage is 4 (1d8).

trait.name: Adaptive Camouflage
entries: If the dragon spends at least 1 minute in a particular type of terrain, such as a forest, its Stealth is 19 while in that terrain.

trait.name: Sparkling Breath
entries: When the dragon hasn’t unleashed its Psychic Fog Breath, tendrils of sparkling blue fog curl out from it with each breath. While the dragon’s Psychic Fog Breath is available, each creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 13 CON save or have disadvantage on WIS saves and on WIS (Insight) checks until the start of its next turn. 107 D D

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

action.name: Psychic Fog Breath
entries: (Recharge 5–6). The dragon exhales a 30-foot cone of sparkling blue fog. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 CON save, taking 35 (10d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

trait.name: Stinging Pollinators
entries: After the verdure dragon exhales its Pollen Breath, pollen lingers in the air, attracting stinging insects. While the dragon’s Pollen Breath is unavailable, a creature that hits the dragon with an attack while within 10 feet of the dragon takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

trait.name: Woodland Walk
entries: As the verdure dragon wyrmling.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks. It can replace its Bite attack with a use of Distracting Breath, if available.

action.name: Bite
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage. 111 D D Pollen Breath (Recharge 5–6). The dragon exhales a cloud of pollen in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 14 CON save. On a failure, a creature takes 31 (7d8) poison damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn’t incapacitated.

action.name: Distracting Breath (Recharge 6)
entries: As the verdure dragon wyrmling, except it is a 30-foot cone, and the save DC is 14.

trait.name: Acidic Weapons
entries: The ystol’s weapon attacks are magical. When the ystol hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 acid damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Flexible Form
entries: The ystol can twist and stretch its body into unnatural positions, allowing it to easily move through any opening large enough for a Small creature. It can squeeze through any opening large enough for a Tiny creature. The ystol’s destination must still have suitable room to accommodate its volume.

trait.name: Grappler
entries: The ystol has advantage on attack rolls against any creature grappled by it.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The ystol has advantage on saves against spells and other magic effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ystol makes two Slam attacks or three Acid Bolt attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) acid damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13) if it is a Medium or smaller creature.

action.name: Acid Bolt
entries: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) acid damage.

bonus.name: Acidic Squeeze
